lines.text: My life, you declare to me that this love of ours will be an everlasting joy between us. Great Gods! grant that she may promise truly, and say this in sincerity and from her soul,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:109" n="1">My life, you declare to me that this love of ours will be an everlasting joy between us. Great Gods! grant that she may promise truly, and say this in sincerity and from her soul,</l>

lines.text: and that through all our lives we may be allowed to prolong together this bond of holy friendship.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:109" n="5">and that through all our lives we may be allowed to prolong together this bond of holy friendship.</l>

lines.text: Aufilena, good professional girls are always praised: they receive their pay for what they intend to do. Because you promised me—which was a lie—you are unprofessional; because you do not give and often bring [home the pay], you do wrong.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:110" n="1">Aufilena, good professional girls are always praised: they receive their pay for what they intend to do. Because you promised me—which was a lie—you are unprofessional; because you do not give and often bring [home the pay], you do wrong.</l>

lines.text: Either to do it is honest, or not to have promised was chaste, Aufilena: but to steal what was given by deceiving, proves you worse than the greedy whore who prostitutes herself with her whole body.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:110" n="5">Either to do it is honest, or not to have promised was chaste, Aufilena: but to steal what was given by deceiving, proves you worse than the greedy whore who prostitutes herself with her whole body.</l>

lines.text: Aufilena, that a bride live content in her husband alone is praise of exceptional praise: but it is preferable to lie beneath any lover you choose, rather than as mother to bring forth brothers [cousins] out of your uncle.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:111" n="1">Aufilena, that a bride live content in her husband alone is praise of exceptional praise: but it is preferable to lie beneath any lover you choose, rather than as mother to bring forth brothers [cousins] out of your uncle.</l>

lines.text: He is a lot of man, Naso, and he who descends with you is not a lot of man: Naso you are a lot—and sexually submissive.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:112" n="1">He is a lot of man, <persName><surname>Naso</surname></persName>, and he who descends with you is not a lot of man: <persName><surname>Naso</surname></persName> you are a lot—and sexually submissive.</l>

lines.text: In the first consulate of Pompey, Cinna, two used to frequent Mucilla: now again made consul, the two remain, but to each one has accrued a thousand. The seed of adultery is fruitful.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:113" n="1">In the first consulate of Pompey, Cinna, two used to frequent Mucilla: now again made consul, the two remain, but to each one has accrued a thousand. The seed of adultery is fruitful.</l>

lines.text: With his estate not falsely is Mentula of Firmum said to be rich, which has everything in it of such excellence, game preserves of every kind, fish, meadows, plowland and beasts. In vain: the yield is overcome by the expense.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:114" n="1">With his estate not falsely is Mentula of <placeName key="tgn,7004029">Firmum</placeName> said to be rich, which has everything in it of such excellence, game preserves of every kind, fish, meadows, plowland and beasts. In vain: the yield is overcome by the expense.</l>

lines.text: Therefore I grant that he is rich, while everything is lacking. Let us praise the estate, while its owner is a needy man.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:114" n="5">Therefore I grant that he is rich, while everything is lacking. Let us praise the estate, while its owner is a needy man.</l>

lines.text: Mentula has something like thirty acres of meadow land, forty under cultivation: the rest are as the sea. Why can he not surpass Croesus in wealth, he who in one estate possesses so much?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:115" n="1">Mentula has something like thirty acres of meadow land, forty under cultivation: the rest are as the sea. Why can he not surpass Croesus in wealth, he who in one estate possesses so much?</l>

lines.text: Meadow, arable land, immense woods, and open fields and marshes, even to the uttermost north and to the Ocean sea! All things great are here, yet is the owner most great beyond all; not a man, but in truth a mentule mighty, menacing!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:115" n="5">Meadow, arable land, immense woods, and open fields and marshes, even to the uttermost north and to the Ocean sea! All things great are here, yet is the owner most great beyond all; not a man, but in truth a mentule mighty, menacing!</l>

lines.text: Often seeking, my mind hunting how I could send to studious you the poems of Battiades, whereby I might soften you towards us, and you might not try to send hostile weapons at my head all the time—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:116" n="1">Often seeking, my mind hunting how I could send to studious you the poems of Battiades, whereby I might soften you towards us, and you might not try to send hostile weapons at my head all the time—</l>

lines.text: I see now that this effort was undertaken by me in vain, Gellius, and that our prayers to this end were of no avail. Your weapons against us we will ward off with our cloak; but, transfixed with ours, you will pay the punishment.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng4:116" n="5">I see now that this effort was undertaken by me in vain, Gellius, and that our prayers to this end were of no avail. Your weapons against us we will ward off with our cloak; but, transfixed with ours, you will pay the punishment.</l>

lines.text: Now smooth’d to polish due with pumice dry
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="1">Now smooth’d to polish due with pumice dry</l>

lines.text: Whereto this lively booklet now give I?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="2"> Whereto this lively booklet now give I?</l>

lines.text: To thee (Cornelius!); for wast ever fain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="3">To thee (<persName><surname>Cornelius</surname></persName>!); for wast ever fain</l>

lines.text: To deem my trifles somewhat boon contain;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="4">To deem my trifles somewhat boon contain;</l>

lines.text: E’en when thou single ’mongst Italians found
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="5">E’en when thou single ’mongst Italians found</l>

lines.text: Daredst all periods in three Scripts expound
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="6">Daredst all periods in three Scripts expound</l>

lines.text: Learned (by Jupiter!) elaborately.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="7">Learned (by <persName><surname>Jupiter</surname></persName>!) elaborately.</l>

lines.text: Then take thee whatso in this booklet be,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="8">Then take thee whatso in this booklet be,</l>

lines.text: Such as it is, whereto O Patron Maid
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="9">Such as it is, whereto O Patron Maid</l>

lines.text: To live down Ages lend thou lasting aid!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:1" n="10">To live down Ages lend thou lasting aid!</l>

lines.text: Sparrow! my pet’s delicious joy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="1">Sparrow! my pet’s delicious joy,</l>

lines.text: Wherewith in bosom nurst to toy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="2">Wherewith in bosom nurst to toy</l>

lines.text: She loves, and gives her finger-tip
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="3">She loves, and gives her finger-tip</l>

lines.text: For sharp-nib’d greedingneb to nip,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="4">For sharp-nib’d greedingneb to nip,</l>

lines.text: Were she who my desire withstood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="5">Were she who my desire withstood</l>

lines.text: To seek some pet of merry mood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="6">To seek some pet of merry mood,</l>

lines.text: As crumb o’ comfort for her grief,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="7">As crumb o’ comfort for her grief,</l>

lines.text: Methinks her burning lowe’s relief:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="8">Methinks her burning lowe’s relief:</l>

lines.text: Could I, as plays she, play with thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="9">Could I, as plays she, play with thee,</l>

lines.text: That mind might win from misery free!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="10">That mind might win from misery free!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="10a"><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * "/></l>

lines.text: To me t’were grateful (as they say),
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="11">To me t’were grateful (as they say), </l>

lines.text: Gold codling was to fleet-foot May,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="12">Gold codling was to fleet-foot May,</l>

lines.text: Whose long-bound zone it loosed for aye.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:2" n="13">Whose long-bound zone it loosed for aye.</l>

head: ON THE DEATH OF LESBIA’S SPARROW

lines.text: Weep every Venus, and all Cupids wail,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="1">Weep every <persName><surname>Venus</surname></persName>, and all Cupids wail, </l>

lines.text: And men whose gentler spirits still prevail.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="2">And men whose gentler spirits still prevail. </l>

lines.text: Dead is the Sparrow of my girl, the joy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="3">Dead is the Sparrow of my girl, the joy,</l>

lines.text: Sparrow, my sweeting’s most delicious toy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="4"> Sparrow, my sweeting’s most delicious toy, </l>

lines.text: Whom loved she dearer than her very eyes;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="5">Whom loved she dearer than her very eyes;</l>

lines.text: For he was honeyed-pet and anywise
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="6">For he was honeyed-pet and anywise</l>

lines.text: Knew her, as even she her mother knew;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="7">Knew her, as even she her mother knew;</l>

lines.text: Ne’er from her bosom’s harbourage he flew
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="8">Ne’er from her bosom’s harbourage he flew</l>

lines.text: But ’round her hopping here, there, everywhere,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="9">But ’round her hopping here, there, everywhere,</l>

lines.text: Piped he to none but her his lady fair.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="10">Piped he to none but her his lady fair.</l>

lines.text: Now must he wander o’er the darkling way
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="11">Now must he wander o’er the darkling way</l>

lines.text: Thither, whence life-return the Fates denay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="12">Thither, whence life-return the Fates denay.</l>

lines.text: But ah! beshrew you, evil Shadows low’ring
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="13">But ah! beshrew you, evil Shadows low’ring</l>

lines.text: In Orcus ever loveliest things devouring:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="14">In Orcus ever loveliest things devouring:</l>

lines.text: Who bore so pretty a Sparrow fro’ her ta’en.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="15">Who bore so pretty a Sparrow fro’ her ta’en.</l>

lines.text: (Oh hapless birdie and Oh deed of bane!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="16">(Oh hapless birdie and Oh deed of bane!)</l>

lines.text: Now by your wanton work my girl appears
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="17">Now by your wanton work my girl appears</l>

lines.text: With turgid eyelids tinted rose by tears.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:3" n="18">With turgid eyelids tinted rose by tears.</l>

lines.text: Yonder Pinnace ye (my guests!) behold
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="1">Yonder Pinnace ye (my guests!) behold</l>

lines.text: Saith she was erstwhile fleetest-fleet of crafts,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="2">Saith she was erstwhile fleetest-fleet of crafts,</l>

lines.text: Nor could by swiftness of aught plank that swims,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="3">Nor could by swiftness of aught plank that swims,</l>

lines.text: Be she outstripped, whether paddle plied,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="4">Be she outstripped, whether paddle plied,</l>

lines.text: Or fared she scudding under canvas-sail.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="5">Or fared she scudding under canvas-sail.</l>

lines.text: Eke she defieth threat’ning Adrian shore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="6">Eke she defieth threat’ning <placeName key="tgn,2095226">Adrian</placeName> shore,</l>

lines.text: Dare not denay her, insular Cyclades,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="7">Dare not denay her, insular <placeName key="tgn,7011270">Cyclades</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: And noble Rhodos and ferocious Thrace,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="8">And noble <placeName key="tgn,7011266">Rhodos</placeName> and ferocious <placeName key="tgn,7002756">Thrace</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: Propontis too and blustering Pontic bight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="9">Propontis too and blustering Pontic bight.</l>

lines.text: Where she (my Pinnace now) in times before,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="10">Where she (my Pinnace now) in times before,</l>

lines.text: Was leafy woodling on Cytórean Chine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="11">Was leafy woodling on Cytórean Chine</l>

lines.text: For ever loquent lisping with her leaves.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="12">For ever loquent lisping with her leaves.</l>

lines.text: Pontic Amastris! Box-tree-clad Cytórus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="13">Pontic Amastris! Box-tree-clad Cytórus!</l>

lines.text: Cognisant were ye, and you weet full well
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="14">Cognisant were ye, and you weet full well</l>

lines.text: (So saith my Pinnace) how from earliest age
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="15">(So saith my Pinnace) how from earliest age</l>

lines.text: Upon your highmost-spiring peak she stood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="16">Upon your highmost-spiring peak she stood,</l>

lines.text: How in your waters first her sculls were dipt,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="17">How in your waters first her sculls were dipt,</l>

lines.text: And thence thro’ many and many an important strait
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="18">And thence thro’ many and many an important strait</l>

lines.text: She bore her owner whether left or right,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="19">She bore her owner whether left or right,</l>

lines.text: Where breezes bade her fare, or Jupiter deigned
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="20">Where breezes bade her fare, or Jupiter deigned</l>

lines.text: At once propitious strike the sail full square;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="21">At once propitious strike the sail full square;</l>

lines.text: Nor to the sea-shore gods was aught of vow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="22">Nor to the sea-shore gods was aught of vow</l>

lines.text: By her deemed needful, when from Ocean’s bourne
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="23">By her deemed needful, when from Ocean’s bourne</l>

lines.text: Extreme she voyaged for this limpid lake.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="24">Extreme she voyaged for this limpid lake.</l>

lines.text: Yet were such things whilome: now she retired
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="25">Yet were such things whilome: now she retired</l>

lines.text: In quiet age devotes herself to thee
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="26">In quiet age devotes herself to thee</l>

lines.text: (O twin-born Castor) twain with Castor’s twin.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:4" n="27">(O twin-born Castor) twain with Castor’s twin.</l>

lines.text: Love we (my Lesbia!) and live we our day,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="1">Love we (my Lesbia!) and live we our day,</l>

lines.text: While all stern sayings crabbed sages say,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="2">While all stern sayings crabbed sages say,</l>

lines.text: At one doit’s value let us price and prize!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="3">At one doit’s value let us price and prize!</l>

lines.text: The Suns can westward sink again to rise
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="4">The Suns can westward sink again to rise</l>

lines.text: But we, extinguished once our tiny light,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="5">But we, extinguished once our tiny light,</l>

lines.text: Perforce shall slumber through one lasting night!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="6">Perforce shall slumber through one lasting night!</l>

lines.text: Kiss me a thousand times, then hundred more,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="7">Kiss me a thousand times, then hundred more,</l>

lines.text: Then thousand others, then a new five-score,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="8">Then thousand others, then a new five-score,</l>

lines.text: Still other thousand other hundred store.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="9">Still other thousand other hundred store.</l>

lines.text: Last when the sums to many thousands grow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="10">Last when the sums to many thousands grow,</l>

lines.text: The tale let’s trouble till no more we know,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="11">The tale let’s trouble till no more we know,</l>

lines.text: Nor envious wight despiteful shall misween us
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="12">Nor envious wight despiteful shall misween us</l>

lines.text: Knowing how many kisses have been kissed between us.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:5" n="13">Knowing how many kisses have been kissed between us.</l>

lines.text: Thy Charmer (Flavius!) to Catullus’ ear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="1">Thy Charmer (Flavius!) to Catullus’ ear</l>

lines.text: Were she not manner’d mean and worst in wit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="2">Were she not manner’d mean and worst in wit</l>

lines.text: Perforce thou hadst praised nor couldst silence keep.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="3">Perforce thou hadst praised nor couldst silence keep.</l>

lines.text: But some enfevered jade, I wot-not-what,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="4">But some enfevered jade, I wot-not-what,</l>

lines.text: Some piece thou lovest, blushing this to own.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="5">Some piece thou lovest, blushing this to own.</l>

lines.text: For, nowise ’customed widower nights to lie
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="6">For, nowise ’customed widower nights to lie</l>

lines.text: Thou ’rt ever summoned by no silent bed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="7">Thou ’rt ever summoned by no silent bed</l>

lines.text: With flow’r-wreaths fragrant and with Syrian oil,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="8">With flow’r-wreaths fragrant and with Syrian oil,</l>

lines.text: By mattress, bolsters, here, there, everywhere
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="9">By mattress, bolsters, here, there, everywhere</l>

lines.text: Deep-dinted, and by quaking, shaking couch
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="10">Deep-dinted, and by quaking, shaking couch</l>

lines.text: All crepitation and mobility.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="11">All crepitation and mobility.</l>

lines.text: Explain! none whoredoms (no!) shall close my lips.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="12">Explain! none whoredoms (no!) shall close my lips.</l>

lines.text: Why? such outfuttered flank thou ne’er wouldst show
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="13">Why? such outfuttered flank thou ne’er wouldst show</l>

lines.text: Had not some fulsome work by thee been wrought.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="14">Had not some fulsome work by thee been wrought.</l>

lines.text: Then what thou holdest, boon or bane be pleased
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="15">Then what thou holdest, boon or bane be pleased </l>

lines.text: Disclose!For thee and thy beloved fain would I
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="16">Disclose!For thee and thy beloved fain would I</l>

lines.text: Upraise to Heaven with my liveliest lay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:6" n="17">Upraise to Heaven with my liveliest lay.</l>

lines.text: Thou ask’st How many kissing bouts I bore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="1">Thou ask’st How many kissing bouts I bore</l>

lines.text: From thee (my Lesbia!) or be enough or more?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="2">From thee (my Lesbia!) or be enough or more?</l>

lines.text: I say what mighty sum of Lybian-sands
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="3">I say what mighty sum of Lybian-sands</l>

lines.text: Confine Cyrene’s Laserpitium-lands
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="4">Confine Cyrene’s Laserpitium-lands</l>

lines.text: ’Twixt Oracle of Jove the Swelterer
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="5">’Twixt Oracle of Jove the Swelterer</l>

lines.text: And olden Battus’ holy Sepulchre,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="6">And olden Battus’ holy Sepulchre,</l>

lines.text: Or stars innumerate through night-stillness ken
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="7">Or stars innumerate through night-stillness ken</l>

lines.text: The stolen Love-delights of mortal men,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="8">The stolen Love-delights of mortal men,</l>

lines.text: For that to kiss thee with unending kisses
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="9">For that to kiss thee with unending kisses</l>

lines.text: For mad Catullus enough and more be this,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="10">For mad Catullus enough and more be this,</l>

lines.text: Risses nor curious wight shall count their tale,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="11">Risses nor curious wight shall count their tale,</l>

lines.text: Nor to bewitch us evil tongue avail.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:7" n="12">Nor to bewitch us evil tongue avail.</l>

lines.text: Woe-full Catullus! cease to play the fool
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="1">Woe-full Catullus! cease to play the fool</l>

lines.text: And what thou seest dead as dead regard!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="2">And what thou seest dead as dead regard!</l>

lines.text: Whilòme the sheeniest suns for thee did shine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="3">Whilòme the sheeniest suns for thee did shine</l>

lines.text: When oft-a-tripping whither led the girl
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="4">When oft-a-tripping whither led the girl</l>

lines.text: By us beloved, as shall none be loved.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="5">By us beloved, as shall none be loved.</l>

lines.text: There all so merry doings then were done
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="6">There all so merry doings then were done</l>

lines.text: After thy liking, nor the girl was loath.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="7">After thy liking, nor the girl was loath.</l>

lines.text: Then certès sheeniest suns for thee did shine.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="8">Then certès sheeniest suns for thee did shine.</l>

lines.text: Now she’s unwilling: thou too (hapless!) will
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="9">Now she’s unwilling: thou too (hapless!) will</l>

lines.text: Her flight to follow, and sad life to live:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="10">Her flight to follow, and sad life to live:</l>

lines.text: Endure with stubborn soul and still obdure.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="11">Endure with stubborn soul and still obdure.</l>

lines.text: Damsel, adieu! Catullus obdurate grown
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="12">Damsel, adieu! Catullus obdurate grown</l>

lines.text: Nor seeks thee, neither asks of thine unwill;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="13">Nor seeks thee, neither asks of thine unwill;</l>

lines.text: Yet shalt thou sorrow when none woos thee more;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="14">Yet shalt thou sorrow when none woos thee more;</l>

lines.text: Reprobate! Woe to thee! What life remains?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="15">Reprobate! Woe to thee! What life remains?</l>

lines.text: Who now shall love thee? Who’ll think thee fair?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="16">Who now shall love thee? Who’ll think thee fair?</l>

lines.text: Whom now shalt ever love? Whose wilt be called?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="17">Whom now shalt ever love? Whose wilt be called?</l>

lines.text: To whom shalt kisses give? whose liplets nip?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="18">To whom shalt kisses give? whose liplets nip?</l>

lines.text: But thou (Catullus!) destiny-doomed obdure.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:8" n="19">But thou (Catullus!) destiny-doomed obdure.</l>

lines.text: Veranius! over every friend of me
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="1">Veranius! over every friend of me</l>

lines.text: Forestanding, owned I hundred thousands three,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="2">Forestanding, owned I hundred thousands three,</l>

lines.text: Home to Penates and to single-soul’d
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="3">Home to Penates and to single-soul’d</l>

lines.text: Brethren, returned art thou and mother old?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="4">Brethren, returned art thou and mother old?</l>

lines.text: Yes, thou art come. Oh, winsome news come well!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="5">Yes, thou art come. Oh, winsome news come well!</l>

lines.text: Now shall I see thee, safely hear thee tell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="6">Now shall I see thee, safely hear thee tell</l>

lines.text: Of sites Iberian, deeds and nations ’spied,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="7">Of sites Iberian, deeds and nations ’spied,</l>

lines.text: (As be thy wont) and neck-a-neck applied
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="8">(As be thy wont) and neck-a-neck applied</l>

lines.text: I’ll greet with kisses thy glad lips and eyne.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="9">I’ll greet with kisses thy glad lips and eyne.</l>

lines.text: Oh! Of all mortal men beatified
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="10">Oh! Of all mortal men beatified</l>

lines.text: Whose joy and gladness greater be than mine?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:9" n="11">Whose joy and gladness greater be than mine?</l>

lines.text: Led me my Varus to his flame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="1">Led me my Varus to his flame,</l>

lines.text: As I from Forum idling came.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="2">As I from Forum idling came.</l>

lines.text: Forthright some whorelet judged I it
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="3">Forthright some whorelet judged I it</l>

lines.text: Nor lacking looks nor wanting wit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="4">Nor lacking looks nor wanting wit,</l>

lines.text: When hied we thither, mid us three
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="5">When hied we thither, mid us three</l>

lines.text: Fell various talk, as how might be
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="6">Fell various talk, as how might be</l>

lines.text: Bithynia now, and how it fared,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="7"><placeName key="tgn,7016608">Bithynia</placeName> now, and how it fared,</l>

lines.text: And if some coin I made or spared.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="8">And if some coin I made or spared.</l>

lines.text: There was no cause (I soothly said)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="9"><q rend="double">There was no cause</q> (I soothly said)</l>

lines.text: The Praetors or the Cohort made
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="10"><q rend="double">The Praetors or the Cohort made</q></l>

lines.text: Thence to return with oilier head;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="11"><q rend="double; merge">Thence to return with oilier head;</q></l>

lines.text: The more when ruled by . . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="12"><q rend="double; merge">The more when ruled by <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . "/></q></l>

lines.text: Praetor, as pile the Cohort rating.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="13"><q rend="double; merge">Praetor, as pile the Cohort rating.</q></l>

lines.text: Quoth they, But certes as ’twas there
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="14">Quoth they, <q rend="double">But certes as ’twas there</q></l>

lines.text: The custom rose, some men to bear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="15"><q rend="double; merge">The custom rose, some men to bear</q></l>

lines.text: Litter thou boughtest? I to her
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="16"><q rend="double; merge">Litter thou boughtest?</q> I to her</l>

lines.text: To seem but richer, wealthier,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="17">To seem but richer, wealthier,</l>

lines.text: Cry, Nay, with me ’twas not so ill
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="18">Cry, <q rend="double">Nay, with me ’twas not so ill</q></l>

lines.text: That, given the Province suffered, still
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="19"><q rend="double; merge">That, given the Province suffered, still</q></l>

lines.text: Eight stiff-backed loons I could not buy.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="20"><q rend="double; merge">Eight stiff-backed loons I could not buy.</q></l>

lines.text: (Withal none here nor there owned I
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="21">(Withal none here nor there owned I</l>

lines.text: Who broken leg of Couch outworn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="22">Who broken leg of Couch outworn</l>

lines.text: On nape of neck had ever borne!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="23">On nape of neck had ever borne!)</l>

lines.text: Then she, as pathic piece became,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="24">Then she, as pathic piece became,</l>

lines.text: Prithee Catullus mine, those same
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="25"><q rend="double">Prithee Catullus mine, those same</q></l>

lines.text: Lend me, Serapis-wards I’d hie. * * * *
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="26"><q rend="double; merge">Lend me, Serapis-wards I’d hie.</q> <gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Easy, on no-wise, no, quoth I,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="27"><q rend="double">Easy, on no-wise, no,</q> quoth I, </l>

lines.text: Whate’er was mine, I lately said
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="28"><q rend="double">Whate’er was mine, I lately said</q> </l>

lines.text: Is some mistake, my camarade
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="29"><q rend="double; merge">Is some mistake, my camarade</q></l>

lines.text: One Cinna-Gaius-bought the lot,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="30"><q rend="double; merge">One Cinna-Gaius-bought the lot,</q></l>

lines.text: But his or mine, it matters what?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="31"><q rend="double; merge">But his or mine, it matters what?</q></l>

lines.text: I use it freely as though bought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="32"><q rend="double; merge">I use it freely as though bought,</q></l>

lines.text: Yet thou, pert troubler, most absurd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="33"><q rend="double; merge">Yet thou, pert troubler, most absurd,</q></l>

lines.text: None suffer’st speak an idle word.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:10" n="34"><q rend="double; merge">None suffer’st speak an idle word.</q></l>

lines.text: Furius and Aurelius, Catullus’ friends,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="1">Furius and Aurelius, Catullus’ friends, </l>

lines.text: Whether extremest Indian shore he brave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="2">Whether extremest Indian shore he brave,</l>

lines.text: Strands where far-resounding billow rends
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="3">Strands where far-resounding billow rends</l>

lines.text: The shattered wave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="4">The shattered wave,</l>

lines.text: Or ’mid Hyrcanians dwell he, Arabs soft and wild,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="5">Or ’mid Hyrcanians dwell he, Arabs soft and wild,</l>

lines.text: Sacis and Parthians of the arrow fain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="6">Sacis and Parthians of the arrow fain,</l>

lines.text: Or where the Seven-mouth’d Nilus mud-defiled
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="7">Or where the Seven-mouth’d Nilus mud-defiled </l>

lines.text: Tinges the Main,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="8">Tinges the Main,</l>

lines.text: Or climb he lofty Alpine Crest and note
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="9">Or climb he lofty Alpine Crest and note</l>

lines.text: Works monumental, Caesar’s grandeur telling,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="10">Works monumental, Caesar’s grandeur telling,</l>

lines.text: Rhine Gallic, horrid Ocean and remote
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="11">Rhine Gallic, horrid Ocean and remote</l>

lines.text: Britons low-dwelling;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="12">Britons low-dwelling;</l>

lines.text: All these (whatever shall the will design
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="13">All these (whatever shall the will design</l>

lines.text: Of Heaven-homed Gods) Oh ye prepared to tempt;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="14">Of Heaven-homed Gods) Oh ye prepared to tempt; </l>

lines.text: Announce your briefest to that damsel mine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="15">Announce your briefest to that damsel mine </l>

lines.text: In words unkempt:—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="16">In words unkempt:—</l>

lines.text: Live she and love she wenchers several,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="17">Live she and love she wenchers several,</l>

lines.text: Embrace three hundred wi’ the like requitals,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="18">Embrace three hundred wi’ the like requitals, </l>

lines.text: None truly loving and withal of all
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="19">None truly loving and withal of all</l>

lines.text: Bursting the vitals:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="20">Bursting the vitals: </l>

lines.text: My love regard she not, my love of yore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="21">My love regard she not, my love of yore,</l>

lines.text: Which fell through fault of her, as falls the fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="22">Which fell through fault of her, as falls the fair </l>

lines.text: Last meadow-floret whenas passed it o’er
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="23">Last meadow-floret whenas passed it o’er</l>

lines.text: touch of the share.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:11" n="24">touch of the share.</l>

head: TO M. ASINIUS WHO STOLE NAPERY

lines.text: Marrúcinus Asinius! ill thou usest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="1">Marrúcinus Asinius! ill thou usest</l>

lines.text: That hand sinistral in thy wit and wine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="2">That hand sinistral in thy wit and wine</l>

lines.text: Filching the napkins of more heedless hosts.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="3">Filching the napkins of more heedless hosts.</l>

lines.text: Dost find this funny? Fool it passeth thee
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="4">Dost find this funny? Fool it passeth thee</l>

lines.text: How ’tis a sordid deed, a sorry jest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="5">How ’tis a sordid deed, a sorry jest.</l>

lines.text: Dost misbelieve me? Trust to Pollio,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="6">Dost misbelieve me? Trust to Pollio,</l>

lines.text: Thy brother, ready to compound such thefts
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="7">Thy brother, ready to compound such thefts</l>

lines.text: E’en at a talent’s cost; for he’s a youth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="8">E’en at a talent’s cost; for he’s a youth</l>

lines.text: In speech past master and in fair pleasantries.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="9">In speech past master and in fair pleasantries.</l>

lines.text: Of hendecasyllabics hundreds three
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="10">Of hendecasyllabics hundreds three</l>

lines.text: Therefore expect thou, or return forthright
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="11">Therefore expect thou, or return forthright</l>

lines.text: Linens whose loss affects me not for worth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="12">Linens whose loss affects me not for worth</l>

lines.text: But as mementoes of a comrade mine.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="13">But as mementoes of a comrade mine.</l>

lines.text: For napkins Saetaban from Ebro-land
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="14">For napkins Saetaban from Ebro-land</l>

lines.text: Fabúllus ent me a free giftie given
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="15">Fabúllus ent me a free giftie given</l>

lines.text: Also Veránius: these perforce I love
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="16">Also Veránius: these perforce I love</l>

lines.text: E’en as my Veraniólus and Fabúllus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:12" n="17">E’en as my Veraniólus and Fabúllus.</l>

head: FABULLUS IS INVITED TO A POET’S SUPPER

lines.text: Thou’lt sup right well with me, Fabúllus mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="1">Thou’lt sup right well with me, Fabúllus mine,</l>

lines.text: In days few-numbered an the Gods design,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="2">In days few-numbered an the Gods design,</l>

lines.text: An great and goodly meal thou bring wi’ thee
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="3">An great and goodly meal thou bring wi’ thee</l>

lines.text: Nowise forgetting damsel bright o’ blee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="4">Nowise forgetting damsel bright o’ blee,</l>

lines.text: With wine, and salty wit and laughs all-gay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="5">With wine, and salty wit and laughs all-gay.</l>

lines.text: An these my bonny man, thou bring, I say
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="6">An these my bonny man, thou bring, I say</l>

lines.text: Thou’lt sup right well, for thy Catullus’ purse
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="7">Thou’lt sup right well, for thy Catullus’ purse</l>

lines.text: Save web of spider nothing does imburse.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="8">Save web of spider nothing does imburse.</l>

lines.text: But thou in countergift more loves shalt take
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="9">But thou in countergift more loves shalt take</l>

lines.text: Or aught of sweeter taste or fairer make:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="10">Or aught of sweeter taste or fairer make:</l>

lines.text: I’ll give thee unguent lent my girl to scent
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="11">I’ll give thee unguent lent my girl to scent</l>

lines.text: By every Venus and all Cupids sent,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="12">By every Venus and all Cupids sent,</l>

lines.text: Which, as thou savour, pray Gods interpose
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="13">Which, as thou savour, pray Gods interpose</l>

lines.text: And thee, Fabúllus, make a Naught-but-nose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:13" n="14">And thee, Fabúllus, make a Naught-but-nose.</l>

lines.text: Did I not liefer love thee than my eyes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="1">Did I not liefer love thee than my eyes</l>

lines.text: (Winsomest Calvus!), for that gift of thine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="2">(Winsomest Calvus!), for that gift of thine</l>

lines.text: Certès I’d hate thee with Vatinian hate.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="3">Certès I’d hate thee with Vatinian hate.</l>

lines.text: Say me, how came I, or by word or deed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="4">Say me, how came I, or by word or deed,</l>

lines.text: To cause thee plague me with so many a bard?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="5">To cause thee plague me with so many a bard?</l>

lines.text: The Gods deal many an ill to such a client,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="6">The Gods deal many an ill to such a client,</l>

lines.text: Who sent of impious wights to thee such crowd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="7">Who sent of impious wights to thee such crowd.</l>

lines.text: But if (as guess I) this choice boon new-found
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="8">But if (as guess I) this choice boon new-found</l>

lines.text: To thee from Commentator Sulla come,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="9">To thee from <q rend="double">Commentator</q> Sulla come,</l>

lines.text: None ill I hold it—well and welcome ’tis,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="10">None ill I hold it—well and welcome ’tis,</l>

lines.text: For that thy labours ne’er to death be doom’d.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="11">For that thy labours ne’er to death be doom’d.</l>

lines.text: Great Gods!What horrid booklet damnable
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="12">Great Gods!What horrid booklet damnable</l>

lines.text: Unto thine own Catullus thou (perdie!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="13">Unto thine own Catullus thou (perdie!)</l>

lines.text: Did send, that ever day by day die he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="14">Did send, that ever day by day die he</l>

lines.text: In Saturnalia, first of festivals.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="15">In Saturnalia, first of festivals.</l>

lines.text: No! No! thus shall’t not pass wi’ thee, sweet wag,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="16">No! No! thus shall’t not pass wi’ thee, sweet wag,</l>

lines.text: For I at dawning day will scour the booths
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="17">For I at dawning day will scour the booths</l>

lines.text: Of bibliopoles, Aquinii, Caesii and
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="18">Of bibliopoles, Aquinii, Caesii and</l>

lines.text: Suffenus, gather all their poison-trash
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="19">Suffenus, gather all their poison-trash</l>

lines.text: And with such torments pay thee for thy pains.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="20">And with such torments pay thee for thy pains.</l>

lines.text: Now for the present hence, adieu! begone
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="21">Now for the present hence, adieu! begone</l>

lines.text: Thither, whence came ye, brought by luckless feet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="22">Thither, whence came ye, brought by luckless feet,</l>

lines.text: Pests of the Century, ye pernicious Poets.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14" n="23">Pests of the Century, ye pernicious Poets.</l>

lines.text: An of my trifles peradventure chance
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14a" n="1"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_24"/>An of my trifles peradventure chance</l>

lines.text: You to be readers, and the hands of you
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14a" n="2"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_25"/>You to be readers, and the hands of you</l>

lines.text: Without a shudder unto us be offer’d
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14a" n="3"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_26"/>Without a shudder unto us be offer’d</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:14a" n="3ff"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_27"/><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * "/></l>

notes: Labeled 14b in the print.

lines.text: To thee I trust my loves and me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="1">To thee I trust my loves and me,</l>

lines.text: (Aurelius!) craving modesty.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="2">(Aurelius!) craving modesty.</l>

lines.text: That (if in mind didst ever long
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="3">That (if in mind didst ever long</l>

lines.text: To win aught chaste unknowing wrong)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="4">To win aught chaste unknowing wrong)</l>

lines.text: Then guard my boy in purest way.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="5">Then guard my boy in purest way.</l>

lines.text: From folk I say not: naught affray
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="6">From folk I say not: naught affray</l>

lines.text: The crowds wont here and there to run
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="7">The crowds wont here and there to run</l>

lines.text: Through street-squares, busied every one;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="8">Through street-squares, busied every one;</l>

lines.text: But thee I dread nor less thy penis
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="9">But thee I dread nor less thy penis</l>

lines.text: Fair or foul, younglings’ foe I ween is!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="10">Fair or foul, younglings’ foe I ween is!</l>

lines.text: Wag it as wish thou, at its will,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="11">Wag it as wish thou, at its will,</l>

lines.text: When out of doors its hope fulfil;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="12">When out of doors its hope fulfil;</l>

lines.text: Him bar I, modestly, methinks.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="13">Him bar I, modestly, methinks.</l>

lines.text: But should ill-mind or lust’s high jinks
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="14">But should ill-mind or lust’s high jinks</l>

lines.text: Thee (Sinner!), drive to sin so dread,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="15">Thee (Sinner!), drive to sin so dread,</l>

lines.text: That durst ensnare our dearling’s head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="16">That durst ensnare our dearling’s head,</l>

lines.text: Ah! woe’s thee (wretch!) and evil fate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="17">Ah! woe’s thee (wretch!) and evil fate,</l>

lines.text: Mullet and radish shall pierce and grate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="18">Mullet and radish shall pierce and grate,</l>

lines.text: When feet-bound, haled through yawning gate.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:15" n="19">When feet-bound, haled through yawning gate.</l>

head: TO AURELIUS AND FURIUS IN DEFENCE OF HIS MUSE’S HONESTY

lines.text: I’ll . . . you twain and . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="1">I’ll <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/>you twain and <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/> </l>

lines.text: Pathic Aurelius!Fúrius, libertines!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="2">Pathic Aurelius!Fúrius, libertines!</l>

lines.text: Who durst determine from my versicles
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="3">Who durst determine from my versicles</l>

lines.text: Which seem o’er softy, that I’m scant of shame.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="4">Which seem o’er softy, that I’m scant of shame.</l>

lines.text: For pious poet it behoves be chaste
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="5">For pious poet it behoves be chaste</l>

lines.text: Himself; no chastity his verses need;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="6">Himself; no chastity his verses need;</l>

lines.text: Nay, gain they finally more salt of wit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="7">Nay, gain they finally more salt of wit</l>

lines.text: When over softy and of scanty shame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="8">When over softy and of scanty shame,</l>

lines.text: Apt for exciting somewhat prurient,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="9">Apt for exciting somewhat prurient,</l>

lines.text: In boys, I say not, but in bearded men
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="10">In boys, I say not, but in bearded men</l>

lines.text: Who fail of movements in their hardened loins.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="11">Who fail of movements in their hardened loins.</l>

lines.text: Ye who so many thousand kisses sung
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="12">Ye who so many thousand kisses sung</l>

lines.text: Have read, deny male masculant I be?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="13">Have read, deny male masculant I be?</l>

lines.text: You twain I’ll . . . and . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:16" n="14">You twain I’ll <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/> and <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/> </l>

lines.text: Colony! fain to display thy games on length of thy town-bridge!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="1">Colony! fain to display thy games on length of thy town-bridge!</l>

lines.text: There, too, ready to dance, though fearing the shaking of crazy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="2">There, too, ready to dance, though fearing the shaking of crazy</l>

lines.text: Logs of the Bridgelet propt on pier-piles newly renewèd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="3">Logs of the Bridgelet propt on pier-piles newly renewèd,</l>

lines.text: Lest supine all sink deep-merged in the marish’s hollow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="4">Lest supine all sink deep-merged in the marish’s hollow,</l>

lines.text: So may the bridge hold good when builded after thy pleasure
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="5">So may the bridge hold good when builded after thy pleasure</l>

lines.text: Where Salisúbulus’ rites with solemn function are sacred,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="6">Where Salisúbulus’ rites with solemn function are sacred,</l>

lines.text: As thou (Colony!) grant me boon of mightiest laughter.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="7">As thou (Colony!) grant me boon of mightiest laughter.</l>

lines.text: Certain a townsman mine I’d lief see thrown from thy gangway
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="8">Certain a townsman mine I’d lief see thrown from thy gangway</l>

lines.text: Hurlèd head over heels precipitous whelmed in the quagmire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="9">Hurlèd head over heels precipitous whelmed in the quagmire,</l>

lines.text: Where the lake and the boglands are most rotten and stinking,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="10">Where the lake and the boglands are most rotten and stinking,</l>

lines.text: Deepest and lividest lie, the swallow of hollow voracious.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="11">Deepest and lividest lie, the swallow of hollow voracious.</l>

lines.text: Witless surely the wight whose sense is less than of boy-babe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="12">Witless surely the wight whose sense is less than of boy-babe</l>

lines.text: Two-year-old and a-sleep on trembling forearm of father.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="13">Two-year-old and a-sleep on trembling forearm of father.</l>

lines.text: He though, wedded to girl in greenest bloom of her youth-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="14">He though, wedded to girl in greenest bloom of her youth-tide,</l>

lines.text: (Bride-wife daintier bred than ever was delicate kidlet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="15">(Bride-wife daintier bred than ever was delicate kidlet,</l>

lines.text: Worthier diligent watch than grape-bunch blackest and ripest)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="16">Worthier diligent watch than grape-bunch blackest and ripest)</l>

lines.text: Suffers her sport as she please nor rates her even at hair’s worth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="17">Suffers her sport as she please nor rates her even at hair’s worth,</l>

lines.text: Nowise ’stirring himself, but lying log-like as alder
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="18">Nowise ’stirring himself, but lying log-like as alder</l>

lines.text: Felled and o’er floating the fosse of safe Ligurian woodsman,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="19">Felled and o’er floating the fosse of safe Ligurian woodsman,</l>

lines.text: Feeling withal, as though such spouse he never had own’d;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="20">Feeling withal, as though such spouse he never had own’d;</l>

lines.text: So this marvel o’ mine sees naught, and nothing can hear he,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="21">So this marvel o’ mine sees naught, and nothing can hear he,</l>

lines.text: What he himself, an he be or not be, wholly unknowing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="22">What he himself, an he be or not be, wholly unknowing.</l>

lines.text: Now would I willingly pitch such wight head first fro’ thy bridge,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="23">Now would I willingly pitch such wight head first fro’ thy bridge,</l>

lines.text: Better a-sudden t’arouse that numskull’s stolid old senses,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="24">Better a-sudden t’arouse that numskull’s stolid old senses,</l>

lines.text: Or in the sluggish mud his soul supine to deposit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="25">Or in the sluggish mud his soul supine to deposit</l>

lines.text: Even as she-mule casts iron shoe where quagmire is stiffest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:17" n="26">Even as she-mule casts iron shoe where quagmire is stiffest.</l>

lines.text: This grove to thee devote I give, Priapus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:18" n="1">This grove to thee devote I give, Priapus!</l>

lines.text: Who home be Lampsacus and holt, Priapus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:18" n="2">Who home be <placeName key="tgn,7002579">Lampsacus</placeName> and holt, Priapus!</l>

lines.text: For thee in cities worship most the shores
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:18" n="3">For thee in cities worship most the shores</l>

lines.text: Of Hellespont the richest oystery strand.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:18" n="4">Of <placeName key="tgn,7002638">Hellespont</placeName> the richest oystery strand.</l>

lines.text: This place, O youths, I protect, nor less this turfbuilded cottage,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="1">This place, O youths, I protect, nor less this turfbuilded cottage,</l>

lines.text: Roofed with its osier-twigs and thatched with its bundles of sedges;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="2">Roofed with its osier-twigs and thatched with its bundles of sedges;</l>

lines.text: I from the dried oak hewn and fashioned with rustical hatchet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="3">I from the dried oak hewn and fashioned with rustical hatchet,</l>

lines.text: Guarding them year by year while more are they evermore thriving.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="4">Guarding them year by year while more are they evermore thriving.</l>

lines.text: For here be owners twain who greet and worship my Godship,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="5">For here be owners twain who greet and worship my Godship,</l>

lines.text: He of the poor hut lord and his son, the pair of them peasants:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="6">He of the poor hut lord and his son, the pair of them peasants:</l>

lines.text: This with assiduous toil aye works the thicketty herbage
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="7">This with assiduous toil aye works the thicketty herbage</l>

lines.text: And the coarse water-grass to clear afar from my chapel:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="8">And the coarse water-grass to clear afar from my chapel:</l>

lines.text: That with his open hand ever brings me offerings humble.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="9">That with his open hand ever brings me offerings humble.</l>

lines.text: Hung up in honour mine are flowery firstlings of spring-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="10">Hung up in honour mine are flowery firstlings of spring-tide,</l>

lines.text: Wreaths with their ears still soft the tender stalklets a-crowning;
