lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="11">Wreaths with their ears still soft the tender stalklets a-crowning;</l>

lines.text: Violets pale are mine by side of the poppy-head pallid;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="12">Violets pale are mine by side of the poppy-head pallid;</l>

lines.text: With the dull yellow gourd and apples sweetest of savour;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="13">With the dull yellow gourd and apples sweetest of savour;</l>

lines.text: Lastly the blushing grape disposed in shade of the vine-tree.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="14">Lastly the blushing grape disposed in shade of the vine-tree.</l>

lines.text: Anon mine altar (this same) with blood (but you will be silent!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="15">Anon mine altar (this same) with blood (but you will be silent!)</l>

lines.text: Bearded kid and anon some horny-hoofed nanny shall sprinkle.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="16">Bearded kid and anon some horny-hoofed nanny shall sprinkle.</l>

lines.text: Wherefore Priapus is bound to requite such honours by service,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="17">Wherefore Priapus is bound to requite such honours by service,</l>

lines.text: Doing his duty to guard both vineyard and garth of his lordling.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="18">Doing his duty to guard both vineyard and garth of his lordling.</l>

lines.text: Here then, O lads, refrain from ill-mannered picking and stealing:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="19">Here then, O lads, refrain from ill-mannered picking and stealing:</l>

lines.text: Rich be the neighbour-hind and negligent eke his Priapus:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="20">Rich be the neighbour-hind and negligent eke his Priapus:</l>

lines.text: Take what be his: this path hence leadeth straight to his ownings.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:19" n="21">Take what be his: this path hence leadeth straight to his ownings.</l>

lines.text: I thuswise fashionèd by rustic art
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="1">I thuswise fashionèd by rustic art</l>

lines.text: And from dried poplar-trunk (O traveller!) hewn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="2">And from dried poplar-trunk (O traveller!) hewn,</l>

lines.text: This fieldlet, leftwards as thy glances fall,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="3">This fieldlet, leftwards as thy glances fall,</l>

lines.text: And my lord’s cottage with his pauper garth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="4">And my lord’s cottage with his pauper garth</l>

lines.text: Protect, repelling thieves’ rapacious hands.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="5">Protect, repelling thieves’ rapacious hands.</l>

lines.text: In spring with vari-coloured wreaths I’m crown’d,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="6">In spring with vari-coloured wreaths I’m crown’d,</l>

lines.text: In fervid summer with the glowing grain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="7">In fervid summer with the glowing grain,</l>

lines.text: Then with green vine-shoot and the luscious bunch,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="8">Then with green vine-shoot and the luscious bunch,</l>

lines.text: And glaucous olive-tree in bitter cold.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="9">And glaucous olive-tree in bitter cold.</l>

lines.text: The dainty she-goat from my pasture bears
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="10">The dainty she-goat from my pasture bears</l>

lines.text: Her milk-distended udders to the town:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="11">Her milk-distended udders to the town:</l>

lines.text: Out of my sheep-cotes ta’en the fatted lamb
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="12">Out of my sheep-cotes ta’en the fatted lamb</l>

lines.text: Sends home with silver right-hand heavily charged;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="13">Sends home with silver right-hand heavily charged;</l>

lines.text: And, while its mother lows, the tender calf
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="14">And, while its mother lows, the tender calf</l>

lines.text: Before the temples of the Gods must bleed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="15">Before the temples of the Gods must bleed.</l>

lines.text: Hence of such Godhead, (traveller !) stand in awe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="16">Hence of such Godhead, (traveller !) stand in awe,</l>

lines.text: Best it befits thee off to keep thy hands.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="17">Best it befits thee off to keep thy hands.</l>

lines.text: Thy cross is ready, shaped as artless yard;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="18">Thy cross is ready, shaped as artless yard;</l>

lines.text: I’m willing, ’faith (thou say’st) but ’faith here comes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="19"><q rend="double">I’m willing, ’faith</q> (thou say’st) but ’faith here comes</l>

lines.text: The boor, and plucking forth with bended arm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="20">The boor, and plucking forth with bended arm</l>

lines.text: Makes of this tool a club for doughty hand.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:20" n="21">Makes of this tool a club for doughty hand.</l>

lines.text: Aurelius, father of the famisht crew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="1">Aurelius, father of the famisht crew,</l>

lines.text: Not sole of starvelings now, but wretches who
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="2">Not sole of starvelings now, but wretches who</l>

lines.text: Were, are, or shall be in the years to come,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="3">Were, are, or shall be in the years to come,</l>

lines.text: My love, my dearling, fain art thou to strum.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="4">My love, my dearling, fain art thou to strum.</l>

lines.text: Nor privately; for nigh thou com’st and jestest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="5">Nor privately; for nigh thou com’st and jestest</l>

lines.text: And to his side close-sticking all things questest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="6">And to his side close-sticking all things questest.</l>

lines.text: ’Tis vain: while lay’st thou snares for me the worst,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="7">’Tis vain: while lay’st thou snares for me the worst,</l>

lines.text: By . . . . I will teach thee first.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="8">By <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . ."/> I will teach thee first.</l>

lines.text: An food-full thus do thou, my peace I’d keep:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="9">An food-full thus do thou, my peace I’d keep:</l>

lines.text: But what (ah me ! ah me !) compels me weep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="10">But what (ah me ! ah me !) compels me weep</l>

lines.text: Are thirst and famine to my dearling fated.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="11">Are thirst and famine to my dearling fated.</l>

lines.text: Cease thou so doing while as modest rated,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="12">Cease thou so doing while as modest rated,</l>

lines.text: Lest to thy will thou win—but . . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:21" n="13">Lest to thy will thou win—but <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . ."/></l>

lines.text: Varus, yon wight Suffenus known to thee
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="1">Varus, yon wight Suffenus known to thee</l>

lines.text: Fairly for wit, free talk, urbanity,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="2">Fairly for wit, free talk, urbanity,</l>

lines.text: The same who scribbles verse in amplest store—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="3">The same who scribbles verse in amplest store—</l>

lines.text: Methinks he fathers thousands ten or more
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="4">Methinks he fathers thousands ten or more</l>

lines.text: Indited not as wont on palimpsest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="5">Indited not as wont on palimpsest,</l>

lines.text: But paper-royal, brand-new boards, and best
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="6">But paper-royal, brand-new boards, and best</l>

lines.text: Fresh bosses, crimson ribbands, sheets with lead
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="7">Fresh bosses, crimson ribbands, sheets with lead</l>

lines.text: Ruled, and with pumice-powder all well polished.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="8">Ruled, and with pumice-powder all well polished.</l>

lines.text: These as thou readest, seem that fine, urbane
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="9">These as thou readest, seem that fine, urbane</l>

lines.text: Suffenus, goat-herd mere, or ditcher-swain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="10">Suffenus, goat-herd mere, or ditcher-swain</l>

lines.text: Once more, such horrid change is there, so vile.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="11">Once more, such horrid change is there, so vile.</l>

lines.text: What must we wot thereof? a Droll erst while,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="12">What must we wot thereof? a Droll erst while,</l>

lines.text: Or (if aught) cleverer, he with converse meets,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="13">Or (if aught) cleverer, he with converse meets,</l>

lines.text: He now in dullness, dullest villain beats
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="14">He now in dullness, dullest villain beats</l>

lines.text: Forthright on handling verse, nor is the wight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="15">Forthright on handling verse, nor is the wight</l>

lines.text: Ever so happy as when verse he write:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="16">Ever so happy as when verse he write:</l>

lines.text: So self admires he with so full delight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="17">So self admires he with so full delight.</l>

lines.text: In sooth, we all thus err, nor man there be
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="18">In sooth, we all thus err, nor man there be</l>

lines.text: But in some matter a Suffenus see
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="19">But in some matter a Suffenus see</l>

lines.text: Thou canst: his lache allotted none shall lack
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="20">Thou canst: his lache allotted none shall lack</l>

lines.text: Yet spy we nothing of our back-borne pack.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:22" n="21">Yet spy we nothing of our back-borne pack.</l>

head: TO FURIUS SATIRICALLY PRAISING HIS POVERTY

lines.text: Furius !Nor chest, nor slaves can claim,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="1">Furius !Nor chest, nor slaves can claim,</l>

lines.text: Bug, Spider, nor e’e n hearth aflame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="2">Bug, Spider, nor e’e n hearth aflame,</l>

lines.text: Yet thine a sire and step-dame who
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="3">Yet thine a sire and step-dame who</l>

lines.text: Wi’ tooth can ever flint-food chew!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="4">Wi’ tooth can ever flint-food chew!</l>

lines.text: So thou, and pleasant happy life
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="5">So thou, and pleasant happy life</l>

lines.text: Lead wi’ thy parents wooden wife.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="6">Lead wi’ thy parents wooden wife.</l>

lines.text: Nor be this marvel: hale are all,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="7">Nor be this marvel: hale are all,</l>

lines.text: Well ye digest; no fears appal
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="8">Well ye digest; no fears appal</l>

lines.text: For household-arsons, heavy ruin,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="9">For household-arsons, heavy ruin,</l>

lines.text: Plunderings impious, poison-brewin’
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="10">Plunderings impious, poison-brewin’</l>

lines.text: Or other parlous case forlorn.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="11">Or other parlous case forlorn.</l>

lines.text: Your frames are hard and dried like horn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="12">Your frames are hard and dried like horn,</l>

lines.text: Or if more arid aught ye know
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="13">Or if more arid aught ye know</l>

lines.text: By suns and frosts and hunger-throe.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="14">By suns and frosts and hunger-throe.</l>

lines.text: Then why not happy as thou’rt hale?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="15">Then why not happy as thou’rt hale?</l>

lines.text: Sweat’s strange to thee, spit fails, and fail
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="16">Sweat’s strange to thee, spit fails, and fail</l>

lines.text: Phlegm and foul snivel from the nose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="17">Phlegm and foul snivel from the nose.</l>

lines.text: Add cleanness that aye cleanlier shows
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="18">Add cleanness that aye cleanlier shows</l>

lines.text: A bum than salt-pot cleanlier,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="19">A bum than salt-pot cleanlier,</l>

lines.text: Nor ten times cack’st in total year,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="20">Nor ten times cack’st in total year,</l>

lines.text: And harder ’tis than pebble or bean
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="21">And harder ’tis than pebble or bean</l>

lines.text: Which rubbed in hand or crumbled, e’en
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="22">Which rubbed in hand or crumbled, e’en</l>

lines.text: On finger ne’er shall make unclean.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="23">On finger ne’er shall make unclean.</l>

lines.text: Such blessings (Furius !) such a prize
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="24">Such blessings (Furius !) such a prize</l>

lines.text: Never belittle nor despise;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="25">Never belittle nor despise;</l>

lines.text: Hundred sesterces seek no more
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="26">Hundred sesterces seek no more</l>

lines.text: With wonted prayer—enow’s thy store!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:23" n="27">With wonted prayer—enow’s thy store!</l>

head: TOJUVENTIUS CONCERNING THE CHOICE OF A FRIEND

lines.text: O of Juventian youths the flowret fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="1">O of Juventian youths the flowret fair</l>

lines.text: Not of these only, but of all that were
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="2">Not of these only, but of all that were</l>

lines.text: Or shall be, coming in the coming years,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="3">Or shall be, coming in the coming years,</l>

lines.text: Better waste Midas’ wealth (to me appears)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="4">Better waste Midas’ wealth (to me appears)</l>

lines.text: On him that owns nor slave nor money-chest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="5">On him that owns nor slave nor money-chest</l>

lines.text: Than thou shouldst suffer by his love possest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="6">Than thou shouldst suffer by his love possest.</l>

lines.text: What! is he vile or not fair?Yes! I attest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="7"><q rend="double">What! is he vile or not fair?</q><q rend="double">Yes!</q> I attest, </l>

lines.text: Yet owns this man so comely neither slaves nor chest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="8"><q rend="double">Yet owns this man so comely neither slaves nor chest</q> </l>

lines.text: My words disdain thou or accept at best
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="9"><q rend="double; merge">My words disdain thou or accept at best</q></l>

lines.text: Yet neither slave he owns nor money-chest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:24" n="10"><q rend="double; merge">Yet neither slave he owns nor money-chest.</q></l>

lines.text: Thou bardache Thallus! more than Coney’s robe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="1">Thou bardache Thallus! more than Coney’s robe</l>

lines.text: Soft, or goose-marrow or ear’s lowmost lobe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="2">Soft, or goose-marrow or ear’s lowmost lobe,</l>

lines.text: Or Age’s languid yard and cobweb’d part,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="3">Or Age’s languid yard and cobweb’d part,</l>

lines.text: Same Thallus greedier than the gale thou art,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="4">Same Thallus greedier than the gale thou art,</l>

lines.text: When the Kite-goddess shows thee Gulls agape,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="5">When the Kite-goddess shows thee Gulls agape,</l>

lines.text: Return my muffler thou hast dared to rape,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="6">Return my muffler thou hast dared to rape,</l>

lines.text: Saetaban napkins, tablets of Thynos, all
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="7">Saetaban napkins, tablets of Thynos, all</l>

lines.text: Which (Fool!) ancestral heirlooms thou didst call.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="8">Which (Fool!) ancestral heirlooms thou didst call.</l>

lines.text: These now unglueing from thy claws restore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="9">These now unglueing from thy claws restore,</l>

lines.text: Lest thy soft hands, and floss-like flanklets score
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="10">Lest thy soft hands, and floss-like flanklets score </l>

lines.text: The burning scourges, basely signed and lined,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="11">The burning scourges, basely signed and lined,</l>

lines.text: And thou unwonted toss like wee barque tyned
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="12">And thou unwonted toss like wee barque tyned</l>

lines.text: ’Mid vasty Ocean vexed by madding wind!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:25" n="13">’Mid vasty Ocean vexed by madding wind!</l>

lines.text: Furius! our Villa never Austral force
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:26" n="1">Furius! our Villa never Austral force</l>

lines.text: Broke, neither set thereon Favonius’ course,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:26" n="2">Broke, neither set thereon Favonius’ course,</l>

lines.text: Nor savage Boreas, nor Epeliot’s strain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:26" n="3">Nor savage Boreas, nor Epeliot’s strain,</l>

lines.text: But fifteen thousand crowns and hundreds twain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:26" n="4">But fifteen thousand crowns and hundreds twain</l>

lines.text: Wreckt it, —Oh ruinous by-wind, breezy bane!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:26" n="5">Wreckt it, —Oh ruinous by-wind, breezy bane!</l>

lines.text: Thou youngling drawer of Falernian old
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="1">Thou youngling drawer of Falernian old</l>

lines.text: Crown me the goblets with a bitterer wine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="2">Crown me the goblets with a bitterer wine</l>

lines.text: As was Postumia’s law that rules the feast
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="3">As was Postumia’s law that rules the feast</l>

lines.text: Than ebriate grape-stone more inebriate.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="4">Than ebriate grape-stone more inebriate.</l>

lines.text: But ye fare whither please ye (water-nymphs!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="5">But ye fare whither please ye (water-nymphs!)</l>

lines.text: To wine pernicious, and to sober folk
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="6">To wine pernicious, and to sober folk</l>

lines.text: Migrate ye: mere Thyonian juice be here!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:27" n="7">Migrate ye: mere Thyonian juice be here!</l>

head: TO FRIENDS ON RETURN FROM TRAVEL

lines.text: Followers of Piso, empty band
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="1">Followers of Piso, empty band</l>

lines.text: With your light budgets packt to hand,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="2">With your light budgets packt to hand,</l>

lines.text: Veránius best! Fabúllus mine!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="3">Veránius best! Fabúllus mine!</l>

lines.text: What do ye? Bore ye enough, in fine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="4">What do ye? Bore ye enough, in fine</l>

lines.text: Of frost and famine with yon sot?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="5">Of frost and famine with yon sot?</l>

lines.text: What loss or gain have haply got
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="6">What loss or gain have haply got</l>

lines.text: Your tablets? so, whenas I ranged
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="7">Your tablets? so, whenas I ranged</l>

lines.text: With Praetor, gains for loss were changed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="8">With Praetor, gains for loss were changed.</l>

lines.text: O Memmius! thou did’st long and late
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="9"><q rend="double">O Memmius! thou did’st long and late</q> </l>

lines.text: . . . me supine slow and . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="10"><q rend="double; merge"><gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/> me supine slow and <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/></q></l>

lines.text: But (truly see I) in such case
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="11">But (truly see I) in such case</l>

lines.text: Diddled you were by wight as base
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="12">Diddled you were by wight as base</l>

lines.text: Sans mercy. Noble friends go claim!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="13">Sans mercy. Noble friends go claim!</l>

lines.text: Now god and goddess give you grame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="14">Now god and goddess give you grame</l>

lines.text: Disgrace of Romulus! Remus’ shame!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:28" n="15">Disgrace of Romulus! Remus’ shame!</l>

head: TO CAESAR OF MAMURRA, CALLED MENTULA

lines.text: Who e’er could witness this (who could endure
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="1">Who e’er could witness this (who could endure </l>

lines.text: Except the lewdling, dicer, greedy-gut)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="2">Except the lewdling, dicer, greedy-gut)</l>

lines.text: That should Mamurra get what hairy Gaul
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="3">That should Mamurra get what hairy <placeName key="tgn,1000070">Gaul</placeName></l>

lines.text: And all that farthest Britons held whilòme?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="4">And all that farthest Britons held whilòme?</l>

lines.text: (Thou bardache Romulus!) this wilt see and bear?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="4a">(Thou bardache Romulus!) this wilt see and bear?</l>

lines.text: Then art a lewdling, dicer, greedy-gut!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="5">Then art a lewdling, dicer, greedy-gut!</l>

lines.text: He now superb with pride superfluous
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="6">He now superb with pride superfluous</l>

lines.text: Shall go perambulate the bedrooms all
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="7">Shall go perambulate the bedrooms all</l>

lines.text: Like white-robed dovelet or Adonis-love.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="8">Like white-robed dovelet or Adonis-love.</l>

lines.text: Romulus thou bardache! this wilt see and bear?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="9">Romulus thou bardache! this wilt see and bear?</l>

lines.text: Then art a lewdling, dicer, greedy-gut!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="10">Then art a lewdling, dicer, greedy-gut!</l>

lines.text: Is’t for such like name, sole Emperor thou!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="11">Is’t for such like name, sole Emperor thou!</l>

lines.text: Thou soughtest extreme Occidental Isle?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="12">Thou soughtest extreme Occidental Isle?</l>

lines.text: That this your . . . . Mentula
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="13">That this your <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . "/> Mentula</l>

lines.text: Millions and Milliards might at will absorb?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="14">Millions and Milliards might at will absorb?</l>

lines.text: What is’t but Liberality misplaced?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="15">What is’t but Liberality misplaced?</l>

lines.text: What trifles wasted he, small heirlooms spent?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="16">What trifles wasted he, small heirlooms spent?</l>

lines.text: First his paternal goods were clean dispersed;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="17">First his paternal goods were clean dispersed;</l>

lines.text: Second went Pontus’ spoils and for the third,—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="18">Second went <placeName key="tgn,7016619">Pontus</placeName>’ spoils and for the third,—</l>

lines.text: Ebro-land,—weets it well gold-rolling Tage.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="19">Ebro-land,—weets it well gold-rolling Tage.</l>

lines.text: Fear him the Gallias? Him the Britons’ fear?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="20">Fear him the Gallias? Him the Britons’ fear? </l>

lines.text: Why cherish this ill-wight? what ’vails he do?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="21">Why cherish this ill-wight? what ’vails he do?</l>

lines.text: Save fat paternal heritage devour?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="22">Save fat paternal heritage devour?</l>

lines.text: Lost ye for such a name, o puissant pair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="23">Lost ye for such a name, o puissant pair</l>

lines.text: (Father and Son-in-law), our all-in-all?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:29" n="24">(Father and Son-in-law), our all-in-all?</l>

lines.text: Alfénus! short of memory, false to comrades dearest-dear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="1">Alfénus! short of memory, false to comrades dearest-dear,</l>

lines.text: Now hast no pity (hardened Soul!) for friend and loving fere?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="2">Now hast no pity (hardened Soul!) for friend and loving fere?</l>

lines.text: Now to betray me, now to guile. thou (traitor!) ne’er dost pause?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="3">Now to betray me, now to guile. thou (traitor!) ne’er dost pause?</l>

lines.text: Yet impious feats of fraudful men ne’er force the Gods’ applause:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="4">Yet impious feats of fraudful men ne’er force the Gods’ applause:</l>

lines.text: When heed’st thou not deserting me (Sad me!) in sorest scathe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="5">When heed’st thou not deserting me (Sad me!) in sorest scathe,</l>

lines.text: Ah say whate’er shall humans do? in whom shall man show faith?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="6">Ah say whate’er shall humans do? in whom shall man show faith?</l>

lines.text: For sure thou bad’st me safely yield my spirit (wretch!) to thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="7">For sure thou bad’st me safely yield my spirit (wretch!) to thee,</l>

lines.text: Lulling my love as though my life were all security.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="8">Lulling my love as though my life were all security.</l>

lines.text: The same now dost withdraw thyself and every word and deed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="9">The same now dost withdraw thyself and every word and deed</l>

lines.text: Thou suffer’st winds and airy clouds to sweep fromout thy head.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="10">Thou suffer’st winds and airy clouds to sweep fromout thy head.</l>

lines.text: But an forget thou, mindful be the Gods, and Faith in mind
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="11">But an forget thou, mindful be the Gods, and Faith in mind</l>

lines.text: Bears thee, and soon shall gar thee rue the deeds by thee design’d.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:30" n="12">Bears thee, and soon shall gar thee rue the deeds by thee design’d.</l>

head: ON RETURN TO SIRMIO AND HIS VILLA

lines.text: Sirmio! of Islands and Peninsulas
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="1"><persName><surname>Sirmio</surname></persName>! of Islands and Peninsulas</l>

lines.text: Eyelet, and whatsoe’er in limpid meres
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="2">Eyelet, and whatsoe’er in limpid meres</l>

lines.text: And vasty Ocean either Neptune owns,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="3">And vasty Ocean either Neptune owns,</l>

lines.text: Thy scenes how willing-glad once more I see,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="4">Thy scenes how willing-glad once more I see,</l>

lines.text: At pain believing Thynia and the Fields
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="5">At pain believing Thynia and the Fields</l>

lines.text: Bithynian left, I’m safe to sight thy Site.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="6">Bithynian left, I’m safe to sight thy Site.</l>

lines.text: Oh what more blessèd be than cares resolved,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="7">Oh what more blessèd be than cares resolved,</l>

lines.text: When mind casts burthen and by peregrine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="8">When mind casts burthen and by peregrine</l>

lines.text: Work over wearied, lief we hie us home
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="9">Work over wearied, lief we hie us home</l>

lines.text: To lie reposing in the longed-for bed!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="10">To lie reposing in the longed-for bed!</l>

lines.text: This be the single meed for toils so triste.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="11">This be the single meed for toils so triste.</l>

lines.text: Hail, O fair Sirmio, in thy lord rejoice:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="12">Hail, O fair <persName><surname>Sirmio</surname></persName>, in thy lord rejoice:</l>

lines.text: And ye, O’ waves of Lybian Lake be glad,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="13">And ye, O’ waves of Lybian Lake be glad,</l>

lines.text: And laugh what laughter pealeth in my home.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:31" n="14">And laugh what laughter pealeth in my home.</l>

lines.text: ILL love my Ipsithilla sweetest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="1">ILL love my Ipsithilla sweetest,</l>

lines.text: My desires and my Wit the meetest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="2">My desires and my Wit the meetest,</l>

lines.text: So bid me join thy nap o’ noon!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="3">So bid me join thy nap o’ noon!</l>

lines.text: Then (after bidding) add the boon
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="4">Then (after bidding) add the boon</l>

lines.text: Undraw thy threshold-bolt none dare,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="5">Undraw thy threshold-bolt none dare,</l>

lines.text: Lest thou be led afar to fare;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="6">Lest thou be led afar to fare;</l>

lines.text: Nay bide at home, for us prepare
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="7">Nay bide at home, for us prepare</l>

lines.text: Nine-fold continuous love-delights.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="8">Nine-fold continuous love-delights.</l>

lines.text: But aught do thou to hurry things,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="9">But aught do thou to hurry things,</l>

lines.text: For dinner-full I lie aback,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="10">For dinner-full I lie aback,</l>

lines.text: And gown and tunic through I crack.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:32" n="11">And gown and tunic through I crack.</l>

lines.text: OH, best of robbers who in Baths delight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="1">OH, best of robbers who in Baths delight, </l>

lines.text: Vibennius, sire and son, the Ingle hight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="2">Vibennius, sire and son, the Ingle hight,</l>

lines.text: (For that the father’s hand be fouler one
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="3">(For that the father’s hand be fouler one</l>

lines.text: And with his anus greedier is the Son)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="4">And with his anus greedier is the Son)</l>

lines.text: Why not to banishment and evil hours
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="5">Why not to banishment and evil hours</l>

lines.text: Haste ye, when all the parent’s plundering powers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="6">Haste ye, when all the parent’s plundering powers</l>

lines.text: Are public knowledge, nor canst gain a Cent
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="7">Are public knowledge, nor canst gain a Cent</l>

lines.text: Son! by the vending of thy pilèd vent.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:33" n="8">Son! by the vending of thy pilèd vent.</l>

lines.text: Diana’s faith inbred we bear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="1">Diana’s faith inbred we bear</l>

lines.text: Youths whole of heart and maidens fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="2">Youths whole of heart and maidens fair,</l>

lines.text: Let boys no blemishes impair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="3">Let boys no blemishes impair,</l>

lines.text: And girls of Dian sing!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="4"> And girls of Dian sing!</l>

lines.text: O great Latonian progeny,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="5">O great Latonian progeny,</l>

lines.text: Of greatest Jove descendancy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="6">Of greatest Jove descendancy,</l>

lines.text: Whom mother bare ’neath olive-tree,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="7">Whom mother bare ’neath olive-tree,</l>

lines.text: Deep in the Delian dell;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="8"> Deep in the Delian dell;</l>

lines.text: That of the mountains reign thou Queen
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="9">That of the mountains reign thou Queen</l>

lines.text: And forest ranges ever green,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="10">And forest ranges ever green,</l>

lines.text: And coppices by man unseen,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="11">And coppices by man unseen,</l>

lines.text: And rivers resonant.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="12">And rivers resonant.</l>

lines.text: Thou art Lucína, Juno hight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="13">Thou art Lucína, Juno hight</l>

lines.text: By mothers lien in painful plight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="14">By mothers lien in painful plight,</l>

lines.text: Thou puissant Trivia and the Light
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="15">Thou puissant Trivia and the Light</l>

lines.text: Bastard, yclept the Lune.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="16">Bastard, yclept the <persName><surname>Lune</surname></persName>.</l>

lines.text: Thou goddess with thy monthly stage,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="17">Thou goddess with thy monthly stage,</l>

lines.text: The yearly march doth mete and guage
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="18">The yearly march doth mete and guage</l>

lines.text: An d rustic peasant’s messuage,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="19">An d rustic peasant’s messuage,</l>

lines.text: Dost brim with best o’ crops,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="20">Dost brim with best o’ crops,</l>

lines.text: Be hailed by whatso name of grace,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="21">Be hailed by whatso name of grace, </l>

lines.text: Please thee and olden Romulus’ race,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="22">Please thee and olden Romulus’ race, </l>

lines.text: Thy wonted favour deign embrace,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="23">Thy wonted favour deign embrace,</l>

lines.text: And save with choicest aid.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:34" n="24">And save with choicest aid.</l>

lines.text: Now to that tender bard, my Comrade fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="1">Now to that tender bard, my Comrade fair,</l>

lines.text: (Cecilius) say I, Paper go, declare,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="2">(Cecilius) say I, <q rend="double">Paper go, declare,</q></l>

lines.text: Verona must we make and bid to New
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="3"><q rend="double; merge"><placeName key="perseus,Verona">Verona</placeName> must we make and bid to New</q></l>

lines.text: Comum’s town-walls and Larian Shores adieu;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="4"><q rend="double; merge"><placeName key="perseus,Comum">Comum</placeName>’s town-walls and Larian Shores adieu;</q></l>

lines.text: For I determined certain fancies he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="5">For I determined certain fancies he</l>

lines.text: Accept from mutual friend to him and me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="6">Accept from mutual friend to him and me.</l>

lines.text: Wherefore he will, if wise, devour the way,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="7">Wherefore he will, if wise, devour the way,</l>

lines.text: Though the blonde damsel thousand times essay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="8">Though the blonde damsel thousand times essay</l>

lines.text: Recall his going and with arms a-neck
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="9">Recall his going and with arms a-neck</l>

lines.text: A-winding would e’er seek his course to check;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="10">A-winding would e’er seek his course to check;</l>

lines.text: A girl who (if the truth be truly told)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="11">A girl who (if the truth be truly told)</l>

lines.text: Dies of a hopeless passion uncontroul’d;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="12">Dies of a hopeless passion uncontroul’d;</l>

lines.text: For since the doings of the Díndymus-dame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="13">For since the doings of the Díndymus-dame,</l>

lines.text: By himself storied, she hath read, a flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="14">By himself storied, she hath read, a flame</l>

lines.text: Wasting her inmost marrow-core hath burned.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="15">Wasting her inmost marrow-core hath burned. </l>

lines.text: I pardon thee, than Sapphic Muse more learn’d,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="16">I pardon thee, than Sapphic Muse more learn’d,</l>

lines.text: Damsel: for truly sung in sweetest lays
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="17">Damsel: for truly sung in sweetest lays</l>

lines.text: Was by Cecilius Magna Mater’s praise.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:35" n="18">Was by Cecilius Magna Mater’s praise.</l>

head: ONTHE ANNALS—A SO-CALLED POEM OF VOLUSIUS

lines.text: Volusius’ Annals, paper scum-bewrayed!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="1">Volusius’ Annals, paper scum-bewrayed!</l>

lines.text: Fulfil that promise erst my damsel made;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="2">Fulfil that promise erst my damsel made;</l>

lines.text: Who vowed to Holy Venus and her son,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="3">Who vowed to Holy Venus and her son,</l>

lines.text: Cupid, should I return to her anon
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="4">Cupid, should I return to her anon</l>

lines.text: And cease to brandish iamb-lines accurst,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="5">And cease to brandish iamb-lines accurst,</l>

lines.text: The writ selected erst of bards the worst
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="6">The writ selected erst of bards the worst</l>

lines.text: She to the limping Godhead would devote
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="7">She to the limping Godhead would devote</l>

lines.text: With slowly-burning wood of illest note.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="8">With slowly-burning wood of illest note.</l>

lines.text: This was the vilest which my girl could find
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="9">This was the vilest which my girl could find</l>

lines.text: With vow facetious to the Gods assigned.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="10">With vow facetious to the Gods assigned. </l>

lines.text: Now, O Creation of the azure sea,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="11">Now, O Creation of the azure sea,</l>

lines.text: Holy Idalium, Urian havenry
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="12">Holy <placeName key="tgn,7002336">Idalium</placeName>, Urian havenry</l>

lines.text: Haunting, Ancona, Cnidos’ reedy site,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="13">Haunting, <placeName key="perseus,Ancona">Ancona</placeName>, <placeName key="tgn,5003757">Cnidos</placeName>’ reedy site,</l>

lines.text: Amathus, Golgos, and the tavern hight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="14"><placeName key="perseus,Amathus">Amathus</placeName>, Golgos, and the tavern hight</l>

lines.text: Durrachium-thine Adrian abode—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="15">Durrachium-thine Adrian abode—</l>

lines.text: The vow accepting, recognize the vowed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="16">The vow accepting, recognize the vowed</l>

lines.text: As not unworthy and unhandsome naught.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="17">As not unworthy and unhandsome naught.</l>

lines.text: But do ye meanwhile to the fire be brought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="18">But do ye meanwhile to the fire be brought, </l>

lines.text: That teem with boorish jest of sorry blade,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="19">That teem with boorish jest of sorry blade, </l>

lines.text: Volusius’ Annals, paper scum-bewrayed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:36" n="20">Volusius’ Annals, paper scum-bewrayed.</l>

head: TO THE FREQUENTERS OF A LOW TAVERN

lines.text: Salacious Tavern and ye taverner-host,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="1">Salacious Tavern and ye taverner-host,</l>

lines.text: From Pileate Brothers the ninth pile-post,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="2">From Pileate Brothers the ninth pile-post,</l>

lines.text: D’ye claim, you only of the, mentule boast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="3">D’ye claim, you only of the, mentule boast,</l>

lines.text: D’ye claim alone what damsels be the best
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="4">D’ye claim alone what damsels be the best</l>

lines.text: To swive: as he-goats holding all the rest?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="5">To swive: as he-goats holding all the rest?</l>

lines.text: Is’t when like boobies sit ye incontinent here,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="6">Is’t when like boobies sit ye incontinent here,</l>

lines.text: One or two hundred, deem ye that I fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="7">One or two hundred, deem ye that I fear</l>

lines.text: Two hundred . . . . . at one brunt?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="8">Two hundred <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . ."/> at one brunt?</l>

lines.text: Ay, think so, natheless all your tavern-front
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="9">Ay, think so, natheless all your tavern-front</l>

lines.text: With many a scorpion I will over-write.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="10">With many a scorpion I will over-write.</l>

lines.text: For that my damsel, fro’ my breast took flight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="11">For that my damsel, fro’ my breast took flight,</l>

lines.text: By me so lovèd, as shall loved be none,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="12">By me so lovèd, as shall loved be none,</l>

lines.text: Wherefor so mighty wars were waged and won,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="13">Wherefor so mighty wars were waged and won,</l>

lines.text: Does sit in public here. Ye fain, rich wights,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="14">Does sit in public here. Ye fain, rich wights,</l>

lines.text: All woo her: thither too (the chief of slights !)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="15">All woo her: thither too (the chief of slights !) </l>

lines.text: All pitiful knaves and by-street wenchers fare,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="16">All pitiful knaves and by-street wenchers fare,</l>

lines.text: And thou, (than any worse), with hanging hair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="17">And thou, (than any worse), with hanging hair,</l>

lines.text: In coney-breeding Celtiberia bred,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="18">In coney-breeding Celtiberia bred,</l>

lines.text: Egnatius! bonnified by beard full-fed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="19">Egnatius! bonnified by beard full-fed,</l>

lines.text: And teeth with Spanish urine polishèd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:37" n="20">And teeth with Spanish urine polishèd.</l>

lines.text: Cornificius! ’Tis ill with thy Catullus,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="1">Cornificius! ’Tis ill with thy Catullus,</l>

lines.text: ’Tis ill (by Hercules) distressfully:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="2">’Tis ill (by Hercules) distressfully:</l>

lines.text: Iller and iller every day and hour.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="3"><placeName key="tgn,1124856">Iller</placeName> and iller every day and hour.</l>

lines.text: Whose soul (as smallest boon and easiest)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="4">Whose soul (as smallest boon and easiest)</l>

lines.text: With what of comfort hast thou deign’d console?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="5">With what of comfort hast thou deign’d console?</l>

lines.text: Wi’ thee I’m angered! Dost so prize my love?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="6">Wi’ thee I’m angered! Dost so prize my love?</l>

lines.text: Yet some consoling utterance had been well
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="7">Yet some consoling utterance had been well</l>

lines.text: Though sadder ’twere than Simonídean tears.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:38" n="8">Though sadder ’twere than Simonídean tears.</l>

head: ON EGNATIUS OF THE WHITE TEETH

lines.text: Egnatius for that owns he teeth snow-white,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="1">Egnatius for that owns he teeth snow-white,</l>

lines.text: Grins ever, everywhere. When placed a wight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="2">Grins ever, everywhere. When placed a wight</l>

lines.text: In dock, when pleader would draw tears, the while
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="3">In dock, when pleader would draw tears, the while</l>

lines.text: He grins. When pious son at funeral pile
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="4">He grins. When pious son at funeral pile</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="5"/>

lines.text: Mourns, or lone mother sobs for sole lost son,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0">Mourns, or lone mother sobs for sole lost son,</l>

lines.text: He grins. Whate’er, whene’er, howe’er is done,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="6">He grins. Whate’er, whene’er, howe’er is done,</l>

lines.text: Of deed he grins. Such be his malady,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="7">Of deed he grins. Such be his malady,</l>

lines.text: Nor kind, nor courteous-so beseemeth me—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="8">Nor kind, nor courteous-so beseemeth me—</l>

lines.text: Then take thou good Egnatius, rede of mine!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="9">Then take thou good Egnatius, rede of mine!</l>

lines.text: Wert Thou Corrupt Sabine Or A Tiburtine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="10">Wert Thou Corrupt Sabine Or A Tiburtine,</l>

lines.text: Stuffed Umbrian or Tuscan overgrown
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="11">Stuffed Umbrian or Tuscan overgrown</l>

lines.text: Swarthy Lanuvian with his teeth-rows shown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="12">Swarthy Lanuvian with his teeth-rows shown,</l>

lines.text: Transpadan also, that mine own I touch,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="13">Transpadan also, that mine own I touch,</l>

lines.text: Or any washing teeth to shine o’er much,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="14">Or any washing teeth to shine o’er much,</l>

lines.text: Yet thy incessant grin I would not see,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="15">Yet thy incessant grin I would not see,</l>

lines.text: For naught than laughter silly sillier be.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="16">For naught than laughter silly sillier be.</l>

lines.text: Thou Celtiber art, in Celtiberia born,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="17">Thou Celtiber art, in Celtiberia born,</l>

lines.text: Where man who’s urined therewith loves a-morn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="18">Where man who’s urined therewith loves a-morn</l>

lines.text: His teeth and ruddy gums to scour and score;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="19">His teeth and ruddy gums to scour and score;</l>

lines.text: So the more polisht are your teeth, the more
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="20">So the more polisht are your teeth, the more</l>

lines.text: Argue they sipping stale in ampler store.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:39" n="21">Argue they sipping stale in ampler store.</l>

head: THREATENING RAVIDUS WHO STOLE HIS MISTRESS

lines.text: What thought of folly Rávidus (poor churl!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="1">What thought of folly Rávidus (poor churl!)</l>

lines.text: Upon my iambs thus would headlong hurl?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="2">Upon my iambs thus would headlong hurl?</l>

lines.text: What good or cunning counsellor would fain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="3">What good or cunning counsellor would fain</l>

lines.text: Urge thee to struggle in such strife insane?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="4">Urge thee to struggle in such strife insane?</l>

lines.text: Is’t that the vulgar mouth thy name by rote?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="5">Is’t that the vulgar mouth thy name by rote?</l>

lines.text: What will’st thou? Wishest on any wise such note?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="6">What will’st thou? Wishest on any wise such note?</l>

lines.text: Then shalt be noted since my love so lief
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="7">Then shalt be noted since my love so lief</l>

lines.text: For love thou sued’st to thy lasting grief.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:40" n="8">For love thou sued’st to thy lasting grief.</l>

lines.text: That Ametina, worn-out whore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="1">That Ametina, worn-out whore,</l>

lines.text: Me for a myriad oft would bore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="2">Me for a myriad oft would bore,</l>

lines.text: That strumpet of th’ ignoble nose,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="3">That strumpet of th’ ignoble nose,</l>

lines.text: To leman, rakehell Formian chose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="4">To leman, rakehell Formian chose.</l>

lines.text: An ye would guard her (kinsmen folk)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="5">An ye would guard her (kinsmen folk)</l>

lines.text: Your friends and leaches d’ye convoke:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="6">Your friends and leaches d’ye convoke:</l>

lines.text: The girl’s not sound-sens’d; ask ye naught
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="7">The girl’s not sound-sens’d; ask ye naught</l>

lines.text: Of her complaint: she’s love-distraught.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:41" n="8">Of her complaint: she’s love-distraught.</l>

head: ON A STRUMPET WHO STOLE HIS TABLETS

lines.text: Come, Hendecasyllabics, many as may
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="1">Come, Hendecasyllabics, many as may</l>

lines.text: All hither, every one that of you be!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="2">All hither, every one that of you be!</l>

lines.text: That fulsome harlot makes me laughing-stock
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="3">That fulsome harlot makes me laughing-stock</l>

lines.text: And she refuses at our prayer restore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="4">And she refuses at our prayer restore</l>

lines.text: Our stolen Note-books, an such slights ye bear.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="5">Our stolen Note-books, an such slights ye bear.</l>

lines.text: Let us pursue her clamouring our demands.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="6">Let us pursue her clamouring our demands.</l>

lines.text: Who’s she? ye question: yonder one ye sight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="7"><q rend="double">Who’s she?</q> ye question: yonder one ye sight</l>

lines.text: Mincingly pacing mime-like, perfect pest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="8">Mincingly pacing mime-like, perfect pest,</l>

lines.text: With jaws wide grinning like a Gallic pup.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="9">With jaws wide grinning like a Gallic pup.</l>

lines.text: Stand all round her dunning with demands,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="10">Stand all round her dunning with demands, </l>

lines.text: Return (O rotten whore!) our noting books.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="11"><q rend="double">Return (O rotten whore!) our noting books.</q></l>

lines.text: Our noting books (O rotten whore!) return!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="12"><q rend="double; merge">Our noting books (O rotten whore!) return!</q></l>

lines.text: No doit thou car’st? O Mire! O Stuff O’ stews!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="13">No doit thou car’st? O Mire! O Stuff O’ stews!</l>

lines.text: Or if aught fouler filthier dirt there be.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="14">Or if aught fouler filthier dirt there be.</l>

lines.text: Yet must we never think these words suffice.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="15">Yet must we never think these words suffice. </l>

lines.text: But if naught else avail, at least a blush
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="16">But if naught else avail, at least a blush</l>

lines.text: Forth of that bitch-like brazen brow we’ll squeeze.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="17">Forth of that bitch-like brazen brow we’ll squeeze.</l>

lines.text: Cry all together in a higher key
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="18">Cry all together in a higher key</l>

lines.text: Restore (O rotten whore!) our noting books,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="19"><q rend="double">Restore (O rotten whore!) our noting books,</q></l>

lines.text: Our noting books (O rotten whore!) restore!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="20"><q rend="double; merge">Our noting books (O rotten whore!) restore!</q></l>

lines.text: Still naught avails us, nothing is she moved.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="21">Still naught avails us, nothing is she moved.</l>

lines.text: Now must our measures and our modes be changed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:42" n="22">Now must our measures and our modes be changed</l>

lines.text: An we would anywise our cause advance.
