lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="171">Within bestrewn thy bridegroom see</l>

lines.text: On couch of Tyrian cramoisy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="172">On couch of Tyrian cramoisy</l>

lines.text: All imminent awaiting thee.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="173">All imminent awaiting thee.</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus io,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="174"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_170"/>O Hymen Hymenaeus io,</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="175">O Hymen Hymenaeus.</l>

lines.text: For in his breast not less than thine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="176">For in his breast not less than thine</l>

lines.text: Burn high the flames that deepest shrine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="177">Burn high the flames that deepest shrine,</l>

lines.text: Yet his the lowe far deeper lien.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="178">Yet his the lowe far deeper lien.</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymemeus io,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="179"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_175"/>O Hymen Hymemeus io,</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="180">O Hymen Hymenaeus.</l>

lines.text: Let fall the maid’s soft arms, thou fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="181">Let fall the maid’s soft arms, thou fair</l>

lines.text: Boy purple-hem’d: now be thy care
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="182">Boy purple-hem’d: now be thy care</l>

lines.text: Her bridegroom’s couch she seek and share.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="183">Her bridegroom’s couch she seek and share.</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus io,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="184"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_180"/>O Hymen Hymenaeus io,</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="185">O Hymen Hymenaeus.</l>

lines.text: Ye wives time-tried to husbands wed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="186">Ye wives time-tried to husbands wed,</l>

lines.text: Well-known for chastity inbred,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="187">Well-known for chastity inbred,</l>

lines.text: Dispose the virginette a-bed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="188">Dispose the virginette a-bed.</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus io,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="189"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_185"/>O Hymen Hymenaeus io,</l>

lines.text: O Hymen Hymenaeus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="190">O Hymen Hymenaeus.</l>

lines.text: Groom, now ’tis meet thou hither pace,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="191">Groom, now ’tis meet thou hither pace,</l>

lines.text: With bride in genial bed to blend,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="192">With bride in genial bed to blend,</l>

lines.text: For sheenly shines her flowery face
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="193">For sheenly shines her flowery face</l>

lines.text: Where the white chamomiles contend
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="194"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_190"/>Where the white chamomiles contend</l>

lines.text: With poppies blushing red.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="195">With poppies blushing red.</l>

lines.text: Yet bridegroom (So may Godhead deign
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="196">Yet bridegroom (So may Godhead deign</l>

lines.text: Help me!) nowise in humbler way
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="197">Help me!) nowise in humbler way</l>

lines.text: Art fair, nor Venus shall disdain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="198">Art fair, nor <persName><surname>Venus</surname></persName> shall disdain</l>

lines.text: Thy charms, but look! how wanes the day:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="199"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_195"/>Thy charms, but look! how wanes the day:</l>

lines.text: Forward, nor loiter more!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="200">Forward, nor loiter more!</l>

lines.text: No longer loitering makest thou,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="201">No longer loitering makest thou,</l>

lines.text: Now comest thou.May Venus good
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="202">Now comest thou.May <persName><surname>Venus</surname></persName> good</l>

lines.text: Aid thee when frankly takest thou
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="203">Aid thee when frankly takest thou</l>

lines.text: Thy wishes won, nor true Love woo’d
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="204"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_200"/>Thy wishes won, nor true Love woo’d</l>

lines.text: Thou carest to conceal.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="205">Thou carest to conceal.</l>

lines.text: Of Afric’s wolds and wilds each grain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="206">Of Afric’s wolds and wilds each grain,</l>

lines.text: Or constellations glistening,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="207">Or constellations glistening,</l>

lines.text: First reckon he that of the twain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="208">First reckon he that of the twain</l>

lines.text: To count alone were fain to bring
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="209"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_205"/>To count alone were fain to bring</l>

lines.text: The many thousand joys.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="210">The many thousand joys.</l>

lines.text: Play as ye please: soon prove ye deft
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="211">Play as ye please: soon prove ye deft</l>

lines.text: At babying babes,—’twere ill design’d
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="212">At babying babes,—’twere ill design’d</l>

lines.text: A name thus ancient should be left
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="213">A name thus ancient should be left</l>

lines.text: Heirless, but issue like of kind
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="214"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_210"/>Heirless, but issue like of kind</l>

lines.text: Engendered aye should be.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="215">Engendered aye should be.</l>

lines.text: A wee Torquaitus fain I’d see
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="216">A wee Torquaitus fain I’d see</l>

lines.text: Encradled on his mother’s breast
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="217">Encradled on his mother’s breast</l>

lines.text: Put forth his tender puds while he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="218">Put forth his tender puds while he</l>

lines.text: Smiles to his sire with sweetest gest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="219"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_215"/>Smiles to his sire with sweetest gest</l>

lines.text: And liplets half apart.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="220">And liplets half apart.</l>

lines.text: Let son like father’s semblance show
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="221">Let son like father’s semblance show</l>

lines.text: (Manlius!) so with easy guess
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="222">(<persName><surname>Manlius</surname></persName>!) so with easy guess</l>

lines.text: All know him where his sire they know,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="223">All know him where his sire they know,</l>

lines.text: And still his face and form express
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="224"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_220"/>And still his face and form express</l>

lines.text: His mother’s honest love.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="225">His mother’s honest love.</l>

lines.text: Approve shall fair approof his birth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="226">Approve shall fair approof his birth</l>

lines.text: From mother’s seed-stock generous,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="227">From mother’s seed-stock generous,</l>

lines.text: As rarest fame of mother’s worth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="228">As rarest fame of mother’s worth</l>

lines.text: Unique exalts Telemachus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="229"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_225"/>Unique exalts Telemachus</l>

lines.text: Penelope’s own son.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="230">Penelope’s own son.</l>

lines.text: Fast close the door-leaves, virgin band:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="231">Fast close the door-leaves, virgin band:</l>

lines.text: Enow we’ve played.But ye the fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="232">Enow we’ve played.But ye the fair</l>

lines.text: New-wedded twain live happy, and
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="233">New-wedded twain live happy, and</l>

lines.text: Functions of lusty married pair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="234"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_230"/>Functions of lusty married pair</l>

lines.text: Exercise sans surcease.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:61" n="235">Exercise sans surcease.</l>

head: Nuptial Song By Youths And Damsels
Epithalamium
Youths
Damsels
Youths
Damsels
Youths
Damsels
Youths
Damsels
Youths
Youths and Damsels

lines.text: Vesper is here, O youths, rise all; for Vesper Olympus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="1"><persName><surname>Vesper</surname></persName> is here, O youths, rise all; for Vesper Olympus</l>

lines.text: Scales and in fine enfires what lights so long were expected!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="2">Scales and in fine enfires what lights so long were expected!</l>

lines.text: Time ’tis now to arise, now leave we tables rich laden,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="3">Time ’tis now to arise, now leave we tables rich laden,</l>

lines.text: Now shall the Virgin come; now chaunt we the Hymenaeus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="4">Now shall the Virgin come; now chaunt we the Hymenaeus.</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="5">Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: View ye the Youths, O Maids unwed? Then rise to withstand them:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="6">View ye the Youths, O Maids unwed? Then rise to withstand them:</l>

lines.text: Doubtless the night-fraught Star displays his splendour Oetean.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="7">Doubtless the night-fraught Star displays his splendour Oetean.</l>

lines.text: Sooth ’tis so; d’ye sight how Speedily sprang they to warfare?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="8">Sooth ’tis so; d’ye sight how Speedily sprang they to warfare?</l>

lines.text: Nor for a naught up-sprang: they’ll Sing what need we to conquer.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="9">Nor for a naught up-sprang: they’ll Sing what need we to conquer.</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="10">Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: Nowise easy the palm for us (Companions!) be proffer’d,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="11">Nowise easy the palm for us (Companions!) be proffer’d,</l>

lines.text: Lo! now the maidens muse and meditate matter of forethought
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="12">Lo! now the maidens muse and meditate matter of forethought</l>

lines.text: Nor meditate they in vain; they muse a humorous something.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="13">Nor meditate they in vain; they muse a humorous something.</l>

lines.text: Yet naught wonder it is, their sprites be wholly in labour.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="14">Yet naught wonder it is, their sprites be wholly in labour.</l>

lines.text: We bear divided thought one way and hearing in other:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="15">We bear divided thought one way and hearing in other:</l>

lines.text: Vanquish’t by right we must be, since Victory loveth the heedful.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="16">Vanquish’t by right we must be, since Victory loveth the heedful.</l>

lines.text: Therefore at least d’ye turn your minds the task to consider,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="17">Therefore at least d’ye turn your minds the task to consider,</l>

lines.text: Soon shall begin their say whose countersay shall befit you.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="18">Soon shall begin their say whose countersay shall befit you.</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="19">Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: Hesperus! say what flame more cruel in Heaven be fanned?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="20"><persName><surname>Hesperus</surname></persName>! say what flame more cruel in Heaven be fanned?</l>

lines.text: Thou who the girl perforce canst tear from a mother’s embraces,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="21">Thou who the girl perforce canst tear from a mother’s embraces,</l>

lines.text: Tear from a parent’s clasp her child despite of her clinging
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="22">Tear from a parent’s clasp her child despite of her clinging</l>

lines.text: And upon love-hot youth bestowest her chastest of maidenhoods!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="23">And upon love-hot youth bestowest her chastest of maidenhoods!</l>

lines.text: What shall the foeman deal more cruel to city becaptured?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="24">What shall the foeman deal more cruel to city becaptured?</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="25">Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: Hesperus! say what flame more gladsome in Heavens be shining?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="26"><persName><surname>Hesperus</surname></persName>! say what flame more gladsome in Heavens be shining?</l>

lines.text: Thou whose light makes sure long-pledged connubial promise
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="27">Thou whose light makes sure long-pledged connubial promise</l>

lines.text: Plighted erewhile by men and erstwhile plighted by parents.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="28">Plighted erewhile by men and erstwhile plighted by parents.</l>

lines.text: Yet to be ne’er fulfilled before thy fire’s ardours have risen!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="29">Yet to be ne’er fulfilled before thy fire’s ardours have risen!</l>

lines.text: What better boon can the gods bestow than hour so desirèd?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="30">What better boon can the gods bestow than hour so desirèd?</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="31">Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="31a"><gap reason="lost" extent=" * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Hesperus! one of ourselves (Companions!) carried elsewhither
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="32"><persName><surname>Hesperus</surname></persName>! one of ourselves (Companions!) carried elsewhither</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="32a"><gap reason="lost" extent=" * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="32aa"><add>Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</add></l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="32aaa"><gap reason="lost" extent=" * * * "/></l>

lines.text: For at thy coming in sight a guard is constantly watching.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="33">For at thy coming in sight a guard is constantly watching.</l>

lines.text: Hidden o’nights lurk thieves and these as oft as returnest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="34">Hidden o’nights lurk thieves and these as oft as returnest,</l>

lines.text: Hesper! thou seizest them with title changed to Eous.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="35"><persName><surname>Hesper</surname></persName>! thou seizest them with title changed to Eous.</l>

lines.text: Pleases the bevy unwed with feigned complaints to accuse thee.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="36">Pleases the bevy unwed with feigned complaints to accuse thee.</l>

lines.text: What if assail they whom their souls in secrecy cherish?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="37">What if assail they whom their souls in secrecy cherish?</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="38">Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: E’en as a flow’ret born secluded in garden enclosed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="39">E’en as a flow’ret born secluded in garden enclosed,</l>

lines.text: Unto the flock unknown and ne’er uptorn by the ploughshare,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="40">Unto the flock unknown and ne’er uptorn by the ploughshare,</l>

lines.text: Soothed by the zephyrs and strengthened by suns and nourish’t by showers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="41">Soothed by the zephyrs and strengthened by suns and nourish’t by showers</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="41a"><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Loves her many a youth and longs for her many a maiden:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="42">Loves her many a youth and longs for her many a maiden:</l>

lines.text: Yet from her lissome stalk when cropt that flower deflowered,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="43">Yet from her lissome stalk when cropt that flower deflowered,</l>

lines.text: Loves her never a youth nor longs for her ever a maiden:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="44">Loves her never a youth nor longs for her ever a maiden:</l>

lines.text: Thus while the virgin be whole, such while she’s the dearling of kinsfolk;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="45">Thus while the virgin be whole, such while she’s the dearling of kinsfolk;</l>

lines.text: Yet no sooner is lost her bloom from body polluted,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="46">Yet no sooner is lost her bloom from body polluted,</l>

lines.text: Neither to youths she is joy, nor a dearling she to the maidens.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="47">Neither to youths she is joy, nor a dearling she to the maidens.</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="48">Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: E’en as an unmated vine which born in field of the barest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="49">E’en as an unmated vine which born in field of the barest</l>

lines.text: Never upraises head nor breeds the mellowy grape-bunch,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="50">Never upraises head nor breeds the mellowy grape-bunch,</l>

lines.text: But under weight prone-bowed that tender body a-bending
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="51">But under weight prone-bowed that tender body a-bending</l>

lines.text: Makes she her root anon to touch her topmost of tendrils;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="52">Makes she her root anon to touch her topmost of tendrils;</l>

lines.text: Tends her never a hind nor tends her ever a herdsman:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="53">Tends her never a hind nor tends her ever a herdsman:</l>

lines.text: Yet if haply conjoined the same with elm as a husband,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="54">Yet if haply conjoined the same with elm as a husband,</l>

lines.text: Tends her many a hind and tends her many a herdsman:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="55">Tends her many a hind and tends her many a herdsman:</l>

lines.text: Thus is the maid when whole, uncultured waxes she aged;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="56">Thus is the maid when whole, uncultured waxes she aged;</l>

lines.text: But whenas union meet she wins her at ripest of seasons,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="57">But whenas union meet she wins her at ripest of seasons,</l>

lines.text: More to her spouse she is dear and less she’s irk to her parents.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="58">More to her spouse she is dear and less she’s irk to her parents.</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="58a"><add>Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</add></l>

lines.text: But do thou cease to resist (O Maid!) such bridegroom opposing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="59">But do thou cease to resist (O Maid!) such bridegroom opposing,</l>

lines.text: Right it is not to resist whereto consigned thee a father,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="60">Right it is not to resist whereto consigned thee a father,</l>

lines.text: Father and mother of thee unto whom obedience is owing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="61">Father and mother of thee unto whom obedience is owing.</l>

lines.text: Not is that maidenhood all thine own, but partly thy parents!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="62">Not is that maidenhood all thine own, but partly thy parents!</l>

lines.text: Owneth thy sire one third, one third is right of thy mother,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="63">Owneth thy sire one third, one third is right of thy mother,</l>

lines.text: Only the third is thine: stint thee to strive with the others,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="64">Only the third is thine: stint thee to strive with the others,</l>

lines.text: Who to the stranger son have yielded their dues with a dower!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="65">Who to the stranger son have yielded their dues with a dower!</l>

lines.text: Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:62" n="66">Hymen O Hymenaeus: Hymen here, O Hymenaeus!</l>

lines.text: O’er high deep seas in speedy ship his voyage Atys sped
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="1">O’er high deep seas in speedy ship his voyage Atys sped</l>

lines.text: Until he trod the Phrygian grove with hurried eager tread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="2">Until he trod the Phrygian grove with hurried eager tread</l>

lines.text: And as the gloomy tree-shorn stead, the she-god’s home, he sought
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="3">And as the gloomy tree-shorn stead, the she-god’s home, he sought</l>

lines.text: There sorely stung with fiery ire and madman’s vaguing thought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="4">There sorely stung with fiery ire and madman’s vaguing thought,</l>

lines.text: Share he with sharpened flint the freight wherewith his form was fraught.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="5">Share he with sharpened flint the freight wherewith his form was fraught.</l>

lines.text: Then as the she-he sensed limbs were void of manly strain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="6">Then as the she-he sensed limbs were void of manly strain</l>

lines.text: And sighted freshly shed a-ground spot of ensanguined stain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="7">And sighted freshly shed a-ground spot of ensanguined stain,</l>

lines.text: Snatched she the timbrel’s legier load with hands as snowdrops white,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="8">Snatched she the timbrel’s legier load with hands as snowdrops white,</l>

lines.text: Thy timbrel, Mother Cybele, the firstings of thy rite,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="9">Thy timbrel, Mother Cybele, the firstings of thy rite,</l>

lines.text: And as her tender finger-tips on bull-back hollow rang
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="10">And as her tender finger-tips on bull-back hollow rang</l>

lines.text: She rose a-grieving and her song to listening comrades sang.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="11">She rose a-grieving and her song to listening comrades sang.</l>

lines.text: Up Gallae, hie together, haste for Cybele’s deep grove,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="12"><q rend="double">Up Gallae, hie together, haste for Cybele’s deep grove,</q></l>

lines.text: Hie to the Dindymnean dame, ye flocks that love to rove;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="13"><q rend="double; merge">Hie to the Dindymnean dame, ye flocks that love to rove;</q></l>

lines.text: The which affecting stranger steads as bound in exile’s brunt
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="14"><q rend="double; merge">The which affecting stranger steads as bound in exile’s brunt</q></l>

lines.text: My sect pursuing led by me have nerved you to confront
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="15"><q rend="double; merge">My sect pursuing led by me have nerved you to confront</q></l>

lines.text: The raging surge of salty sea and ocean’s tyrant hand
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="16"><q rend="double; merge">The raging surge of salty sea and ocean’s tyrant hand</q></l>

lines.text: As your hate of Venus’ hest your manly forms unmann’d,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="17"><q rend="double; merge">As your hate of <persName><surname>Venus</surname></persName>’ hest your manly forms unmann’d,</q></l>

lines.text: Gladden your souls, ye mistresses, with sense of error bann’d.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="18"><q rend="double; merge">Gladden your souls, ye mistresses, with sense of error bann’d.</q></l>

lines.text: Drive from your spirits dull delay, together follow ye
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="19"><q rend="double; merge">Drive from your spirits dull delay, together follow ye</q></l>

lines.text: To hold of Phrygian goddess, home of Phrygian Cybebe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="20"><q rend="double; merge">To hold of Phrygian goddess, home of Phrygian Cybebe,</q></l>

lines.text: Whereloud the cymbal’s voice resounds with timbrel-echoes blending,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="21"><q rend="double; merge">Whereloud the cymbal’s voice resounds with timbrel-echoes blending,</q></l>

lines.text: And where the Phrygian piper drones grave bass from reed a-bending,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="22"><q rend="double; merge">And where the Phrygian piper drones grave bass from reed a-bending,</q></l>

lines.text: Where toss their ivy-circled heads with might the Maenades
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="23"><q rend="double; merge">Where toss their ivy-circled heads with might the Maenades</q></l>

lines.text: Where ply mid shrilly lullilooes the holiest mysteries,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="24"><q rend="double; merge">Where ply mid shrilly lullilooes the holiest mysteries,</q></l>

lines.text: Where to fly here and there be wont the she-god’s vaguing train,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="25"><q rend="double; merge">Where to fly here and there be wont the she-god’s vaguing train,</q></l>

lines.text: Thither behoves us lead the dance in quick-step hasty strain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="26"><q rend="double; merge">Thither behoves us lead the dance in quick-step hasty strain.</q></l>

lines.text: Soon as had Atys (bastard-she) this lay to comrades sung
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="27">Soon as had Atys (bastard-she) this lay to comrades sung</l>

lines.text: The Chorus sudden lulliloos with quivering, quavering tongue,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="28">The Chorus sudden lulliloos with quivering, quavering tongue,</l>

lines.text: Again the nimble timbrel groans, the scooped-out cymbals clash,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="29">Again the nimble timbrel groans, the scooped-out cymbals clash,</l>

lines.text: And up green Ida flits the Choir, with footsteps hurrying rash
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="30">And up green Ida flits the Choir, with footsteps hurrying rash</l>

lines.text: Then Atys frantic, panting, raves, a-wandering, lost, insane,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="31">Then Atys frantic, panting, raves, a-wandering, lost, insane,</l>

lines.text: And leads with timbrel hent and treads the shades where shadows rain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="32">And leads with timbrel hent and treads the shades where shadows rain,</l>

lines.text: Like heifer spurning load of yoke in yet unbroken pride;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="33">Like heifer spurning load of yoke in yet unbroken pride;</l>

lines.text: And the swift Gallae follow fain their first and fleet-foot guide.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="34">And the swift Gallae follow fain their first and fleet-foot guide.</l>

lines.text: But when the home of Cybele they make with toil out-worn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="35">But when the home of Cybele they make with toil out-worn</l>

lines.text: O’er much, they lay them down to sleep and gifts of Ceres scorn;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="36">O’er much, they lay them down to sleep and gifts of <persName><surname>Ceres</surname></persName> scorn;</l>

lines.text: Till heavy slumbers seal their eyelids langourous, drooping lowly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="37">Till heavy slumbers seal their eyelids langourous, drooping lowly,</l>

lines.text: And raving frenzy flies each brain departing softly, slowly.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="38">And raving frenzy flies each brain departing softly, slowly.</l>

lines.text: But when Dan Sol with radiant eyes that fire his face of gold
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="39">But when Dan Sol with radiant eyes that fire his face of gold</l>

lines.text: Surveyed white aether and solid soil and waters uncontrol’d,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="40">Surveyed white aether and solid soil and waters uncontrol’d,</l>

lines.text: And chased with steeds sonorous-hooved the shades of lingering night,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="41">And chased with steeds sonorous-hooved the shades of lingering night,</l>

lines.text: Then sleep from waking Atys fled fleeting with sudden flight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="42">Then sleep from waking Atys fled fleeting with sudden flight,</l>

lines.text: By Nymph Pasithae welcomed to palpitating breast.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="43">By Nymph Pasithae welcomed to palpitating breast.</l>

lines.text: Thus when his frenzy raging rash was soothed to gentlest rest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="44">Thus when his frenzy raging rash was soothed to gentlest rest,</l>

lines.text: Atys revolved deeds lately done, as thought from breast unfolding,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="45">Atys revolved deeds lately done, as thought from breast unfolding,</l>

lines.text: And what he’d lost and what he was with lucid sprite beholding,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="46">And what he’d lost and what he was with lucid sprite beholding,</l>

lines.text: To shallows led by surging soul again the way ’gan take.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="47">To shallows led by surging soul again the way ’gan take.</l>

lines.text: There casting glance of weeping eyes where vasty billows brake,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="48">There casting glance of weeping eyes where vasty billows brake,</l>

lines.text: Sad-voiced in pitifullest lay his native land bespake.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="49">Sad-voiced in pitifullest lay his native land bespake.</l>

lines.text: Country of me, Creatress mine, born to thee and bred,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="50"><q rend="double">Country of me, Creatress mine, born to thee and bred,</q></l>

lines.text: By hapless me abandoned as by thrall from lordling fled,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="51"><q rend="double; merge">By hapless me abandoned as by thrall from lordling fled,</q></l>

lines.text: When me to Ida’s groves and glades these vaguing footsteps bore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="52"><q rend="double; merge">When me to Ida’s groves and glades these vaguing footsteps bore</q></l>

lines.text: To tarry ’mid the snows and where lurk beasts in antres frore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="53"><q rend="double; merge">To tarry ’mid the snows and where lurk beasts in antres frore</q></l>

lines.text: And seek the deeply hidden lairs where furious ferals meet!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="54"><q rend="double; merge">And seek the deeply hidden lairs where furious ferals meet!</q></l>

lines.text: Where, Country! whither placed must I now hold thy site and seat?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="55"><q rend="double; merge">Where, Country! whither placed must I now hold thy site and seat?</q></l>

lines.text: Lief would these balls of eyes direct to thee their line of sight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="56"><q rend="double; merge">Lief would these balls of eyes direct to thee their line of sight,</q></l>

lines.text: Which for a while, a little while, would free me from despite.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="57"><q rend="double; merge">Which for a while, a little while, would free me from despite.</q></l>

lines.text: Must I for ever roam these groves from house and home afar?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="58"><q rend="double; merge">Must I for ever roam these groves from house and home afar?</q></l>

lines.text: Of country, parents, kith and kin (life’s boon) myself debar?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="59"><q rend="double; merge">Of country, parents, kith and kin (life’s boon) myself debar?</q></l>

lines.text: Fly Forum, flyPalestra, fly the Stadium, the Gymnase?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="60"><q rend="double; merge">Fly Forum, flyPalestra, fly the Stadium, the Gymnase?</q></l>

lines.text: Wretch, ah poor wretch, I’m doomed (my soul!) to mourn throughout my days,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="61"><q rend="double; merge">Wretch, ah poor wretch, I’m doomed (my soul!) to mourn throughout my days,</q></l>

lines.text: For what of form or figure is, which I failed to enjoy?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="62"><q rend="double; merge">For what of form or figure is, which I failed to enjoy?</q></l>

lines.text: I full-grown man, I blooming youth, I stripling, I a boy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="63"><q rend="double; merge">I full-grown man, I blooming youth, I stripling, I a boy,</q></l>

lines.text: I of Gymnasium erst the bloom, I too of oil the pride:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="64"><q rend="double; merge">I of Gymnasium erst the bloom, I too of oil the pride:</q></l>

lines.text: Warm was my threshold, ever stood my gateways opening wide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="65"><q rend="double; merge">Warm was my threshold, ever stood my gateways opening wide,</q></l>

lines.text: My house was ever garlanded and hung with flowery freight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="66"><q rend="double; merge">My house was ever garlanded and hung with flowery freight,</q></l>

lines.text: And couch to quit with rising sun, has ever been my fate:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="67"><q rend="double; merge">And couch to quit with rising sun, has ever been my fate:</q></l>

lines.text: Now must I Cybele’s she-slave, priestess of gods, be hight?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="68"><q rend="double; merge">Now must I Cybele’s she-slave, priestess of gods, be hight?</q></l>

lines.text: I Maenad I, mere bit of self, I neutral barren wight?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="69"><q rend="double; merge">I Maenad I, mere bit of self, I neutral barren wight?</q></l>

lines.text: I spend my life-tide couch’t beneath high-towering Phrygian peaks?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="70"><q rend="double; merge">I spend my life-tide couch’t beneath high-towering Phrygian peaks?</q></l>

lines.text: I dwell on Ida’s verdant slopes mottled with snowy streaks,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="71"><q rend="double; merge">I dwell on Ida’s verdant slopes mottled with snowy streaks,</q></l>

lines.text: Where homes the forest-haunting doe, where roams the wildling boar?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="72"><q rend="double; merge">Where homes the forest-haunting doe, where roams the wildling boar?</q></l>

lines.text: Now, now I rue my deed foredone, now, now it irks me sore!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="73"><q rend="double; merge">Now, now I rue my deed foredone, now, now it irks me sore!</q></l>

lines.text: Whenas from out those roseate lips these accents rapid flew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="74">Whenas from out those roseate lips these accents rapid flew,</l>

lines.text: Bore them to ears divine consigned a Nuncio true and new;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="75">Bore them to ears divine consigned a Nuncio true and new;</l>

lines.text: Then Cybele her lions twain disjoining from their yoke
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="76">Then Cybele her lions twain disjoining from their yoke</l>

lines.text: The left-hand enemy of the herds a-goading thus bespoke:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="77">The left-hand enemy of the herds a-goading thus bespoke:</l>

lines.text: Up feral fell! up, hie with him, see rage his foot-steps urge,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="78"><q rend="double">Up feral fell! up, hie with him, see rage his foot-steps urge,</q></l>

lines.text: See that his fury smite him till he seek the forest verge,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="79"><q rend="double; merge">See that his fury smite him till he seek the forest verge,</q></l>

lines.text: He who with over-freedom fain would fly mine empery.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="80"><q rend="double; merge">He who with over-freedom fain would fly mine empery.</q></l>

lines.text: Go, slash thy flank with lashing tail and sense the strokes of thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="81"><q rend="double; merge">Go, slash thy flank with lashing tail and sense the strokes of thee,</q></l>

lines.text: Make the whole mountain to thy roar sound and resound again,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="82"><q rend="double; merge">Make the whole mountain to thy roar sound and resound again,</q></l>

lines.text: And fiercely toss thy brawny neck that bears the tawny mane!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="83"><q rend="double; merge">And fiercely toss thy brawny neck that bears the tawny mane!</q></l>

lines.text: So quoth an angered Cybele, and yoke with hand untied:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="84">So quoth an angered Cybele, and yoke with hand untied:</l>

lines.text: The feral rose in fiery wrath and self-inciting hied,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="85">The feral rose in fiery wrath and self-inciting hied,</l>

lines.text: A-charging, roaring through the brake with breaking paws he tore.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="86">A-charging, roaring through the brake with breaking paws he tore.</l>

lines.text: But when he reached the humid sands where surges cream the shore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="87">But when he reached the humid sands where surges cream the shore,</l>

lines.text: Spying soft Atys lingering near the marbled pave of sea
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="88">Spying soft Atys lingering near the marbled pave of sea</l>

lines.text: He springs: the terror-madded wretch back to the wood doth flee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="89">He springs: the terror-madded wretch back to the wood doth flee,</l>

lines.text: Where for the remnant of her days a bondmaid’s life led she.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="90">Where for the remnant of her days a bondmaid’s life led she.</l>

lines.text: Great Goddess, Goddess Cybele, Dindymus dame divine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="91">Great Goddess, Goddess Cybele, Dindymus dame divine,</l>

lines.text: Far from my house and home thy wrath and wrack, dread mistress mine:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="92">Far from my house and home thy wrath and wrack, dread mistress mine:</l>

lines.text: Goad others on with Fury’s goad, others to Ire consign!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:63" n="93">Goad others on with Fury’s goad, others to Ire consign!</l>

head: Marriage of Peleus and Thetis
ON ANOTHER PART OF THE COVERLET

lines.text: Pine-trees gendered whilome upon soaring Peliac summit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="1">Pine-trees gendered whilome upon soaring Peliac summit</l>

lines.text: Swam (as the tale is told) through liquid surges of Neptune
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="2">Swam (as the tale is told) through liquid surges of <persName><surname>Neptune</surname></persName></l>

lines.text: Far as the Phasis-flood and frontier-land Aeetean;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="3">Far as the Phasis-flood and frontier-land Aeetean;</l>

lines.text: Whenas the youths elect, of Argive vigour the oak-heart,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="4">Whenas the youths elect, of <placeName key="tgn,5001993">Argive</placeName> vigour the oak-heart,</l>

lines.text: Longing the Golden Fleece of the Colchis-region to harry,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="5">Longing the Golden Fleece of the Colchis-region to harry,</l>

lines.text: Dared in a poop swift-paced to span salt seas and their shallows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="6">Dared in a poop swift-paced to span salt seas and their shallows,</l>

lines.text: Sweeping the deep blue seas with sweeps a-carven of fir-wood.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="7">Sweeping the deep blue seas with sweeps a-carven of fir-wood.</l>

lines.text: She, that governing Goddess of citadels crowning the cities,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="8">She, that governing Goddess of citadels crowning the cities,</l>

lines.text: Builded herself their car fast-flitting with lightest of breezes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="9">Builded herself their car fast-flitting with lightest of breezes,</l>

lines.text: Weaving plants of the pine conjoined in curve of the kelson;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="10">Weaving plants of the pine conjoined in curve of the kelson;</l>

lines.text: Foremost of all to imbue rude Amphitrite with ship-lore.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="11">Foremost of all to imbue rude Amphitrite with ship-lore.</l>

lines.text: Soon as her beak had burst through wind-rackt spaces of ocean,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="12">Soon as her beak had burst through wind-rackt spaces of ocean,</l>

lines.text: While the oar-tortured wave with spumy whiteness was blanching,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="13">While the oar-tortured wave with spumy whiteness was blanching,</l>

lines.text: Surged from the deep abyss and hoar-capped billows the faces
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="14">Surged from the deep abyss and hoar-capped billows the faces</l>

lines.text: Seaborn, Nereids eyeing theprodigy wonder-smitten.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="15">Seaborn, Nereids eyeing theprodigy wonder-smitten.</l>

lines.text: There too mortal orbs through softened spendours regarded
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="16">There too mortal orbs through softened spendours regarded</l>

lines.text: Ocean-nymphs who exposed bodies denuded of raiment
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="17">Ocean-nymphs who exposed bodies denuded of raiment</l>

lines.text: Bare to the breast upthrust from hoar froth capping the sea-depths.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="18">Bare to the breast upthrust from hoar froth capping the sea-depths.</l>

lines.text: Then Thetis Peleus fired (men say) a-sudden with love,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="19">Then Thetis Peleus fired (men say) a-sudden with love,</l>

lines.text: Then Thetis nowise spurned to mate and marry with mortal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="20">Then Thetis nowise spurned to mate and marry with mortal,</l>

lines.text: Then Thetis’ Sire himself her yoke with Peleus sanctioned.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="21">Then Thetis’ Sire himself her yoke with Peleus sanctioned.</l>

lines.text: Oh, in those happier days now fondly yearned-for, you heroes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="22">Oh, in those happier days now fondly yearned-for, you heroes</l>

lines.text: Born; (all hail!) of the gods begotten, and excellent issue
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="23">Born; (all hail!) of the gods begotten, and excellent issue</l>

lines.text: Bred by your mothers, all hail! and placid deal me your favour.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="23b">Bred by your mothers, all hail! and placid deal me your favour.</l>

lines.text: Oft with the sound of me, in strains and spells I’ll invoke you;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="24">Oft with the sound of me, in strains and spells I’ll invoke you;</l>

lines.text: You too by wedding-torch so happily, highly augmented,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="25">You too by wedding-torch so happily, highly augmented,</l>

lines.text: Peleus, Thessaly’s ward, in whose favor Jupiter himself,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="26">Peleus, <placeName key="tgn,7001399">Thessaly</placeName>’s ward, in whose favor <persName><surname>Jupiter</surname></persName> himself,</l>

lines.text: The Father of the gods, resigned his passions.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="27">The Father of the gods, resigned his passions.</l>

lines.text: You Thetis, fairest of maids Nereian, vouchsafed to marry?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="28">You Thetis, fairest of maids Nereian, vouchsafed to marry?</l>

lines.text: You did Tethys empower to woo and wed with her grandchild;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="29">You did Tethys empower to woo and wed with her grandchild;</l>

lines.text: Nor less Oceanus, with water compassing th’ Earth-globe?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="30">Nor less Oceanus, with water compassing th’ Earth-globe?</l>

lines.text: But when ended the term, and wisht-for light of the day-tide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="31">But when ended the term, and wisht-for light of the day-tide</l>

lines.text: Uprose, flocks to the house in concourse mighty, convened,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="32">Uprose, flocks to the house in concourse mighty, convened,</l>

lines.text: Thessaly all, with glad assembly the Palace fulfilling:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="33"><placeName key="tgn,7001399">Thessaly</placeName> all, with glad assembly the Palace fulfilling:</l>

lines.text: Presents afore they bring, and joy in faces declare they.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="34">Presents afore they bring, and joy in faces declare they.</l>

lines.text: Cieros abides a desert: they quit Phthiotican Tempe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="35">Cieros abides a desert: they quit Phthiotican Tempe,</l>

lines.text: Homesteads of Crannon-town, eke bulwarkt walls Larissa;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="36">Homesteads of Crannon-town, eke bulwarkt walls Larissa;</l>

lines.text: Meeting at Pharsalus, and roof Pharsalian seeking.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="37">Meeting at <placeName key="tgn,7010797">Pharsalus</placeName>, and roof Pharsalian seeking.</l>

lines.text: None will the fields now till; soft wax all necks the oxen,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="38">None will the fields now till; soft wax all necks the oxen,</l>

lines.text: Never the humble vine is purged by curve of the rake-tooth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="39">Never the humble vine is purged by curve of the rake-tooth,</l>

lines.text: Never a pruner’s hook thins out the shade of the tree-tufts,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="40">Never a pruner’s hook thins out the shade of the tree-tufts,</l>

lines.text: Never a bull up-plows broad glebe with bend of the coulter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="41">Never a bull up-plows broad glebe with bend of the coulter,</l>

lines.text: Over whose point unuse displays the squalor of rust-stain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="42">Over whose point unuse displays the squalor of rust-stain.</l>

lines.text: But in the homestead’s heart, where’er that opulent palace
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="43">But in the homestead’s heart, where’er that opulent palace</l>

lines.text: Hides a retreat, all shines with splendour of gold and of silver.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="44">Hides a retreat, all shines with splendour of gold and of silver.</l>

lines.text: Ivory blanches the seats, bright gleam the flagons a-table,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="45">Ivory blanches the seats, bright gleam the flagons a-table,</l>

lines.text: All of the mansion joys in royal riches and grandeur.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="46">All of the mansion joys in royal riches and grandeur.</l>

lines.text: But for the Diva’s use bestrewn is the genial bedstead,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="47">But for the Diva’s use bestrewn is the genial bedstead,</l>

lines.text: Hidden in midmost stead, and its polisht framework of Indian
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="48">Hidden in midmost stead, and its polisht framework of Indian</l>

lines.text: Tusk underlies its cloth empurpled by juice of the dye-shell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="49">Tusk underlies its cloth empurpled by juice of the dye-shell.</l>

lines.text: This be a figured cloth with forms of manhood primeval
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="50">This be a figured cloth with forms of manhood primeval</l>

lines.text: Showing by marvel-art the gifts and graces of heroes.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="51">Showing by marvel-art the gifts and graces of heroes.</l>

lines.text: Here upon Dia’s strand wave-resonant, ever-regarding
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="52">Here upon Dia’s strand wave-resonant, ever-regarding</l>

lines.text: Theseus borne from sight outside by fleet of the fleetest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="53">Theseus borne from sight outside by fleet of the fleetest,</l>

lines.text: Stands Ariadne with heart full-filled with furies unbated,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="54">Stands Ariadne with heart full-filled with furies unbated,</l>

lines.text: Nor can her sense as yet believe she ’spies the espied,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="55">Nor can her sense as yet believe she ’spies the espied,</l>

lines.text: When like one that awakes new roused from slumber deceptive,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="56">When like one that awakes new roused from slumber deceptive,</l>

lines.text: Sees she her hapless self lone left on loneliest sandbank:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="57">Sees she her hapless self lone left on loneliest sandbank:</l>

lines.text: While as the mindless youth with oars disturbeth the shallows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="58">While as the mindless youth with oars disturbeth the shallows,</l>

lines.text: Casts to the windy storms what vows he vainly had vowed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="59">Casts to the windy storms what vows he vainly had vowed.</l>

lines.text: Him through the sedges afar the sad-eyed maiden of Minos,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="60">Him through the sedges afar the sad-eyed maiden of Minos,</l>

lines.text: Likest a Bacchant-girl stone-carven, (O her sorrow!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="61">Likest a Bacchant-girl stone-carven, (O her sorrow!)</l>

lines.text: ’Spies, a-tossing the while on sorest billows of love-care.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="62">’Spies, a-tossing the while on sorest billows of love-care.</l>

lines.text: Now no more on her blood-hued hair fine fillets retains she,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="63">Now no more on her blood-hued hair fine fillets retains she,</l>

lines.text: No more now light veil conceals her bosom erst hidden,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="64">No more now light veil conceals her bosom erst hidden,</l>

lines.text: Now no more smooth zone contains her milky-hued paplets:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="65">Now no more smooth zone contains her milky-hued paplets:</l>

lines.text: All gear dropping adown from every part of her person
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="66">All gear dropping adown from every part of her person</l>

lines.text: Thrown, lie fronting her feet to the briny wavelets a sea-toy.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="67">Thrown, lie fronting her feet to the briny wavelets a sea-toy.</l>

lines.text: But at such now no more of her veil or her fillet a-floating
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="68">But at such now no more of her veil or her fillet a-floating</l>

lines.text: Had she regard: on you, Theseus! all of her heart-strength,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="69">Had she regard: on you, Theseus! all of her heart-strength,</l>

lines.text: All of her sprite, her mind, forlorn, were evermore hanging.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="70">All of her sprite, her mind, forlorn, were evermore hanging.</l>

lines.text: Ah, sad soul, by grief and grievance driven beside you,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="71">Ah, sad soul, by grief and grievance driven beside you,</l>

lines.text: Sowed Erycina first those brambly cares in thy bosom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="72">Sowed Erycina first those brambly cares in thy bosom,</l>

lines.text: What while issuing fierce with will enstarkened, Theseus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="73">What while issuing fierce with will enstarkened, Theseus</l>

lines.text: Forth from thebow-bent shore Piraean putting a-seawards
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="74">Forth from thebow-bent shore Piraean putting a-seawards</l>

lines.text: Reacht the Gortynian roofs where dwelt the injurious Monarch.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="75">Reacht the Gortynian roofs where dwelt the injurious Monarch.</l>

lines.text: For ’twas told of yore how forced by pestilence cruel,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="76">For ’twas told of yore how forced by pestilence cruel,</l>

lines.text: Eke as a blood rite due for the Androgeonian murder,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="77">Eke as a blood rite due for the Androgeonian murder,</l>

lines.text: Many a chosen youth and the bloom of damsels unmarried
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="78">Many a chosen youth and the bloom of damsels unmarried</l>

lines.text: Food for the Minotaur, Cecropia was wont to befurnish.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="79">Food for the Minotaur, Cecropia was wont to befurnish.</l>

lines.text: Seeing his narrow walls in such wise vexed with evils,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="80">Seeing his narrow walls in such wise vexed with evils,</l>

lines.text: Theseus of freest will for dear-loved Athens his body
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="81">Theseus of freest will for dear-loved <placeName key="perseus,Athens">Athens</placeName> his body</l>

lines.text: Offered a victim so that no more to Crete be deported
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="82">Offered a victim so that no more to <placeName key="tgn,7012056">Crete</placeName> be deported</l>

lines.text: Lives by Cecropia doomed to burials burying nowise;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="83">Lives by Cecropia doomed to burials burying nowise;</l>

lines.text: Then with a swifty ship and soft breathed breezes a-stirring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="84">Then with a swifty ship and soft breathed breezes a-stirring,</l>

lines.text: Sought he Minos the Haughty where homed in proudest of Mansions.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="85">Sought he Minos the Haughty where homed in proudest of Mansions.</l>

lines.text: Him as with yearning glance forthright espied the royal
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="86">Him as with yearning glance forthright espied the royal</l>

lines.text: Maiden, whom pure chaste couch aspiring delicate odours
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="87">Maiden, whom pure chaste couch aspiring delicate odours</l>

lines.text: Cherisht, in soft embrace of a mother comforted all-whiles,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="88">Cherisht, in soft embrace of a mother comforted all-whiles,</l>

lines.text: (E’en as the myrtles begot by the flowing floods of Eurotas,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="89">(E’en as the myrtles begot by the flowing floods of Eurotas,</l>

lines.text: Or as the tincts distinct brought forth by breath of the springtide)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="90">Or as the tincts distinct brought forth by breath of the springtide)</l>

lines.text: Never the burning lights of her eyes from gazing upon him
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="91">Never the burning lights of her eyes from gazing upon him</l>

lines.text: Turned she, before fierce flame in all her body conceived she
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="92">Turned she, before fierce flame in all her body conceived she</l>
