lines.text: Down in its deepest depths and burning within her marrow.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="93">Down in its deepest depths and burning within her marrow.</l>

lines.text: Ah, with unmitigate heart exciting wretchedmost furies,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="94">Ah, with unmitigate heart exciting wretchedmost furies,</l>

lines.text: You, Boy sacrosanct! man’s grief and gladness commingling,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="95">You, Boy sacrosanct! man’s grief and gladness commingling,</l>

lines.text: You too of Golgos Queen and Lady of leafy Idalium,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="96">You too of Golgos Queen and Lady of leafy <placeName key="tgn,7002336">Idalium</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: Whelm’d you in what manner waves that maiden fantasy-fired,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="97">Whelm’d you in what manner waves that maiden fantasy-fired,</l>

lines.text: All for a blond-haired youth suspiring many a singulf!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="98">All for a blond-haired youth suspiring many a singulf!</l>

lines.text: Whiles how dire was the dread she dreed in languishing heart-strings;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="99">Whiles how dire was the dread she dreed in languishing heart-strings;</l>

lines.text: How yet more, ever more, with golden splendour she paled!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="100">How yet more, ever more, with golden splendour she paled!</l>

lines.text: Whenas yearning to mate his might with the furious monster
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="101">Whenas yearning to mate his might with the furious monster</l>

lines.text: Theseus braved his death or sought the prizes of praises.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="102">Theseus braved his death or sought the prizes of praises.</l>

lines.text: Then of her gifts to gods not ingrate, nor profiting naught,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="103">Then of her gifts to gods not ingrate, nor profiting naught,</l>

lines.text: Promise with silent lip, addressed she timidly vowing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="104">Promise with silent lip, addressed she timidly vowing.</l>

lines.text: For as an oak that shakes on topmost summit of Taurus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="105">For as an oak that shakes on topmost summit of Taurus</l>

lines.text: Its boughs, or cone-growing pine from bole bark resin exuding,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="106">Its boughs, or cone-growing pine from bole bark resin exuding,</l>

lines.text: Whirlwind of passing might that twists the stems with its storm-blasts,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="107">Whirlwind of passing might that twists the stems with its storm-blasts,</l>

lines.text: Uproots, deracinates, forthright its trunk to the farthest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="108">Uproots, deracinates, forthright its trunk to the farthest,</l>

lines.text: Prone falls, shattering wide what lies in line of its downfall,—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="109">Prone falls, shattering wide what lies in line of its downfall,—</l>

lines.text: Thus was that wildling flung by Theseus and vanquisht of body,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="110">Thus was that wildling flung by Theseus and vanquisht of body,</l>

lines.text: Vainly tossing its horns and goring the wind to no purpose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="111">Vainly tossing its horns and goring the wind to no purpose.</l>

lines.text: Thence with abounding praise returned he, guiding his footsteps,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="112">Thence with abounding praise returned he, guiding his footsteps,</l>

lines.text: While a fine drawn thread checked steps in wander abounding,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="113">While a fine drawn thread checked steps in wander abounding,</l>

lines.text: Lest when issuing forth of the winding maze labyrinthine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="114">Lest when issuing forth of the winding maze labyrinthine</l>

lines.text: Baffled become his track by inobservable error.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="115">Baffled become his track by inobservable error.</l>

lines.text: But for what cause should I, from early subject digressing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="116">But for what cause should I, from early subject digressing,</l>

lines.text: Tell of the daughter who the face of her sire unseeing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="117">Tell of the daughter who the face of her sire unseeing,</l>

lines.text: Eke her sister’s embrace nor less her mother’s endearments,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="118">Eke her sister’s embrace nor less her mother’s endearments,</l>

lines.text: Who in despair bewept her hapless child that so gladly
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="119">Who in despair bewept her hapless child that so gladly</l>

lines.text: Chose before every and each the lively wooing of Theseus?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="120">Chose before every and each the lively wooing of Theseus?</l>

lines.text: Or how borne by the ship to the yeasting shore-line of Dia
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="121">Or how borne by the ship to the yeasting shore-line of Dia</l>

lines.text: Came she? or how when bound her eyes in bondage of slumber
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="122">Came she? or how when bound her eyes in bondage of slumber</l>

lines.text: Left her that chosen mate with mind unmindful departing?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="123">Left her that chosen mate with mind unmindful departing?</l>

lines.text: Often (they tell) with heart inflamed by fiery fury
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="124">Often (they tell) with heart inflamed by fiery fury</l>

lines.text: Poured she shrilling of shrieks from deepest depths of her bosom;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="125">Poured she shrilling of shrieks from deepest depths of her bosom;</l>

lines.text: Now she would sadly scale the broken faces of mountains,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="126">Now she would sadly scale the broken faces of mountains,</l>

lines.text: Whence she might overglance the boundless boiling of billows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="127">Whence she might overglance the boundless boiling of billows,</l>

lines.text: Then she wouldrush to bestem the salt-plain’s quivering wavelet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="128">Then she wouldrush to bestem the salt-plain’s quivering wavelet</l>

lines.text: And from her ankles bare the dainty garment uplifting,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="129">And from her ankles bare the dainty garment uplifting,</l>

lines.text: Spoke she these words (’tis said) from sorrow’s deepest abysses,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="130">Spoke she these words (’tis said) from sorrow’s deepest abysses,</l>

lines.text: While from her tear-drencht face outburst cold shivering sobs.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="131">While from her tear-drencht face outburst cold shivering sobs.</l>

lines.text: Thus from my patrial shore, O traitor, hurried to exile,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="132"><q rend="double">Thus from my patrial shore, O traitor, hurried to exile,</q></l>

lines.text: Me on a lonely strand hast left, perfidious Theseus?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="133"><q rend="double; merge">Me on a lonely strand hast left, perfidious Theseus?</q></l>

lines.text: Thus wise farest, despite the godhead of Deities spurned,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="134"><q rend="double; merge">Thus wise farest, despite the godhead of Deities spurned,</q></l>

lines.text: (Reckless, alas!) to your home convoying perjury-curses?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="135"><q rend="double; merge">(Reckless, alas!) to your home convoying perjury-curses?</q></l>

lines.text: Naught, then, ever availed that mind of cruelest counsel
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="136"><q rend="double; merge">Naught, then, ever availed that mind of cruelest counsel</q></l>

lines.text: Alter? No saving grace in you was evermore ready,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="137"><q rend="double; merge">Alter? No saving grace in you was evermore ready,</q></l>

lines.text: That to have pity on me vouchsafed your pitiless bosom?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="138"><q rend="double; merge">That to have pity on me vouchsafed your pitiless bosom?</q></l>

lines.text: Nevertheless not in past time such were the promises wordy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="139"><q rend="double; merge">Nevertheless not in past time such were the promises wordy</q></l>

lines.text: Lavished; nor such hopes to me the hapless were bidden;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="140"><q rend="double; merge">Lavished; nor such hopes to me the hapless were bidden;</q></l>

lines.text: But the glad married joys, the longed-for pleasures of wedlock.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="141"><q rend="double; merge">But the glad married joys, the longed-for pleasures of wedlock.</q></l>

lines.text: All now empty and vain, by breath of the breezes bescattered!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="142"><q rend="double; merge">All now empty and vain, by breath of the breezes bescattered!</q></l>

lines.text: Now, let woman no more trust her to man when he sweareth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="143"><q rend="double; merge">Now, let woman no more trust her to man when he sweareth,</q></l>

lines.text: Ne’er let her hope to find or truth or faith in his pleadings,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="144"><q rend="double; merge">Ne’er let her hope to find or truth or faith in his pleadings,</q></l>

lines.text: Who when lustful thought forelooks to somewhat attaining,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="145"><q rend="double; merge">Who when lustful thought forelooks to somewhat attaining,</q></l>

lines.text: Never an oath they fear, shall spare no promise to promise.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="146"><q rend="double; merge">Never an oath they fear, shall spare no promise to promise.</q></l>

lines.text: Yet no sooner they sate all lewdness and lecherous fancy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="147"><q rend="double; merge">Yet no sooner they sate all lewdness and lecherous fancy,</q></l>

lines.text: Nothing remember of words and reck they naught of fore-swearing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="148"><q rend="double; merge">Nothing remember of words and reck they naught of fore-swearing.</q></l>

lines.text: Certes, you did I snatch from midmost whirlpool of ruin
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="149"><q rend="double; merge">Certes, you did I snatch from midmost whirlpool of ruin</q></l>

lines.text: Deadly, and held it cheap loss of a brother to suffer
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="150"><q rend="double; merge">Deadly, and held it cheap loss of a brother to suffer</q></l>

lines.text: Rather than fail your need (O false!) at hour the supremest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="151"><q rend="double; merge">Rather than fail your need (O false!) at hour the supremest.</q></l>

lines.text: Therefore my limbs are doomed to be torn of birds, and of ferals
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="152"><q rend="double; merge">Therefore my limbs are doomed to be torn of birds, and of ferals</q></l>

lines.text: Prey, nor shall upheapt Earth afford a grave to my body.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="153"><q rend="double; merge">Prey, nor shall upheapt Earth afford a grave to my body.</q></l>

lines.text: Say me, what lioness bare you ’neath lone rock of the desert?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="154"><q rend="double; merge">Say me, what lioness bare you ’neath lone rock of the desert?</q></l>

lines.text: What sea spued you conceived from out the spume of his surges!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="155"><q rend="double; merge">What sea spued you conceived from out the spume of his surges!</q></l>

lines.text: What manner Syrt, what ravening Scylla, what vasty Charybdis?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="156"><q rend="double; merge">What manner Syrt, what ravening Scylla, what vasty Charybdis?</q></l>

lines.text: you who for sweet life saved such meeds are lief of returning!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="157"><q rend="double; merge">you who for sweet life saved such meeds are lief of returning!</q></l>

lines.text: If never willed your breast with me to mate you in marriage,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="158"><q rend="double; merge">If never willed your breast with me to mate you in marriage,</q></l>

lines.text: Hating the savage law decreed by primitive parent,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="159"><q rend="double; merge">Hating the savage law decreed by primitive parent,</q></l>

lines.text: Still of your competence ’twas within your household to home me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="160"><q rend="double; merge">Still of your competence ’twas within your household to home me,</q></l>

lines.text: Where I might serve as slave in gladsome service familiar,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="161"><q rend="double; merge">Where I might serve as slave in gladsome service familiar,</q></l>

lines.text: Laving your snow-white feet in clearest chrystalline waters
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="162"><q rend="double; merge">Laving your snow-white feet in clearest chrystalline waters</q></l>

lines.text: Or with its purpling gear your couch in company strewing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="163"><q rend="double; merge">Or with its purpling gear your couch in company strewing.</q></l>

lines.text: Yet for what cause should I complain in vain to the winds that unknow me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="164"><q rend="double; merge">Yet for what cause should I complain in vain to the winds that unknow me,</q></l>

lines.text: (I so beside me with grief!) which ne’er of senses endued
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="165"><q rend="double; merge">(I so beside me with grief!) which ne’er of senses endued</q></l>

lines.text: Hear not the words sent forth nor aught avail they to answer?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="166"><q rend="double; merge">Hear not the words sent forth nor aught avail they to answer?</q></l>

lines.text: Now be his course well-nigh engaged in midway of ocean,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="167"><q rend="double; merge">Now be his course well-nigh engaged in midway of ocean,</q></l>

lines.text: Nor any mortal shape appears in barrens of sea-wrack.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="168"><q rend="double; merge">Nor any mortal shape appears in barrens of sea-wrack.</q></l>

lines.text: Thus at the latest hour with insults over-sufficient
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="169"><q rend="double; merge">Thus at the latest hour with insults over-sufficient</q></l>

lines.text: E’en to my plaints fere Fate begrudges ears that would hear me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="170"><q rend="double; merge">E’en to my plaints fere Fate begrudges ears that would hear me.</q></l>

lines.text: Jupiter! Lord of All-might, Oh would in days that are bygone
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="171"><q rend="double; merge"><persName><surname>Jupiter</surname></persName>! Lord of All-might, Oh would in days that are bygone</q></l>

lines.text: Ne’er had Cecropian poops toucht ground at Gnossian foreshore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="172"><q rend="double; merge">Ne’er had Cecropian poops toucht ground at Gnossian foreshore,</q></l>

lines.text: Nor to the unconquered Bull that tribute direful conveying
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="173"><q rend="double; merge">Nor to the unconquered Bull that tribute direful conveying</q></l>

lines.text: Had the false Seaman bound to Cretan island his hawser,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="174"><q rend="double; merge">Had the false Seaman bound to Cretan island his hawser,</q></l>

lines.text: Nor had yon evil wight, ’neath shape the softest hard purpose
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="175"><q rend="double; merge">Nor had yon evil wight, ’neath shape the softest hard purpose</q></l>

lines.text: Hiding, enjoyed repose within our mansion beguested!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="176"><q rend="double; merge">Hiding, enjoyed repose within our mansion beguested!</q></l>

lines.text: Whither can wend I now? What hope lends help to the lost one?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="177"><q rend="double; merge">Whither can wend I now? What hope lends help to the lost one?</q></l>

lines.text: Idomenean mounts shall I scale? Ah, parted by whirlpools
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="178"><q rend="double; merge">Idomenean mounts shall I scale? Ah, parted by whirlpools</q></l>

lines.text: Widest, yon truculent main where yields it power of passage?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="179"><q rend="double; merge">Widest, yon truculent main where yields it power of passage?</q></l>

lines.text: Aid of my sire can I crave? Whom I willing abandoned,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="180"><q rend="double; merge">Aid of my sire can I crave? Whom I willing abandoned,</q></l>

lines.text: Treading in tracks of a youth bewrayed with blood of a brother!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="181"><q rend="double; merge">Treading in tracks of a youth bewrayed with blood of a brother!</q></l>

lines.text: Can I console my soul with the helpful love of a helpmate
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="182"><q rend="double; merge">Can I console my soul with the helpful love of a helpmate</q></l>

lines.text: Who flies me with pliant oars, flies overbounding the sea-depths?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="183"><q rend="double; merge">Who flies me with pliant oars, flies overbounding the sea-depths?</q></l>

lines.text: Nay, if this Coast I quit, this lone isle lends me no roof-tree,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="184"><q rend="double; merge">Nay, if this Coast I quit, this lone isle lends me no roof-tree,</q></l>

lines.text: Nor aught issue allows begirt by billows of Ocean:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="185"><q rend="double; merge">Nor aught issue allows begirt by billows of Ocean:</q></l>

lines.text: Nowhere is path for flight: none hope shows: all things are silent:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="186"><q rend="double; merge">Nowhere is path for flight: none hope shows: all things are silent:</q></l>

lines.text: All be a desolate waste: all makes display of destruction.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="187"><q rend="double; merge">All be a desolate waste: all makes display of destruction.</q></l>

lines.text: Yet never close these eyes in latest languor of dying,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="188"><q rend="double; merge">Yet never close these eyes in latest languor of dying,</q></l>

lines.text: Ne’er from my wearied frame go forth slow-ebbing my senses,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="189"><q rend="double; merge">Ne’er from my wearied frame go forth slow-ebbing my senses,</q></l>

lines.text: Ere from the Gods just doom implore I, treason-betrayed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="190"><q rend="double; merge">Ere from the Gods just doom implore I, treason-betrayed,</q></l>

lines.text: And with my breath supreme firm faith of Celestials invoke I.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="191"><q rend="double; merge">And with my breath supreme firm faith of Celestials invoke I.</q></l>

lines.text: Therefore, O you who ’venge man’s deed with penalties direful,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="192"><q rend="double; merge">Therefore, O you who ’venge man’s deed with penalties direful,</q></l>

lines.text: Eumenides! aye wont to bind with viperous hairlocks
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="193"><q rend="double; merge">Eumenides! aye wont to bind with viperous hairlocks</q></l>

lines.text: Foreheads,—Oh, deign outspeak fierce wrath from bosom outbreathing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="194"><q rend="double; merge">Foreheads,—Oh, deign outspeak fierce wrath from bosom outbreathing,</q></l>

lines.text: Hither, Oh hither, speed, and lend you all ear to my grievance,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="195"><q rend="double; merge">Hither, Oh hither, speed, and lend you all ear to my grievance,</q></l>

lines.text: Which now sad I (alas!) outpour from innermost vitals
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="196"><q rend="double; merge">Which now sad I (alas!) outpour from innermost vitals</q></l>

lines.text: Maugre my will, sans help, blind, fired with furious madness.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="197"><q rend="double; merge">Maugre my will, sans help, blind, fired with furious madness.</q></l>

lines.text: And, as indeed all spring from veriest core of my bosom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="198"><q rend="double; merge">And, as indeed all spring from veriest core of my bosom,</q></l>

lines.text: Suffer you not the cause of grief and woe to evanish;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="199"><q rend="double; merge">Suffer you not the cause of grief and woe to evanish;</q></l>

lines.text: But with the Will wherewith could Theseus leave me in loneness,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="200"><q rend="double; merge">But with the Will wherewith could Theseus leave me in loneness,</q></l>

lines.text: Goddesses! bid that Will lead him, lead his, to destruction.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="201"><q rend="double; merge">Goddesses! bid that Will lead him, lead his, to destruction.</q></l>

lines.text: E’en as she thus poured forth these words from anguish of bosom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="202">E’en as she thus poured forth these words from anguish of bosom,</l>

lines.text: And for this cruel deed, distracted, sued she for vengeance,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="203">And for this cruel deed, distracted, sued she for vengeance,</l>

lines.text: Nodded the Ruler of Gods Celestial, matchless of All-might,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="204">Nodded the Ruler of Gods Celestial, matchless of All-might,</l>

lines.text: When at the gest earth-plain and horrid spaces of ocean
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="205">When at the gest earth-plain and horrid spaces of ocean</l>

lines.text: Trembled, and every sphere rockt stars and planets resplendent.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="206">Trembled, and every sphere rockt stars and planets resplendent.</l>

lines.text: Meanwhile Theseus himself, obscured in blindness of darkness
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="207">Meanwhile Theseus himself, obscured in blindness of darkness</l>

lines.text: As to his mind, dismiss’d from breast oblivious all things
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="208">As to his mind, dismiss’d from breast oblivious all things</l>

lines.text: Erewhile enjoined and held hereto in memory constant,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="209">Erewhile enjoined and held hereto in memory constant,</l>

lines.text: Nor for his saddened sire the gladness-signals uphoisting
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="210">Nor for his saddened sire the gladness-signals uphoisting</l>

lines.text: Heralded safe return within sight of the Erechthean harbour.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="211">Heralded safe return within sight of the Erechthean harbour.</l>

lines.text: For ’twas told of yore, when from walls of the Virginal Deess
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="212">For ’twas told of yore, when from walls of the Virginal Deess</l>

lines.text: Aegeus speeding his son, to the care of breezes committed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="213">Aegeus speeding his son, to the care of breezes committed,</l>

lines.text: Thus with a last embrace to the youth spoke words of commandment:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="214">Thus with a last embrace to the youth spoke words of commandment:</l>

lines.text: Son! far nearer my heart (you alone) than life of the longest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="215"><q rend="double">Son! far nearer my heart (you alone) than life of the longest,</q></l>

lines.text: Son, I perforce dismiss to doubtful, dangerous chances,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="216"><q rend="double; merge">Son, I perforce dismiss to doubtful, dangerous chances,</q></l>

lines.text: Lately restored to me when eld draws nearest his ending,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="217"><q rend="double; merge">Lately restored to me when eld draws nearest his ending,</q></l>

lines.text: Since such fortune in me, and in you such boiling of valour
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="218"><q rend="double; merge">Since such fortune in me, and in you such boiling of valour</q></l>

lines.text: Tear you away from me so loath, whose eyes in their languor
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="219"><q rend="double; merge">Tear you away from me so loath, whose eyes in their languor</q></l>

lines.text: Never are sated with sight of my son, all-dearest of figures.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="220"><q rend="double; merge">Never are sated with sight of my son, all-dearest of figures.</q></l>

lines.text: Nor will I send you forth with joy that gladdens my bosom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="221"><q rend="double; merge">Nor will I send you forth with joy that gladdens my bosom,</q></l>

lines.text: Nor will I suffer you show boon signs of favouring Fortune,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="222"><q rend="double; merge">Nor will I suffer you show boon signs of favouring Fortune,</q></l>

lines.text: But from my soul I’ll first express an issue of sorrow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="223"><q rend="double; merge">But from my soul I’ll first express an issue of sorrow,</q></l>

lines.text: Soiling my hoary hairs with dust and ashes commingled;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="224"><q rend="double; merge">Soiling my hoary hairs with dust and ashes commingled;</q></l>

lines.text: Then will I hang stained sails fast-made to the wavering yard-arms,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="225"><q rend="double; merge">Then will I hang stained sails fast-made to the wavering yard-arms,</q></l>

lines.text: So shall our mourning thought and burning torture of spirit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="226"><q rend="double; merge">So shall our mourning thought and burning torture of spirit</q></l>

lines.text: Show by the dark sombre-dye of Iberian canvas spread.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="227"><q rend="double; merge">Show by the dark sombre-dye of Iberian canvas spread.</q></l>

lines.text: But, grant me the grace Who dwells in Sacred Itone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="228"><q rend="double; merge">But, grant me the grace Who dwells in Sacred Itone,</q></l>

lines.text: (And our issue to guard and ward the seats of Erechtheus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="229"><q rend="double; merge">(And our issue to guard and ward the seats of Erechtheus</q></l>

lines.text: Sware She) that if your right is besprent with blood of the Man-Bull,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="230"><q rend="double; merge">Sware She) that if your right is besprent with blood of the Man-Bull,</q></l>

lines.text: Then do you so-wise act, and stored in memory’s heart-core
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="231"><q rend="double; merge">Then do you so-wise act, and stored in memory’s heart-core</q></l>

lines.text: Dwell these mandates of me, no time their traces untracing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="232"><q rend="double; merge">Dwell these mandates of me, no time their traces untracing.</q></l>

lines.text: Dip, when first shall arise our hills to gladden your eye-glance,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="233"><q rend="double; merge">Dip, when first shall arise our hills to gladden your eye-glance,</q></l>

lines.text: Down from your every mast the ill-omened vestments of mourning,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="234"><q rend="double; merge">Down from your every mast the ill-omened vestments of mourning,</q></l>

lines.text: Then let the twisten ropes upheave the whitest of canvas,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="235"><q rend="double; merge">Then let the twisten ropes upheave the whitest of canvas,</q></l>

lines.text: Wherewith splendid shall gleam the tallest spars of the top-mast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="235a"><q rend="double; merge">Wherewith splendid shall gleam the tallest spars of the top-mast,</q></l>

lines.text: These seeing sans delay with joy exalting my spirit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="236"><q rend="double; merge">These seeing sans delay with joy exalting my spirit</q></l>

lines.text: Well shall I wot boon Time sets you returning before me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="237"><q rend="double; merge">Well shall I wot boon Time sets you returning before me.</q></l>

lines.text: Such were the mandates which stored at first in memory constant
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="238">Such were the mandates which stored at first in memory constant</l>

lines.text: Faded from Theseus’ mind like mists, compelled by the whirlwind,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="239">Faded from Theseus’ mind like mists, compelled by the whirlwind,</l>

lines.text: Fleet from aerial crests of mountains hoary with snow-drifts.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="240">Fleet from aerial crests of mountains hoary with snow-drifts.</l>

lines.text: But as the sire had sought the citadel’s summit for outlook,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="241">But as the sire had sought the citadel’s summit for outlook,</l>

lines.text: Wasting his anxious eyes with tear-floods evermore flowing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="242">Wasting his anxious eyes with tear-floods evermore flowing,</l>

lines.text: Forthright e’en as he saw the sail-gear darkened with dye-stain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="243">Forthright e’en as he saw the sail-gear darkened with dye-stain,</l>

lines.text: Headlong himself flung he from the sea-cliff’s pinnacled summit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="244">Headlong himself flung he from the sea-cliff’s pinnacled summit</l>

lines.text: Holding his Theseus lost by doom of pitiless Fortune.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="245">Holding his Theseus lost by doom of pitiless Fortune.</l>

lines.text: Thus as he came to the home funest, his roof-tree paternal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="246">Thus as he came to the home funest, his roof-tree paternal,</l>

lines.text: Theseus (vaunting the death), what dule to the maiden of Minos
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="247">Theseus (vaunting the death), what dule to the maiden of Minos</l>

lines.text: Dealt with unminding mind so dree’d he similar dolour.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="248">Dealt with unminding mind so dree’d he similar dolour.</l>

lines.text: She too gazing in grief at the kelson vanishing slowly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="249">She too gazing in grief at the kelson vanishing slowly,</l>

lines.text: Self-wrapt, manifold cares revolved in spirit perturbed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="250">Self-wrapt, manifold cares revolved in spirit perturbed.</l>

lines.text: But from the further side came flitting bright-faced Iacchus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="251">But from the further side came flitting bright-faced Iacchus</l>

lines.text: Girded by Satyr-crew and Nysa-reared Sileni
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="252">Girded by Satyr-crew and Nysa-reared Sileni</l>

lines.text: Burning with love unto thee (Ariadne!) and greeting thy presence.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="253">Burning with love unto thee (Ariadne!) and greeting thy presence.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="253a"><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Who flocking eager to fray did rave with infuriate spirit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="254">Who flocking eager to fray did rave with infuriate spirit,</l>

lines.text: Evoe frenzying loud, with heads at Evoe rolling.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="255"><q rend="double">Evoe</q> frenzying loud, with heads at <q rend="double">Evoe</q> rolling.</l>

lines.text: Brandisht some of the maids their thyrsi sheathed of spear-point,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="256">Brandisht some of the maids their thyrsi sheathed of spear-point,</l>

lines.text: Some snatcht limbs and joints of sturlings rended to pieces,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="257">Some snatcht limbs and joints of sturlings rended to pieces,</l>

lines.text: These girt necks and waists with writhing bodies of vipers,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="258">These girt necks and waists with writhing bodies of vipers,</l>

lines.text: Those with the gear enwombed in crates dark orgies ordained—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="259">Those with the gear enwombed in crates dark orgies ordained—</l>

lines.text: Orgies that ears profane must vainly lust for o’er hearing—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="260">Orgies that ears profane must vainly lust for o’er hearing—</l>

lines.text: Others with palms on high smote hurried strokes on the cymbal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="261">Others with palms on high smote hurried strokes on the cymbal,</l>

lines.text: Or from the polisht brass woke thin-toned tinkling music,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="262">Or from the polisht brass woke thin-toned tinkling music,</l>

lines.text: While from the many there boomed and blared hoarse blast of the horn-trump,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="263">While from the many there boomed and blared hoarse blast of the horn-trump,</l>

lines.text: And with its horrid skirl loud shrilled the barbarous bag-pipe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="264">And with its horrid skirl loud shrilled the barbarous bag-pipe</l>

lines.text: Showing such varied forms, that richly-decorated couch-cloth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="265">Showing such varied forms, that richly-decorated couch-cloth</l>

lines.text: Folded in strait embrace the bedding drapery-veiled.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="266">Folded in strait embrace the bedding drapery-veiled.</l>

lines.text: This when the Thessalan youths had eyed with eager inspection
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="267">This when the Thessalan youths had eyed with eager inspection</l>

lines.text: Fulfilled, place they began to provide for venerate Godheads,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="268">Fulfilled, place they began to provide for venerate Godheads,</l>

lines.text: Even as Zephyrus’ breath, seas couching placid at dawn-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="269">Even as Zephyrus’ breath, seas couching placid at dawn-tide,</l>

lines.text: Roughens, then stings and spurs the wavelets slantingly fretted—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="270">Roughens, then stings and spurs the wavelets slantingly fretted—</l>

lines.text: Rising Aurora the while ’neath Sol the wanderer’s threshold—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="271">Rising Aurora the while ’neath Sol the wanderer’s threshold—</l>

lines.text: Tardy at first they flow by the clement breathing of breezes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="272">Tardy at first they flow by the clement breathing of breezes</l>

lines.text: Urged, and echo the shores with soft-toned ripples of laughter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="273">Urged, and echo the shores with soft-toned ripples of laughter,</l>

lines.text: But as the winds wax high so waves wax higher and higher,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="274">But as the winds wax high so waves wax higher and higher,</l>

lines.text: Flashing and floating afar to outswim morn’s purpurine splendours,—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="275">Flashing and floating afar to outswim morn’s purpurine splendours,—</l>

lines.text: So did the crowd fare forth, the royal vestibule leaving,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="276">So did the crowd fare forth, the royal vestibule leaving,</l>

lines.text: And to their house each wight with vaguing paces departed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="277">And to their house each wight with vaguing paces departed.</l>

lines.text: After their wending, the first, foremost from Pelion’s summit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="278">After their wending, the first, foremost from <placeName key="tgn,2096449">Pelion</placeName>’s summit,</l>

lines.text: Chiron came to the front with woodland presents surcharged:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="279">Chiron came to the front with woodland presents surcharged:</l>

lines.text: Whatso of blooms and flowers bring forth Thessalian uplands
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="280">Whatso of blooms and flowers bring forth Thessalian uplands</l>

lines.text: Mighty with mountain crests, whate’er of riverine lea flowers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="281">Mighty with mountain crests, whate’er of riverine lea flowers</l>

lines.text: Reareth Favonius’ air, bud-breeding, tepidly breathing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="282">Reareth Favonius’ air, bud-breeding, tepidly breathing,</l>

lines.text: All in his hands brought he, unseparate in woven garlands,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="283">All in his hands brought he, unseparate in woven garlands,</l>

lines.text: Whereat laughed the house as soothed by pleasure of perfume.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="284">Whereat laughed the house as soothed by pleasure of perfume.</l>

lines.text: Presently Péneus appears, deserting verdurous Tempe—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="285">Presently Péneus appears, deserting verdurous <placeName key="tgn,7014367">Tempe</placeName>—</l>

lines.text: Tempe girt by her belts of greenwood ever impending,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="286"><placeName key="tgn,7014367">Tempe</placeName> girt by her belts of greenwood ever impending,</l>

lines.text: Left for the Mamonides with frequent dances to worship—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="287">Left for the Mamonides with frequent dances to worship—</l>

lines.text: Nor is he empty of hand, for bears he tallest of beeches
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="288">Nor is he empty of hand, for bears he tallest of beeches</l>

lines.text: Deracinate, and bays with straight boles lofty and stately,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="289">Deracinate, and bays with straight boles lofty and stately,</l>

lines.text: Not without nodding plane-tree nor less the flexible sister
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="290">Not without nodding plane-tree nor less the flexible sister</l>

lines.text: Fire-slain Phaëton left, and not without cypresses airy.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="291">Fire-slain Phaëton left, and not without cypresses airy.</l>

lines.text: These in a line wide-broke set he, the Mansion surrounding,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="292">These in a line wide-broke set he, the Mansion surrounding,</l>

lines.text: So by the soft leaves screened, the porch might flourish in verdure.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="293">So by the soft leaves screened, the porch might flourish in verdure.</l>

lines.text: Follows hard on his track with active spirit Prometheus,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="294">Follows hard on his track with active spirit Prometheus,</l>

lines.text: Bearing extenuate sign of penalties suffer’d in by-gones.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="295">Bearing extenuate sign of penalties suffer’d in by-gones.</l>

lines.text: Paid erewhiles what time fast-bound as to every member,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="296">Paid erewhiles what time fast-bound as to every member,</l>

lines.text: Hung he in carkanet slung from the Scythian rocktor.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="297">Hung he in carkanet slung from the Scythian rocktor.</l>

lines.text: Last did the Father of Gods with his sacred spouse and his offspring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="298">Last did the Father of Gods with his sacred spouse and his offspring,</l>

lines.text: Proud from the Heavens proceed, thee leaving (Phoebus) in loneness,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="299">Proud from the Heavens proceed, thee leaving (Phoebus) in loneness,</l>

lines.text: Lone wi’ thy sister twin who haunteth mountains of Idrus:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="300">Lone wi’ thy sister twin who haunteth mountains of Idrus:</l>

lines.text: For that the Virgin spurned as thou the person of Peleus,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="301">For that the Virgin spurned as thou the person of Peleus,</l>

lines.text: Nor Thetis’ nuptial torch would greet by act of her presence.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="302">Nor Thetis’ nuptial torch would greet by act of her presence.</l>

lines.text: When they had leaned their limbs upon snowy benches reposing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="303">When they had leaned their limbs upon snowy benches reposing,</l>

lines.text: Tables largely arranged with various viands were garnisht.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="304">Tables largely arranged with various viands were garnisht.</l>

lines.text: But, ere opened the feast, with infirm gesture their semblance
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="305">But, ere opened the feast, with infirm gesture their semblance</l>

lines.text: Shaking, the Parcae fell to chaunting veridique verses.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="306">Shaking, the Parcae fell to chaunting veridique verses.</l>

lines.text: Robed were their tremulous frames all o’er in muffle of garments
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="307">Robed were their tremulous frames all o’er in muffle of garments</l>

lines.text: Bright-white, purple of hem enfolding heels in its edges;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="308">Bright-white, purple of hem enfolding heels in its edges;</l>

lines.text: Snowy the fillets that bound heads aged by many a year-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="309">Snowy the fillets that bound heads aged by many a year-tide,</l>

lines.text: And, as their wont aye was, their hands plied labour unceasing.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="310">And, as their wont aye was, their hands plied labour unceasing.</l>

lines.text: Each in her left upheld with soft fleece clothed a distaff,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="311">Each in her left upheld with soft fleece clothed a distaff,</l>

lines.text: Then did the right that drew forth thread with upturn of fingers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="312">Then did the right that drew forth thread with upturn of fingers</l>

lines.text: Gently fashion the yarn which deftly twisted by thumb-ball
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="313">Gently fashion the yarn which deftly twisted by thumb-ball</l>

lines.text: Speeded the spindle poised by thread-whorl perfect of polish;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="314">Speeded the spindle poised by thread-whorl perfect of polish;</l>

lines.text: Thus as the work was wrought, the lengths were trimmed wi’ the fore-teeth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="315">Thus as the work was wrought, the lengths were trimmed wi’ the fore-teeth,</l>

lines.text: While to their thin, dry lips stuck wool-flecks severed by biting,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="316">While to their thin, dry lips stuck wool-flecks severed by biting,</l>

lines.text: Which at the first outstood from yarn-hanks evenly fine-drawn.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="317">Which at the first outstood from yarn-hanks evenly fine-drawn.</l>

lines.text: Still at their feet in front soft fleece-flecks white as the snow-flake
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="318">Still at their feet in front soft fleece-flecks white as the snow-flake</l>

lines.text: Lay in the trusty guard of wickers woven in withies.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="319">Lay in the trusty guard of wickers woven in withies.</l>

lines.text: Always a-carding the wool, with clear-toned voices resounding
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="320">Always a-carding the wool, with clear-toned voices resounding</l>

lines.text: Told they such lots as these in song divinely directed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="321">Told they such lots as these in song divinely directed,</l>

lines.text: Chaunts which none after-time shall ’stablish falsehood-convicted.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="322">Chaunts which none after-time shall ’stablish falsehood-convicted.</l>

lines.text: O who by virtues great all highmosthonours enhancest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="323">O who by virtues great all highmosthonours enhancest,</l>

lines.text: Guard of Emáthia-land, most famous made by thine offspring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="324">Guard of Emáthia-land, most famous made by thine offspring,</l>

lines.text: Take what the Sisters deign this gladsome day to disclose thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="325">Take what the Sisters deign this gladsome day to disclose thee,</l>

lines.text: Oracles soothfast told,—And ye, by Destiny followed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="326">Oracles soothfast told,—And ye, by Destiny followed,</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="327">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Soon to thy sight shall rise, their fond hopes bringing to bridegrooms,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="328">Soon to thy sight shall rise, their fond hopes bringing to bridegrooms,</l>

lines.text: Hesperus: soon shall come thy spouse with planet auspicious,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="329"><persName><surname>Hesperus</surname></persName>: soon shall come thy spouse with planet auspicious,</l>

lines.text: Who shall thy mind enbathe with a love that softens the spirit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="330">Who shall thy mind enbathe with a love that softens the spirit,</l>

lines.text: And as thyself shall prepare for sinking in languorous slumber,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="331">And as thyself shall prepare for sinking in languorous slumber,</l>

lines.text: Under thy neck robust, soft arms dispreading as pillow.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="332">Under thy neck robust, soft arms dispreading as pillow.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="333">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Never a house like this such loves as these hath united,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="334">Never a house like this such loves as these hath united,</l>

lines.text: Never did love conjoin by such-like covenant lovers,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="335">Never did love conjoin by such-like covenant lovers,</l>

lines.text: As th’according tie Thetis deigned in concert wi’ Peleus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="336">As th’according tie Thetis deigned in concert wi’ Peleus.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="337">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Born of yon twain shall come Achilles guiltless of fear-sense,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="338">Born of yon twain shall come Achilles guiltless of fear-sense,</l>

lines.text: Known by his forceful breast and ne’er by back to the foeman,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="339">Known by his forceful breast and ne’er by back to the foeman,</l>

lines.text: Who shall at times full oft in doubtful contest of race-course
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="340">Who shall at times full oft in doubtful contest of race-course</l>

lines.text: Conquer the fleet-foot doe with slot-tracks smoking and burning.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="341">Conquer the fleet-foot doe with slot-tracks smoking and burning.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="342">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: None shall with him compare, howe’er war-doughty a hero,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="343">None shall with him compare, howe’er war-doughty a hero,</l>

lines.text: Whenas the Phrygian rills flow deep with bloodshed of Teucer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="344">Whenas the Phrygian rills flow deep with bloodshed of Teucer,</l>

lines.text: And beleaguering the walls of Troy with longest of warfare
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="345">And beleaguering the walls of <placeName key="tgn,7014164">Troy</placeName> with longest of warfare</l>

lines.text: He shall the works lay low, third heir of Pelops the perjured.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="346">He shall the works lay low, third heir of Pelops the perjured.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="347">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: His be the derring-do and deeds of valour egregious,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="348">His be the derring-do and deeds of valour egregious,</l>

lines.text: Often mothers shall own at funeral-rites of their children,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="349">Often mothers shall own at funeral-rites of their children,</l>

lines.text: What time their hoary hairs from head in ashes are loosened,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="350">What time their hoary hairs from head in ashes are loosened,</l>

lines.text: And wi’ their hands infirm thay smite their bosoms loose duggèd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="351">And wi’ their hands infirm thay smite their bosoms loose duggèd.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="352">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: For as the toiling hind bestrewing denseness of corn-stalks
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="353">For as the toiling hind bestrewing denseness of corn-stalks</l>

lines.text: Under the broiling sun mows grain-fields yellow to harvest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="354">Under the broiling sun mows grain-fields yellow to harvest,</l>

lines.text: So shall his baneful brand strew earth with corpses of Troy-born.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="355">So shall his baneful brand strew earth with corpses of Troy-born.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="356">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Aye to his valorous worth attest shall wave of Scamander
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="357">Aye to his valorous worth attest shall wave of Scamander</l>

lines.text: Which unto Hellè-Sea fast flowing ever dischargeth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="358">Which unto Hellè-Sea fast flowing ever dischargeth,</l>

lines.text: Straiter whose course shall grow by up-heaped barrage of corpses,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="359">Straiter whose course shall grow by up-heaped barrage of corpses,</l>

lines.text: While in his depths runs warm his stream with slaughter commingled.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="360">While in his depths runs warm his stream with slaughter commingled.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="361">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Witness in fine shall be the victim rendered to death-stroke,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="362">Witness in fine shall be the victim rendered to death-stroke,</l>

lines.text: Whenas the earthern tomb on lofty tumulus builded
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="363">Whenas the earthern tomb on lofty tumulus builded</l>

lines.text: Shall of the stricken maid receive limbs white as the snow-flake.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="364">Shall of the stricken maid receive limbs white as the snow-flake.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="365">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: For when at last shall Fors to weary Achaians her fiat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="366">For when at last shall Fors to weary Achaians her fiat</l>

lines.text: Deal, of Dardanus-town to burst Neptunian fetters,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="367">Deal, of Dardanus-town to burst Neptunian fetters,</l>

lines.text: Then shall the high-reared tomb stand bathed with Polyxena’s life-blood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="368">Then shall the high-reared tomb stand bathed with Polyxena’s life-blood,</l>

lines.text: Who, as the victim doomed to fall by the double-edged falchion,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="369">Who, as the victim doomed to fall by the double-edged falchion,</l>

lines.text: Forward wi’ hams relaxt shall smite a body beheaded.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="370">Forward wi’ hams relaxt shall smite a body beheaded.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="371">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Wherefore arise, ye pair, conjoin loves ardently longed-for,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="372">Wherefore arise, ye pair, conjoin loves ardently longed-for,</l>

lines.text: Now doth the groom receive with happiest omen his goddess,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="373">Now doth the groom receive with happiest omen his goddess,</l>

lines.text: Now let the bride at length to her yearning spouse be delivered.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="374">Now let the bride at length to her yearning spouse be delivered.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="375">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Neither the nurse who comes at dawn to visit her nursling
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="376">Neither the nurse who comes at dawn to visit her nursling</l>

lines.text: E’er shall avail her neck to begird with yesterday’s ribband.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="377">E’er shall avail her neck to begird with yesterday’s ribband.</l>

lines.text: [Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O spindles.]
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="378">[Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O spindles.]</l>

lines.text: Nor shall the mother’s soul for ill-matcht daughter a-grieving
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="379">Nor shall the mother’s soul for ill-matcht daughter a-grieving</l>

lines.text: Lose by a parted couch all hopes of favourite grandsons.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="380">Lose by a parted couch all hopes of favourite grandsons.</l>

lines.text: Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="381">Speed ye, the well-spun woof out-drawing, speed ye, O Spindles.</l>

lines.text: Thus in the bygone day Peleus’ fate foretelling
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="382">Thus in the bygone day Peleus’ fate foretelling</l>

lines.text: Chaunted from breasts divine prophetic verse the Parcae.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="383">Chaunted from breasts divine prophetic verse the Parcae.</l>

lines.text: For that the pure chaste homes of heroes to visit in person
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="384">For that the pure chaste homes of heroes to visit in person</l>

lines.text: Oft-tide the Gods, and themselves to display where mortals were gathered,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="385">Oft-tide the Gods, and themselves to display where mortals were gathered,</l>

lines.text: Wont were the Heavenlies while none human piety spurned.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="386">Wont were the Heavenlies while none human piety spurned.</l>

lines.text: Often the Deities’ Sire, in fulgent temple a-dwelling,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="387">Often the Deities’ Sire, in fulgent temple a-dwelling,</l>

lines.text: Whenas in festal days received he his annual worship,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="388">Whenas in festal days received he his annual worship,</l>

lines.text: Looked upon hundreds of bulls felled prone on pavement before him.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="389">Looked upon hundreds of bulls felled prone on pavement before him.</l>

lines.text: Full oft Liber who roamed from topmost peak of Parnassus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="390">Full oft Liber who roamed from topmost peak of <placeName key="tgn,2113566">Parnassus</placeName></l>

lines.text: Hunted his howling host, his Thyiads with tresses dishevelled.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="391">Hunted his howling host, his Thyiads with tresses dishevelled.</l>

lines.text: Then with contending troops from all their city outflocking
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="392">Then with contending troops from all their city outflocking</l>

lines.text: Gladly the Delphians hailed their God with smoking of altars.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="393">Gladly the Delphians hailed their God with smoking of altars.</l>
