lines.text: Often in death-full war and bravest of battle, or Mavors
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="394">Often in death-full war and bravest of battle, or Mavors</l>

lines.text: Or rapid Triton’s Queen or eke the Virgin Rhamnusian,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="395">Or rapid Triton’s Queen or eke the Virgin Rhamnusian,</l>

lines.text: Bevies of weaponed men exhorting, proved their presence.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="396">Bevies of weaponed men exhorting, proved their presence.</l>

lines.text: But from the time when earth was stained with unspeakable scandals
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="397">But from the time when earth was stained with unspeakable scandals</l>

lines.text: And forth fro’ greeding breasts of all men justice departed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="398">And forth fro’ greeding breasts of all men justice departed,</l>

lines.text: Then did the brother drench his hands in brotherly bloodshed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="399">Then did the brother drench his hands in brotherly bloodshed,</l>

lines.text: Stinted the son in heart to mourn decease of his parents,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="400">Stinted the son in heart to mourn decease of his parents,</l>

lines.text: Longèd the sire to sight his first-born’s funeral convoy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="401">Longèd the sire to sight his first-born’s funeral convoy</l>

lines.text: So more freely the flower of step-dame-maiden to rifle;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="402">So more freely the flower of step-dame-maiden to rifle;</l>

lines.text: After that impious Queen her guiltless son underlying,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="403">After that impious Queen her guiltless son underlying,</l>

lines.text: Impious, the household gods with crime ne’er dreading to sully—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="404">Impious, the household gods with crime ne’er dreading to sully—</l>

lines.text: All things fair and nefand being mixt in fury of evil
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="405">All things fair and nefand being mixt in fury of evil</l>

lines.text: Turned from ourselves avert the great goodwill of the Godheads.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="406">Turned from ourselves avert the great goodwill of the Godheads.</l>

lines.text: Wherefor they nowise deign our human assemblies to visit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="407">Wherefor they nowise deign our human assemblies to visit,</l>

lines.text: Nor do they suffer themselves be met in light of the day-tide.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:64" n="408">Nor do they suffer themselves be met in light of the day-tide.</l>

head: TO HORTALUS LAMENTING A LOST BROTHER.

lines.text: Albeit care that consumes, with dule assiduous grieving,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="1">Albeit care that consumes, with dule assiduous grieving,</l>

lines.text: Me from the Learnèd Maids (Hortalus!) ever seclude,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="2">Me from the Learnèd Maids (Hortalus!) ever seclude,</l>

lines.text: Nor can avail sweet births of the Muses thou to deliver
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="3">Nor can avail sweet births of the Muses thou to deliver</l>

lines.text: Thought o’ my mind; (so much floats it on flooding of ills:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="4">Thought o’ my mind; (so much floats it on flooding of ills:</l>

lines.text: For that the Lethe-wave upsurging of late from abysses,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="5">For that the Lethe-wave upsurging of late from abysses,</l>

lines.text: Lavèd my brother’s foot, paling with pallor of death,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="6">Lavèd my brother’s foot, paling with pallor of death,</l>

lines.text: He whom the Trojan soil, Rhoetean shore underlying,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="7">He whom the Trojan soil, Rhoetean shore underlying, </l>

lines.text: Buries for ever and aye, forcibly snatched from our sight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="8">Buries for ever and aye, forcibly snatched from our sight.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="8a"><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: I can address; no more shall I hear thee tell of thy doings,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="9">I can address; no more shall I hear thee tell of thy doings,</l>

lines.text: Say, shall I never again, brother all liefer than life,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="10">Say, shall I never again, brother all liefer than life,</l>

lines.text: Sight thee henceforth? But I will surely love thee for ever
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="11">Sight thee henceforth? But I will surely love thee for ever</l>

lines.text: Ever what songs I sing saddened shall be by thy death;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="12">Ever what songs I sing saddened shall be by thy death;</l>

lines.text: Such as the Daulian bird ’neath gloom of shadowy frondage
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="13">Such as the Daulian bird ’neath gloom of shadowy frondage</l>

lines.text: Warbles, of Itys lost ever bemoaning the lot.)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="14">Warbles, of Itys lost ever bemoaning the lot.)</l>

lines.text: Yet amid grief so great to thee, my Hortalus, send I
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="15">Yet amid grief so great to thee, my Hortalus, send I</l>

lines.text: These strains sung to a mode borrowed from Battiades;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="16">These strains sung to a mode borrowed from Battiades;</l>

lines.text: Lest shouldest weet of me thy words, to wandering wind-gusts
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="17">Lest shouldest weet of me thy words, to wandering wind-gusts</l>

lines.text: Vainly committed, perchance forth of my memory flowed—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="18">Vainly committed, perchance forth of my memory flowed— </l>

lines.text: As did that apple sent for a furtive giftie by wooer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="19">As did that apple sent for a furtive giftie by wooer,</l>

lines.text: In the chaste breast of the Maid hidden a-sudden out-sprang;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="20">In the chaste breast of the Maid hidden a-sudden out-sprang;</l>

lines.text: For did the hapless forget when in loose-girt garment it lurkèd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="21">For did the hapless forget when in loose-girt garment it lurkèd,</l>

lines.text: Forth would it leap as she rose, scared by her mother’s approach,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="22">Forth would it leap as she rose, scared by her mother’s approach,</l>

lines.text: And while coursing headlong, it rolls far out of her keeping,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="23">And while coursing headlong, it rolls far out of her keeping,</l>

lines.text: O’er the triste virgin’s brow flushes the conscious blush.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:65" n="24">O’er the triste virgin’s brow flushes the conscious blush.</l>

lines.text: He who every light of the sky world’s vastness inspected,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="1">He who every light of the sky world’s vastness inspected,</l>

lines.text: He who mastered in mind risings and settings of stars,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="2">He who mastered in mind risings and settings of stars,</l>

lines.text: How of the fast rising sun obscured be the fiery splendours,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="3">How of the fast rising sun obscured be the fiery splendours,</l>

lines.text: How at the seasons assured vanish the planets from view,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="4">How at the seasons assured vanish the planets from view,</l>

lines.text: How Diana to lurk thief-like ’neath Latmian stone-fields,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="5">How <placeName key="tgn,2118015">Diana</placeName> to lurk thief-like ’neath Latmian stone-fields,</l>

lines.text: Summoned by sweetness of Love, comes from her aëry gyre;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="6">Summoned by sweetness of Love, comes from her aëry gyre;</l>

lines.text: That same Cónon espied among lights Celestial shining
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="7">That same Cónon espied among lights Celestial shining</l>

lines.text: Me, Berenice’s Hair, which, from her glorious head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="8">Me, Berenice’s Hair, which, from her glorious head, </l>

lines.text: Fulgent in brightness afar, to many a host of the Godheads
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="9">Fulgent in brightness afar, to many a host of the Godheads</l>

lines.text: Stretching her soft smooth arms she vowed to devoutly bestow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="10">Stretching her soft smooth arms she vowed to devoutly bestow,</l>

lines.text: What time strengthened by joy of new-made wedlock the monarch
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="11">What time strengthened by joy of new-made wedlock the monarch</l>

lines.text: Bounds of Assyrian land hurried to plunder and pill;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="12">Bounds of Assyrian land hurried to plunder and pill;</l>

lines.text: Bearing of nightly strife new signs and traces delicious,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="13">Bearing of nightly strife new signs and traces delicious,</l>

lines.text: Won in the war he waged virginal trophies to win.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="14">Won in the war he waged virginal trophies to win. </l>

lines.text: Loathsome is Venus to all new-paired? Else why be the parents’
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="15">Loathsome is <persName><surname>Venus</surname></persName> to all new-paired? Else why be the parents’</l>

lines.text: Pleasure frustrated aye by the false flow of tears
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="16">Pleasure frustrated aye by the false flow of tears </l>

lines.text: Poured in profusion amid illuminate genial chamber?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="17">Poured in profusion amid illuminate genial chamber?</l>

lines.text: Nay not real the ’groans; ever so help me the Gods!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="18">Nay not real the ’groans; ever so help me the Gods!</l>

lines.text: This truth taught me my Queen by force of manifold ’plainings
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="19">This truth taught me my Queen by force of manifold ’plainings</l>

lines.text: After her new groom hied facing the fierceness of fight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="20">After her new groom hied facing the fierceness of fight.</l>

lines.text: Yet so thou mournedst not for a bed deserted of husband,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="21">Yet so thou mournedst not for a bed deserted of husband,</l>

lines.text: As for a brother beloved wending on woefullest way?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="22">As for a brother beloved wending on woefullest way?</l>

lines.text: How was the marrow of thee consumedly wasted by sorrow!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="23">How was the marrow of thee consumedly wasted by sorrow!</l>

lines.text: So clean forth of thy breast, rackt with solicitous care,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="24">So clean forth of thy breast, rackt with solicitous care,</l>

lines.text: Mind fled, sense being reft! But I have known thee for certain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="25">Mind fled, sense being reft! But I have known thee for certain</l>

lines.text: E’en from young virginal years lofty of spirit to be.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="26">E’en from young virginal years lofty of spirit to be. </l>

lines.text: Hast thou forgotten the feat whose greatness won thee a royal
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="27">Hast thou forgotten the feat whose greatness won thee a royal</l>

lines.text: Marriage—a deed so prow, never a prower was dared?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="28">Marriage—a deed so prow, never a prower was dared?</l>

lines.text: Yet how sad was the speech thou spakest, thy husband farewelling!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="29">Yet how sad was the speech thou spakest, thy husband farewelling!</l>

lines.text: (Jupiter!) Often thine eyes wiping with sorrowful hand!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="30">(<persName><surname>Jupiter</surname></persName>!) Often thine eyes wiping with sorrowful hand!</l>

lines.text: What manner God so great thus changed thee? Is it that lovers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="31">What manner God so great thus changed thee? Is it that lovers</l>

lines.text: Never will tarry afar parted from person beloved?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="32">Never will tarry afar parted from person beloved?</l>

lines.text: Then unto every God on behalf of thy helpmate, thy sweeting,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="33">Then unto every God on behalf of thy helpmate, thy sweeting,</l>

lines.text: Me thou gayest in vow, not without bloodshed of bulls,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="34">Me thou gayest in vow, not without bloodshed of bulls,</l>

lines.text: If he be granted return, and long while nowise delaying,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="35">If he be granted return, and long while nowise delaying,</l>

lines.text: Captive Asia he add unto Egyptian bounds.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="36">Captive <placeName key="tgn,2097781">Asia</placeName> he add unto Egyptian bounds.</l>

lines.text: Now for such causes I, enrolled in host of the Heavens,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="37">Now for such causes I, enrolled in host of the Heavens,</l>

lines.text: By a new present, discharge promise thou madest of old:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="38">By a new present, discharge promise thou madest of old:</l>

lines.text: Maugrè my will, O Queen, my place on thy head I relinquished,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="39">Maugrè my will, O Queen, my place on thy head I relinquished,</l>

lines.text: Maugrè my will, I attest, swearing by thee and thy head;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="40">Maugrè my will, I attest, swearing by thee and thy head;</l>

lines.text: Penalty due shall befall whoso makes oath to no purpose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="41">Penalty due shall befall whoso makes oath to no purpose.</l>

lines.text: Yet who assumes the vaunt forceful as iron to be?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="42">Yet who assumes the vaunt forceful as iron to be? </l>

lines.text: E’en was that mount o’erthrown, though greatest in universe, where through
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="43">E’en was that mount o’erthrown, though greatest in universe, where through</l>

lines.text: Thía’s illustrious race speeded its voyage to end,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="44">Thía’s illustrious race speeded its voyage to end,</l>

lines.text: Whenas the Medes brought forth new sea, and barbarous youth-hood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="45">Whenas the Medes brought forth new sea, and barbarous youth-hood</l>

lines.text: Urged an Armada to swim traversing middle-Athos.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="46">Urged an <placeName key="tgn,2051145">Armada</placeName> to swim traversing middle-<placeName key="tgn,7002722">Athos</placeName>. </l>

lines.text: What can be done by Hair when such things yield them to Iron?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="47">What can be done by Hair when such things yield them to Iron?</l>

lines.text: Jupiter! Grant Chalybon perish the whole of the race,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="48"><persName><surname>Jupiter</surname></persName>! Grant Chalybon perish the whole of the race,</l>

lines.text: Eke who in primal times ore seeking under the surface
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="49">Eke who in primal times ore seeking under the surface</l>

lines.text: Showed th’ example, and spalled iron however so hard.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="50">Showed th’ example, and spalled iron however so hard.</l>

lines.text: Shortly before I was shorn my sister tresses bewailèd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="51">Shortly before I was shorn my sister tresses bewailèd</l>

lines.text: Lot of me, e’en as the sole brother to Memnon the Black,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="52">Lot of me, e’en as the sole brother to Memnon the Black,</l>

lines.text: Winnowing upper air wi’ feathers flashing and quiv’ring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="53">Winnowing upper air wi’ feathers flashing and quiv’ring,</l>

lines.text: Chloris’ wing-borne steed, came before Arsinoë,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="54">Chloris’ wing-borne steed, came before Arsinoë,</l>

lines.text: Whence upraising myself he flies through aëry shadows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="55">Whence upraising myself he flies through aëry shadows,</l>

lines.text: And in chaste Venus’ breast drops he the present he bears.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="56">And in chaste Venus’ breast drops he the present he bears.</l>

lines.text: Eke Zephyritis had sent, for the purpose trusted, her bondsman,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="57">Eke Zephyritis had sent, for the purpose trusted, her bondsman,</l>

lines.text: Settler of Grecian strain on the Canopian strand.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="58">Settler of Grecian strain on the Canopian strand.</l>

lines.text: So willed various Gods, lest sole ’mid lights of the Heavens
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="59">So willed various Gods, lest sole ’mid lights of the Heavens</l>

lines.text: Should Ariadne’s crown taken from temples of her
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="60">Should Ariadne’s crown taken from temples of her</l>

lines.text: Glitter in gold, but we not less shine fulgent in splendour,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="61">Glitter in gold, but we not less shine fulgent in splendour,</l>

lines.text: We the consecrate spoils shed by a blond-hued head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="62">We the consecrate spoils shed by a blond-hued head,</l>

lines.text: Even as weeping-wet sought I the fanes of Celestials
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="63">Even as weeping-wet sought I the fanes of Celestials </l>

lines.text: Placed me the Goddess a new light amid star-lights of old:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="64">Placed me the Goddess a new light amid star-lights of old:</l>

lines.text: For with Virgo in touch and joining the furious Lion’s
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="65">For with Virgo in touch and joining the furious Lion’s</l>

lines.text: Radiance with Callisto, maid of Lyc´on beloved,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="66">Radiance with Callisto, maid of Lyc´on beloved, </l>

lines.text: Wind I still to the west, conducting tardy Boötes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="67">Wind I still to the west, conducting tardy Boötes,</l>

lines.text: Who unwilling and slow must into Ocean merge.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="68">Who unwilling and slow must into Ocean merge. </l>

lines.text: Yet though press me o’night the pacing footprints of Godheads,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="69">Yet though press me o’night the pacing footprints of Godheads,</l>

lines.text: Tethys, hoary of hair, ever regains me by day.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="70">Tethys, hoary of hair, ever regains me by day. </l>

lines.text: (Lend me thy leave to speak such words, Rhamnusian Virgin,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="71">(Lend me thy leave to speak such words, Rhamnusian Virgin,</l>

lines.text: Verities like unto these never in fear will I veil;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="72">Verities like unto these never in fear will I veil; </l>

lines.text: Albeit every star asperse me with enemy’s censure,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="73">Albeit every star asperse me with enemy’s censure,</l>

lines.text: Secrets in soothfast heart hoarded perforce I reveal.)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="74">Secrets in soothfast heart hoarded perforce I reveal.) </l>

lines.text: Nowise gladdens me so this state as absence torments me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="75">Nowise gladdens me so this state as absence torments me,</l>

lines.text: Absence doomëd for aye ta’en fro’ my mistress’s head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="76">Absence doomëd for aye ta’en fro’ my mistress’s head,</l>

lines.text: Where I was wont (though she such cares unknew in her girlhood)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="77">Where I was wont (though she such cares unknew in her girlhood)</l>

lines.text: Many a thousand scents, Syrian unguents, to sip.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="78">Many a thousand scents, Syrian unguents, to sip. </l>

lines.text: Now do you pair conjoined by the longed-for light of the torches,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="79">Now do you pair conjoined by the longed-for light of the torches,</l>

lines.text: Earlier yield not selves unto unanimous wills
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="80">Earlier yield not selves unto unanimous wills </l>

lines.text: Nor wi’ the dresses doft your barèd nipples encounter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="81">Nor wi’ the dresses doft your barèd nipples encounter,</l>

lines.text: Ere shall yon onyx-vase pour me libations glad,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="82">Ere shall yon onyx-vase pour me libations glad,</l>

lines.text: Onyx yours, ye that seek only rights of virtuous bed-rite.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="83">Onyx yours, ye that seek only rights of virtuous bed-rite.</l>

lines.text: But who yieldeth herself unto advowtry impure,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="84">But who yieldeth herself unto advowtry impure,</l>

lines.text: Ah! may her loathed gifts in light dust uselessly soak,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="85">Ah! may her loathed gifts in light dust uselessly soak,</l>

lines.text: For of unworthy sprite never a gift I desire.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="86">For of unworthy sprite never a gift I desire.</l>

lines.text: Rather, O new-mated brides, be concord aye your companion,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="87">Rather, O new-mated brides, be concord aye your companion,</l>

lines.text: Ever let constant love dwell in the dwellings of you.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="88">Ever let constant love dwell in the dwellings of you. </l>

lines.text: Yet when thou sightest, O Queen, the Constellations, I pray thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="89">Yet when thou sightest, O Queen, the Constellations, I pray thee,</l>

lines.text: Every festal day Venus the Goddess appease;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="90">Every festal day Venus the Goddess appease;</l>

lines.text: Nor of thy unguent-gifts allow myself to be lacking,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="91">Nor of thy unguent-gifts allow myself to be lacking,</l>

lines.text: Nay, do thou rather add largeliest increase to boons.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="92">Nay, do thou rather add largeliest increase to boons. </l>

lines.text: Would but the stars down fall! Could I of my Queen be the hair-lock,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="93">Would but the stars down fall! Could I of my Queen be the hair-lock,</l>

lines.text: Neighbour to Hydrochois e’en let Oarion shine.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:66" n="94">Neighbour to Hydrochois e’en let Oarion shine.</l>

head: DIALOGUE CONCERNING CATULLUS AT A HARLOT’S DOOR.
Quintus.
Door.
Quintus.
Door.
Quintus.
Door.
Quintus.
Door.
Quintus.
Door.

lines.text: O to the gentle spouse right dear, right dear to his parent,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="1">O to the gentle spouse right dear, right dear to his parent,</l>

lines.text: Hail, and with increase fair Jupiter lend thee his aid,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="2">Hail, and with increase fair Jupiter lend thee his aid,</l>

lines.text: Door, ’tis said wast fain kind service render to Balbus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="3">Door, ’tis said wast fain kind service render to Balbus</l>

lines.text: Erst while, long as the house by her old owner was held;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="4">Erst while, long as the house by her old owner was held;</l>

lines.text: Yet wast rumoured again to serve a purpose malignant,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="5">Yet wast rumoured again to serve a purpose malignant,</l>

lines.text: After the elder was stretched, thou being oped for a bride.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="6">After the elder was stretched, thou being oped for a bride.</l>

lines.text: Come, then, tell us the why in thee such change be reported
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="7">Come, then, tell us the why in thee such change be reported</l>

lines.text: That to thy lord hast abjured faithfulness owed of old?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="8">That to thy lord hast abjured faithfulness owed of old?</l>

lines.text: Never (so chance I to please Caeci1ius owning me now-a-days!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="9">Never (so chance I to please Caeci1ius owning me now-a-days!)</l>

lines.text: Is it my own default, how so they say it be mine;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="10">Is it my own default, how so they say it be mine;</l>

lines.text: Nor can any declare aught sin by me was committed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="11">Nor can any declare aught sin by me was committed.</l>

lines.text: Yet it is so declared (Quintus!) by fable of folk;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="12">Yet it is so declared (Quintus!) by fable of folk;</l>

lines.text: Who, whenever they find things done no better than should be,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="13">Who, whenever they find things done no better than should be,</l>

lines.text: Come to me outcrying all:—Door, the default is thine own!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="14">Come to me outcrying all:—<q rend="double">Door, the default is thine own!</q></l>

lines.text: This be never enough for thee one-worded to utter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="15">This be never enough for thee one-worded to utter,</l>

lines.text: But in such way to deal, each and all sense it and see.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="16">But in such way to deal, each and all sense it and see.</l>

lines.text: What shall I do? None asks, while nobody troubles to know.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="17">What shall I do? None asks, while nobody troubles to know.</l>

lines.text: Willing are we? unto us stay not thy saying to say.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="18">Willing are we? unto us stay not thy saying to say.</l>

lines.text: First let me note that the maid to us committed (assert they)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="19">First let me note that the maid to us committed (assert they)</l>

lines.text: Was but a fraud: her mate never a touch of her had,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="20">Was but a fraud: her mate never a touch of her had,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="21"><gap reason="lost" rend=" . . . . . . . "/></l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="22"><gap reason="lost" rend=" . . . . . . . "/></l>

lines.text: But that a father durst dishonour the bed of his first-born,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="23">But that a father durst dishonour the bed of his first-born,</l>

lines.text: Folk all swear, and the house hapless with incest bewray;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="24">Folk all swear, and the house hapless with incest bewray;</l>

lines.text: Or that his impious mind was blunt with fiery passion
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="25">Or that his impious mind was blunt with fiery passion</l>

lines.text: Or that his impotent son sprang from incapable seed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="26">Or that his impotent son sprang from incapable seed.</l>

lines.text: And to be sought was one with nerve more nervous endowèd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="27">And to be sought was one with nerve more nervous endowèd,</l>

lines.text: Who could better avail zone of the virgin to loose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="28">Who could better avail zone of the virgin to loose.</l>

lines.text: ’Sooth, of egregious sire for piety wondrous, thou tellest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="29">’Sooth, of egregious sire for piety wondrous, thou tellest,</l>

lines.text: Who in the heart of his son lief was . . . !
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="30">Who in the heart of his son lief was <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . ."/> !</l>

lines.text: Yet professed herself not only this to be knowing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="31">Yet professed herself not only this to be knowing, </l>

lines.text: Brixia-town that lies under the Cycnean cliff,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="32">Brixia-town that lies under the Cycnean cliff,</l>

lines.text: Traversed by Mella-stream’s soft-flowing yellow-hued current,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="33">Traversed by Mella-stream’s soft-flowing yellow-hued current,</l>

lines.text: Brixia, Vérona’s mother, I love for my home.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="34">Brixia, Vérona’s mother, I love for my home.</l>

lines.text: Eke of Posthumius’ loves and Cornelius too there be tattle,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="35">Eke of Posthumius’ loves and Cornelius too there be tattle,</l>

lines.text: With whom dared the dame evil advowtry commit.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="36">With whom dared the dame evil advowtry commit.</l>

lines.text: Here might somebody ask:—How, Door, hast mastered such matter?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="37">Here might somebody ask:—<q rend="double">How, Door, hast mastered such matter?</q></l>

lines.text: Thou that canst never avail threshold of owner to quit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="38"><q rend="double; merge">Thou that canst never avail threshold of owner to quit,</q></l>

lines.text: Neither canst listen to folk since here fast fixt to the side-posts
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="39"><q rend="double; merge">Neither canst listen to folk since here fast fixt to the side-posts</q></l>

lines.text: Only one office thou hast, shutting or opening the house.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="40"><q rend="double; merge">Only one office thou hast, shutting or opening the house.</q></l>

lines.text: Oft have I heard our dame in furtive murmurs o’er telling,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="41">Oft have I heard our dame in furtive murmurs o’er telling,</l>

lines.text: When with her handmaids alone, these her flagitious deeds,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="42">When with her handmaids alone, these her flagitious deeds,</l>

lines.text: Citing fore-cited names for that she never could fancy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="43">Citing fore-cited names for that she never could fancy</l>

lines.text: Ever a Door was endow’d either with earlet or tongue.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="44">Ever a Door was endow’d either with earlet or tongue.</l>

lines.text: Further she noted a wight whose name in public to mention
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="45">Further she noted a wight whose name in public to mention</l>

lines.text: Nill I, lest he upraise eyebrows of carroty hue;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="46">Nill I, lest he upraise eyebrows of carroty hue;</l>

lines.text: Long is the loon and large the law-suit brought they against him
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="47">Long is the loon and large the law-suit brought they against him</l>

lines.text: Touching a child-bed false, claim of a belly that lied.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:67" n="48">Touching a child-bed false, claim of a belly that lied.</l>

lines.text: When to me sore opprest by bitter chance of misfortune
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="1">When to me sore opprest by bitter chance of misfortune</l>

lines.text: This thy letter thou send’st written wi’ blotting of tears,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="2">This thy letter thou send’st written wi’ blotting of tears,</l>

lines.text: So might I save thee flung by spuming billows of ocean,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="3">So might I save thee flung by spuming billows of ocean,</l>

lines.text: Shipwreckt, rescuing life snatcht from the threshold of death;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="4">Shipwreckt, rescuing life snatcht from the threshold of death;</l>

lines.text: Eke neither Venus the Holy to rest in slumber’s refreshment
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="5">Eke neither Venus the Holy to rest in slumber’s refreshment</l>

lines.text: Grants thee her grace on couch lying deserted and lone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="6">Grants thee her grace on couch lying deserted and lone,</l>

lines.text: Nor can the Muses avail with dulcet song of old writers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="7">Nor can the Muses avail with dulcet song of old writers</l>

lines.text: Ever delight thy mind sleepless in anxious care;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="8">Ever delight thy mind sleepless in anxious care;</l>

lines.text: Grateful be this to my thought since thus thy friend I’m entitled,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="9">Grateful be this to my thought since thus thy friend I’m entitled,</l>

lines.text: Hence of me seekest thou gifts Muses and Venus can give:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="10">Hence of me seekest thou gifts Muses and Venus can give:</l>

lines.text: But that bide not unknown to thee my sorrows (O Manius!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="11">But that bide not unknown to thee my sorrows (O Manius!)</l>

lines.text: And lest office of host I should be holden to hate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="12">And lest office of host I should be holden to hate, </l>

lines.text: Learn how in Fortune’s deeps I chance myself to be drownèd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="13">Learn how in Fortune’s deeps I chance myself to be drownèd,</l>

lines.text: Nor fro’ the poor rich boons furthermore prithee require.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="14">Nor fro’ the poor rich boons furthermore prithee require.</l>

lines.text: What while first to myself the pure-white garment was given,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="15">What while first to myself the pure-white garment was given,</l>

lines.text: Whenas my flowery years flowed in fruition of spring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="16">Whenas my flowery years flowed in fruition of spring,</l>

lines.text: Much I disported enow, nor ’bode I a stranger to Goddess
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="17">Much I disported enow, nor ’bode I a stranger to Goddess</l>

lines.text: Who with our cares is lief sweetness of bitter to mix:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="18">Who with our cares is lief sweetness of bitter to mix:</l>

lines.text: Yet did a brother’s death pursuits like these to my sorrow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="19">Yet did a brother’s death pursuits like these to my sorrow</l>

lines.text: Bid for me cease: Oh, snatcht brother! from wretchedest me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="20">Bid for me cease: Oh, snatcht brother! from wretchedest me.</l>

lines.text: Then, yea, thou by thy dying hast broke my comfort, O brother;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="21">Then, yea, thou by thy dying hast broke my comfort, O brother;</l>

lines.text: Buried together wi’ thee lieth the whole of our house;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="22">Buried together wi’ thee lieth the whole of our house;</l>

lines.text: Perisht along wi’ thyself all gauds and joys of our life-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="23">Perisht along wi’ thyself all gauds and joys of our life-tide,</l>

lines.text: Douce love fostered by thee during the term of our days.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="24">Douce love fostered by thee during the term of our days.</l>

lines.text: After thy doom of death fro’ mind I banishèd wholly
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="25">After thy doom of death fro’ mind I banishèd wholly</l>

lines.text: Studies like these, and all lending a solace to soul;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="26">Studies like these, and all lending a solace to soul;</l>

lines.text: Wherefore as to thy writ:—Verona’s home for Catullus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="27">Wherefore as to thy writ:—<q rend="double">Verona’s home for Catullus</q></l>

lines.text: Bringeth him shame, for there men of superior mark
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="28"><q rend="double; merge">Bringeth him shame, for there men of superior mark</q></l>

lines.text: Must on a deserted couch fain chafe their refrigerate limbs:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="29"><q rend="double; merge">Must on a deserted couch fain chafe their refrigerate limbs:</q></l>

lines.text: Such be no shame (Manius!): rather ’tis matter of ruth.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="30">Such be no shame (Manius!): rather ’tis matter of ruth.</l>

lines.text: Pardon me, then, wilt thou an gifts bereft me by grieving
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="31">Pardon me, then, wilt thou an gifts bereft me by grieving</l>

lines.text: These I send not to thee since I avail not present.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="32">These I send not to thee since I avail not present. </l>

lines.text: For, that I own not here abundant treasure of writings
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="33">For, that I own not here abundant treasure of writings</l>

lines.text: Has for its cause, in Rome dwell I; and there am I homed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="34">Has for its cause, in Rome dwell I; and there am I homed,</l>

lines.text: There be my seat, and there my years are gathered to harvest;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="35">There be my seat, and there my years are gathered to harvest;</l>

lines.text: Out of book-cases galore here am I followed by one.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="36">Out of book-cases galore here am I followed by one. </l>

lines.text: This being thus, nill I thou deem ’tis spirit malignant
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="37">This being thus, nill I thou deem ’tis spirit malignant</l>

lines.text: Acts in such wise or mind lacking of liberal mood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="38">Acts in such wise or mind lacking of liberal mood </l>

lines.text: That to thy prayer both gifts be not in plenty supplièd:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="39">That to thy prayer both gifts be not in plenty supplièd:</l>

lines.text: Willingly both had I sent, had I the needed supply.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68" n="40">Willingly both had I sent, had I the needed supply.</l>

lines.text: Nor can I (Goddesses!) hide in what things Allius sent me
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="1"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_41"/>Nor can I (Goddesses!) hide in what things Allius sent me</l>

lines.text: Aid, forbear to declare what was the aidance he deigned:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="2"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_42"/>Aid, forbear to declare what was the aidance he deigned:</l>

lines.text: Neither shall fugitive Time from centuries ever oblivious
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="3"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_43"/>Neither shall fugitive Time from centuries ever oblivious</l>

lines.text: Veil in the blinds of night friendship he lavisht on me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="4"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_44"/>Veil in the blinds of night friendship he lavisht on me.</l>

lines.text: But will I say unto you what you shall say to the many
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="5"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_45"/>But will I say unto you what you shall say to the many</l>

lines.text: Thousands in turn, and make paper, old crone, to proclaim
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="6"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_46"/>Thousands in turn, and make paper, old crone, to proclaim</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="7"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_47"/><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: And in his death become noted the more and the more,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="8"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_48"/>And in his death become noted the more and the more,</l>

lines.text: Nor let spider on high that weaves her delicate webbing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="9"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_49"/>Nor let spider on high that weaves her delicate webbing</l>

lines.text: Practise such labours o’er Allius’ obsolete name.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="10"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_50"/>Practise such labours o’er Allius’ obsolete name.</l>

lines.text: For that ye weet right well what care Amathúsia two-faced
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="11"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_51"/>For that ye weet right well what care Amathúsia two-faced</l>

lines.text: Gave me, and how she dasht every hope to the ground,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="12"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_52"/>Gave me, and how she dasht every hope to the ground,</l>

lines.text: Whenas I burnt so hot as burn Trinacria’s rocks or
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="13"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_53"/>Whenas I burnt so hot as burn Trinacria’s rocks or </l>

lines.text: Mallia stream that feeds Œtéan Thermopylae;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="14"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_54"/>Mallia stream that feeds Œtéan Thermopylae;</l>

lines.text: Nor did these saddened eyes to be dimmed by assiduous weeping
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="15"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_55"/>Nor did these saddened eyes to be dimmed by assiduous weeping</l>

lines.text: Cease, and my cheeks with showers ever in sadness be wet.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="16"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_56"/>Cease, and my cheeks with showers ever in sadness be wet.</l>

lines.text: E’en as from aëry heights of mountain springeth a springlet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="17"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_57"/>E’en as from aëry heights of mountain springeth a springlet</l>

lines.text: Limpidest leaping forth from rocking felted with moss,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="18"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_58"/>Limpidest leaping forth from rocking felted with moss,</l>

lines.text: Then having headlong rolled the prone-laid valley downpouring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="19"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_59"/>Then having headlong rolled the prone-laid valley downpouring,</l>

lines.text: Populous region amid wendeth his gradual way,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="20"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_60"/>Populous region amid wendeth his gradual way,</l>

lines.text: Sweetest solace of all to the sweltering traveller wayworn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="21"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_61"/>Sweetest solace of all to the sweltering traveller wayworn,</l>

lines.text: Whenas the heavy heat fissures the fiery fields;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="22"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_62"/>Whenas the heavy heat fissures the fiery fields; </l>

lines.text: Or, as to seamen lost in night of whirlwind a-glooming
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="23"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_63"/>Or, as to seamen lost in night of whirlwind a-glooming</l>

lines.text: Gentle of breath there comes fairest and favouring breeze,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="24"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_64"/>Gentle of breath there comes fairest and favouring breeze,</l>

lines.text: Pollux anon being prayed, nor less vows offered to Castor:—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="25"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_65"/>Pollux anon being prayed, nor less vows offered to Castor:—</l>

lines.text: Such was the aidance to us Manius pleased to afford.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="26"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_66"/>Such was the aidance to us Manius pleased to afford.</l>

lines.text: He to my narrow domains far wider limits laid open,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="27"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_67"/>He to my narrow domains far wider limits laid open,</l>

lines.text: He too gave me the house, also he gave me the dame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="28"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_68"/>He too gave me the house, also he gave me the dame,</l>

lines.text: She upon whom both might exert them, partners in love deeds.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="29"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_69"/>She upon whom both might exert them, partners in love deeds.</l>

lines.text: Thither graceful of gait pacing my goddess white-hued
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="30"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_70"/>Thither graceful of gait pacing my goddess white-hued</l>

lines.text: Came and with gleaming foot on the worn sole of the threshold
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="31"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_71"/>Came and with gleaming foot on the worn sole of the threshold</l>

lines.text: Stood she and prest its slab creakihg her sandals the while;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="32"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_72"/>Stood she and prest its slab creakihg her sandals the while;</l>

lines.text: E’enso with love enflamed in olden days to her helpmate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="33"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_73"/>E’enso with love enflamed in olden days to her helpmate,</l>

lines.text: Laodamía the home Protesiléan besought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="34"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_74"/>Laodamía the home Protesiléan besought,</l>

lines.text: Sought, but in vain, for ne’er wi’ sacrificial blood shed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="35"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_75"/>Sought, but in vain, for ne’er wi’ sacrificial blood shed</l>

lines.text: Victims appeased the Lords ruling Celestial seats:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="36"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_76"/>Victims appeased the Lords ruling Celestial seats:</l>

lines.text: Never may I so joy in aught (Rhamnusian Virgin!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="37"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_77"/>Never may I so joy in aught (Rhamnusian Virgin!) </l>

lines.text: That I engage in deed maugrè the will of the Lords.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="38"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_78"/>That I engage in deed maugrè the will of the Lords.</l>

lines.text: How starved altar can crave for gore in piety poured,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="39"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_79"/>How starved altar can crave for gore in piety poured,</l>

lines.text: Laodamia learnt taught by the loss of her man,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="40"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_80"/>Laodamia learnt taught by the loss of her man,</l>

lines.text: Driven perforce to loose the neck of new-wedded help-mate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="41"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_81"/>Driven perforce to loose the neck of new-wedded help-mate,</l>

lines.text: Whenas a winter had gone, nor other winter had come,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="42"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_82"/>Whenas a winter had gone, nor other winter had come,</l>

lines.text: Ere in the long dark nights her greeding love was so sated
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="43"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_83"/>Ere in the long dark nights her greeding love was so sated</l>

lines.text: That she had power to live maugrè a marriage broke off,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="44"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_84"/>That she had power to live maugrè a marriage broke off,</l>

lines.text: Which, as the Parcae knew, too soon was fated to happen
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="45"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_85"/>Which, as the Parcae knew, too soon was fated to happen</l>

lines.text: Should he a soldier sail bound for those llian walls.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="46"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_86"/>Should he a soldier sail bound for those llian walls. </l>

lines.text: For that by Helena’s rape, the Champion-leaders of Argives
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="47"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_87"/>For that by Helena’s rape, the Champion-leaders of Argives</l>

lines.text: Unto herself to incite Troy had already begun,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="48"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_88"/>Unto herself to incite Troy had already begun,</l>

lines.text: Troy (ah, curst be the name) common tomb of Asia and Europe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="49"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_89"/>Troy (ah, curst be the name) common tomb of Asia and Europe,</l>

lines.text: Troy to sad ashes that turned valour and valorous men!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="50"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_90"/>Troy to sad ashes that turned valour and valorous men!</l>

lines.text: Eke to our brother beloved, destruction ever lamented
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="51"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_91"/>Eke to our brother beloved, destruction ever lamented</l>

lines.text: Brought she: O Brother for aye lost unto wretchedmost me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="52"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_92"/>Brought she: O Brother for aye lost unto wretchedmost me,</l>

lines.text: Oh, to thy wretchedmost brother lost the light of his life-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="53"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_93"/>Oh, to thy wretchedmost brother lost the light of his life-tide,</l>

lines.text: Buried together wi’ thee lieth the whole of our house:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="54"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_94"/>Buried together wi’ thee lieth the whole of our house:</l>

lines.text: Perisht along wi’ thyself forthright all joys we enjoyèd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="55"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_95"/>Perisht along wi’ thyself forthright all joys we enjoyèd,</l>

lines.text: Douce joys fed by thy love during the term of our days;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="56"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_96"/>Douce joys fed by thy love during the term of our days;</l>

lines.text: Whom now art tombed so far nor ’mid familiar pavestones
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="57"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_97"/>Whom now art tombed so far nor ’mid familiar pavestones</l>

lines.text: Nor wi’ thine ashes stored near to thy kith and thy kin,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="58"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_98"/>Nor wi’ thine ashes stored near to thy kith and thy kin,</l>

lines.text: But in that Troy obscene, that Troy of ill-omen, entombèd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="59"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_99"/>But in that Troy obscene, that Troy of ill-omen, entombèd</l>

lines.text: Holds thee, an alien earth-buried in uttermost bourne.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="60"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_100"/>Holds thee, an alien earth-buried in uttermost bourne.</l>

lines.text: Thither in haste so hot (’tis said) from allwhere the Youth-hood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="61"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_101"/>Thither in haste so hot (’tis said) from allwhere the Youth-hood</l>

lines.text: Grecian, farèd in hosts forth of their hearths and their homes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="62"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_102"/>Grecian, farèd in hosts forth of their hearths and their homes,</l>

lines.text: Lest with a stolen punk with fullest of pleasure should Paris
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="63"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_103"/>Lest with a stolen punk with fullest of pleasure should Paris</l>

lines.text: Fairly at leisure and ease sleep in the pacific bed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="64"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_104"/>Fairly at leisure and ease sleep in the pacific bed.</l>

lines.text: Such was the hapless chance, most beautiful Laodamia,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="65"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_105"/>Such was the hapless chance, most beautiful Laodamia,</l>

lines.text: Tare fro’ thee dearer than life, dearer than spirit itself,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="66"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_106"/>Tare fro’ thee dearer than life, dearer than spirit itself,</l>

lines.text: Him, that husband, whose love in so mighty a whirlpool of passion
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="67"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_107"/>Him, that husband, whose love in so mighty a whirlpool of passion</l>

lines.text: Whelmed thee absorbed and plunged deep in its gulfy abyss,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="68"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_108"/>Whelmed thee absorbed and plunged deep in its gulfy abyss,</l>

lines.text: E’en as the Grecians tell hard by Phenéus of Cylléne
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="69"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_109"/>E’en as the Grecians tell hard by Phenéus of Cylléne</l>

lines.text: Drained was the marish and dried, forming the fattest of soils,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="70"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_110"/>Drained was the marish and dried, forming the fattest of soils,</l>

lines.text: Whenas in days long done to delve through marrow of mountains
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="71"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_111"/>Whenas in days long done to delve through marrow of mountains</l>

lines.text: Daréd, falsing his sire, Amphtryóniades;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="72"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_112"/>Daréd, falsing his sire, Amphtryóniades;</l>

lines.text: What time sure of his shafts he smote Stymphalian monsters
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="73"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_113"/>What time sure of his shafts he smote Stymphalian monsters</l>

lines.text: Slaying their host at the hest dealt by a lord of less worth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="74"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_114"/>Slaying their host at the hest dealt by a lord of less worth,</l>

lines.text: So might the gateway of Heaven be trodden by more of the godheads,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="75"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_115"/>So might the gateway of Heaven be trodden by more of the godheads,</l>

lines.text: Nor might Hébé abide longer to maidenhood doomed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="76"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_116"/>Nor might Hébé abide longer to maidenhood doomed.</l>

lines.text: Yet was the depth of thy love far deeper than deepest of marish
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="77"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_117"/>Yet was the depth of thy love far deeper than deepest of marish</l>

lines.text: Which the hard mistress’s yoke taught him so tamely to bear;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="78"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_118"/>Which the hard mistress’s yoke taught him so tamely to bear;</l>

lines.text: Never was head so dear to a grandsire wasted by life-tide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="79"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_119"/>Never was head so dear to a grandsire wasted by life-tide</l>

lines.text: Whenas one daughter alone a grandson so tardy had reared,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="80"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_120"/>Whenas one daughter alone a grandson so tardy had reared,</l>

lines.text: Who being found against hope to inherit riches of forbears
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="81"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_121"/>Who being found against hope to inherit riches of forbears</l>

lines.text: In the well-witnessed Will haply by name did appear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="82"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_122"/>In the well-witnessed Will haply by name did appear,</l>

lines.text: And ’spite impious hopes of baffled claimant to kinship
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="83"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_123"/>And ’spite impious hopes of baffled claimant to kinship</l>

lines.text: Startles the Vulturine grip clutching the frost-bitten poll.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="84"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_124"/>Startles the Vulturine grip clutching the frost-bitten poll.</l>

lines.text: Nor with such rapture e’er joyed his mate of snowy-hued plumage
