lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="85"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_125"/>Nor with such rapture e’er joyed his mate of snowy-hued plumage</l>

lines.text: Dove-mate, albeit aye wont in her immoderate heat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="86"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_126"/>Dove-mate, albeit aye wont in her immoderate heat </l>

lines.text: Said be the bird to snatch hot kisses with beak ever billing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="87"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_127"/>Said be the bird to snatch hot kisses with beak ever billing,</l>

lines.text: As diddest thou:—yet is Woman multivolent still.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="88"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_128"/>As diddest thou:—yet is Woman multivolent still. </l>

lines.text: But thou ’vailedest alone all these to conquer in love-lowe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="89"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_129"/>But thou ’vailedest alone all these to conquer in love-lowe,</l>

lines.text: When conjoindd once more unto thy yellow-haired spouse.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="90"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_130"/>When conjoindd once more unto thy yellow-haired spouse.</l>

lines.text: Worthy of yielding to her in naught or ever so little
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="91"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_131"/>Worthy of yielding to her in naught or ever so little </l>

lines.text: Came to the bosom of us she, the fair light of my life,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="92"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_132"/>Came to the bosom of us she, the fair light of my life,</l>

lines.text: Round whom fluttering oft the Love-God hither and thither
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="93"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_133"/>Round whom fluttering oft the Love-God hither and thither</l>

lines.text: Shone with a candid sheen robed in his safflower dress.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="94"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_134"/>Shone with a candid sheen robed in his safflower dress.</l>

lines.text: She though never she bide with one Catullus contented,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="95"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_135"/>She though never she bide with one Catullus contented,</l>

lines.text: Yet will I bear with the rare thefts of my dame the discreet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="96"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_136"/>Yet will I bear with the rare thefts of my dame the discreet,</l>

lines.text: Lest over-irk I give which still of fools is the fashion.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="97"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_137"/>Lest over-irk I give which still of fools is the fashion. </l>

lines.text: Often did Juno eke Queen of the Heavenly host
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="98"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_138"/>Often did Juno eke Queen of the Heavenly host</l>

lines.text: Boil wi’ the rabidest rage at dire default of a husband
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="99"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_139"/>Boil wi’ the rabidest rage at dire default of a husband </l>

lines.text: Learning the manifold thefts of her omnivolent Jove,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="100"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_140"/>Learning the manifold thefts of her omnivolent Jove,</l>

lines.text: Yet with the Gods mankind ’tis nowise righteous to liken,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="101"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_141"/>Yet with the Gods mankind ’tis nowise righteous to liken,</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="101a"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_141a"/><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * * * * * "/></l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="101aa"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_141aa"/><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Rid me of graceless task fit for a tremulous sire.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="102"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_142"/>Rid me of graceless task fit for a tremulous sire. </l>

lines.text: Yet was she never to me by hand paternal committed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="103"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_143"/>Yet was she never to me by hand paternal committed</l>

lines.text: Whenas she came to my house reeking Assyrian scents;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="104"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_144"/>Whenas she came to my house reeking Assyrian scents;</l>

lines.text: Nay, in the darkness of night her furtive favours she deigned me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="105"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_145"/>Nay, in the darkness of night her furtive favours she deigned me,</l>

lines.text: Self-willed taking herself from very mate’s very breast.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="106"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_146"/>Self-willed taking herself from very mate’s very breast.</l>

lines.text: Wherefore I hold it enough since given to us and us only
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="107"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_147"/>Wherefore I hold it enough since given to us and us only</l>

lines.text: Boon of that day with Stone whiter than wont she denotes.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="108"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_148"/>Boon of that day with Stone whiter than wont she denotes.</l>

lines.text: This to thee—all that I can—this offering couched in verses
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="109"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_149"/>This to thee—all that I can—this offering couched in verses</l>

lines.text: (Allius!) as my return give I for service galore;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="110"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_150"/>(Allius!) as my return give I for service galore;</l>

lines.text: So wi’ the seabriny rust your name may never be sullied
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="111"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_151"/>So wi’ the seabriny rust your name may never be sullied</l>

lines.text: This day and that nor yet other and other again.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="112"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_152"/>This day and that nor yet other and other again. </l>

lines.text: Hereto add may the Gods all good gifts, which Themis erewhiles
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="113"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_153"/>Hereto add may the Gods all good gifts, which Themis erewhiles</l>

lines.text: Wont on the pious of old from her full store to bestow:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="114"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_154"/>Wont on the pious of old from her full store to bestow:</l>

lines.text: Blest be the times of the twain, thyself and she who thy life is,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="115"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_155"/>Blest be the times of the twain, thyself and she who thy life is,</l>

lines.text: Also the home wherein dallied we, no less the Dame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="116"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_156"/>Also the home wherein dallied we, no less the Dame,</l>

lines.text: Anser to boot who first of mortals brought us together,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="117"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_157"/>Anser to boot who first of mortals brought us together,</l>

lines.text: Whence from beginning all good Fortunes that blest us were born.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="118"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_158"/>Whence from beginning all good Fortunes that blest us were born.</l>

lines.text: Lastly than every else one dearer than self and far dearer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="119"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_159"/>Lastly than every else one dearer than self and far dearer,</l>

lines.text: Light of my life who alive living to me can endear.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:68a" n="120"><milestone unit="throughline" n="throughline_160"/>Light of my life who alive living to me can endear.</l>

notes: Combined with 68 in the print edition. Separated here in keeping with convention.

lines.text: Wonder not blatantly why no woman shall ever be willing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="1">Wonder not blatantly why no woman shall ever be willing</l>

lines.text: (Rufus!) her tender thigh under thyself to bestow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="2">(Rufus!) her tender thigh under thyself to bestow, </l>

lines.text: Not an thou tempt her full by bribes of the rarest garments,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="3">Not an thou tempt her full by bribes of the rarest garments,</l>

lines.text: Or by the dear delights gems the pellucidest deal.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="4">Or by the dear delights gems the pellucidest deal. </l>

lines.text: Harms thee an ugly tale wherein of thee is recorded
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="5">Harms thee an ugly tale wherein of thee is recorded</l>

lines.text: Horrible stench of the goat under thine arm-pits be lodged.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="6">Horrible stench of the goat under thine arm-pits be lodged.</l>

lines.text: All are in dread thereof; nor wonder this, for ’tis evil
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="7">All are in dread thereof; nor wonder this, for ’tis evil</l>

lines.text: Beastie, nor damsel fair ever thereto shall succumb.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="8">Beastie, nor damsel fair ever thereto shall succumb.</l>

lines.text: So do thou either kill that cruel pest o’ their noses,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="9">So do thou either kill that cruel pest o’ their noses,</l>

lines.text: Or at their reason of flight blatantly wondering cease.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:69" n="10">Or at their reason of flight blatantly wondering cease.</l>

lines.text: Never, my woman oft says, with any of men will she mate be,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:70" n="1">Never, my woman oft says, with any of men will she mate be,</l>

lines.text: Save wi’ my own very self, ask her though Jupiter deign!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:70" n="2">Save wi’ my own very self, ask her though Jupiter deign!</l>

lines.text: Says she: but womanly words that are spoken to desireful lover
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:70" n="3">Says she: but womanly words that are spoken to desireful lover</l>

lines.text: Ought to be written on wind or upon water that runs.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:70" n="4">Ought to be written on wind or upon water that runs.</l>

lines.text: An of a goat-stink damned from armpits fusty one suffer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:71" n="1">An of a goat-stink damned from armpits fusty one suffer,</l>

lines.text: Or if a crippling gout worthily any one rack,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:71" n="2">Or if a crippling gout worthily any one rack,</l>

lines.text: ’Tis that rival o’ thine who lief in loves of you meddles,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:71" n="3">’Tis that rival o’ thine who lief in loves of you meddles,</l>

lines.text: And, by a wondrous fate, gains him the twain of such ills.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:71" n="4">And, by a wondrous fate, gains him the twain of such ills.</l>

lines.text: For that, oft as he . . . , so oft that penance be two-fold;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:71" n="5">For that, oft as he <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . "/>, so oft that penance be two-fold;</l>

lines.text: Stifles her stench of goat, he too is kilt by his gout.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:71" n="6">Stifles her stench of goat, he too is kilt by his gout.</l>

lines.text: Wont thou to vaunt whilòme of, knowing only Catullus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="1">Wont thou to vaunt whilòme of, knowing only Catullus</l>

lines.text: (Lesbia!) nor to prefer Jupiter’s self to myself.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="2">(Lesbia!) nor to prefer Jupiter’s self to myself.</l>

lines.text: Then, too, I loved thee well, not as vulgar wretch his mistress
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="3">Then, too, I loved thee well, not as vulgar wretch his mistress</l>

lines.text: But as a father his sons loves and his sons by the law.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="4">But as a father his sons loves and his sons by the law.</l>

lines.text: Now have I learnt thee aright; wherefor though burn I the hotter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="5">Now have I learnt thee aright; wherefor though burn I the hotter,</l>

lines.text: Lighter and viler by far thou unto me hast become.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="6">Lighter and viler by far thou unto me hast become. </l>

lines.text: How can this be? dost ask: ’tis that such injury ever
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="7"><q rend="double">How can this be?</q> dost ask: ’tis that such injury ever</l>

lines.text: Forces the hotter to love, also the less well to will.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:72" n="8">Forces the hotter to love, also the less well to will.</l>

lines.text: Cease thou of any to hope desirèd boon of well-willing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:73" n="1">Cease thou of any to hope desirèd boon of well-willing,</l>

lines.text: Or deem any shall prove pious and true to his dues.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:73" n="2">Or deem any shall prove pious and true to his dues.</l>

lines.text: Waxes the world ingrate, no deed benevolent profits,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:73" n="3">Waxes the world ingrate, no deed benevolent profits, </l>

lines.text: Nay full oft it irks even offending the more:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:73" n="4">Nay full oft it irks even offending the more:</l>

lines.text: Such is my case whom none maltreats more grievously bitter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:73" n="5">Such is my case whom none maltreats more grievously bitter,</l>

lines.text: Than does the man that me held one and only to friend.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:73" n="6">Than does the man that me held one and only to friend.</l>

lines.text: Wont was Gellius hear his uncle rich in reproaches,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:74" n="1">Wont was Gellius hear his uncle rich in reproaches, </l>

lines.text: When any ventured aught wanton in word or in deed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:74" n="2">When any ventured aught wanton in word or in deed.</l>

lines.text: Lest to him chance such befall, his uncle’s consort seduced he,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:74" n="3">Lest to him chance such befall, his uncle’s consort seduced he,</l>

lines.text: And of his uncle himself fashioned an Harpocrates.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:74" n="4">And of his uncle himself fashioned an Harpocrates.</l>

lines.text: What so he willed did he; and nowdays albe his uncle
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:74" n="5">What so he willed did he; and nowdays albe his uncle</l>

lines.text: . . . . he, no word ever that uncle shall speak.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:74" n="6"><gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . "/> he, no word ever that uncle shall speak.</l>

lines.text: Now is my mind to a pass, my Lesbia, brought by thy treason,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:75" n="1">Now is my mind to a pass, my Lesbia, brought by thy treason,</l>

lines.text: So in devotion to thee lost is the duty self due,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:75" n="2">So in devotion to thee lost is the duty self due,</l>

lines.text: Nor can I will thee well if best of women thou prove thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:75" n="3">Nor can I will thee well if best of women thou prove thee,</l>

lines.text: Nor can I cease to love, do thou what doings thou wilt.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:75" n="4">Nor can I cease to love, do thou what doings thou wilt.</l>

lines.text: If to remember deeds whilòme well done be a pleasure
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="1">If to remember deeds whilòme well done be a pleasure </l>

lines.text: Meet for a man who deems all of his dealings be just,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="2">Meet for a man who deems all of his dealings be just,</l>

lines.text: Nor Holy Faith ever broke nor in whatever his compact
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="3">Nor Holy Faith ever broke nor in whatever his compact</l>

lines.text: Sanction of Gods abused better to swindle mankind,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="4">Sanction of Gods abused better to swindle mankind,</l>

lines.text: Much there remains for thee during length of living, Catullus,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="5">Much there remains for thee during length of living, Catullus,</l>

lines.text: Out of that Love ingrate further to solace thy soul;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="6">Out of that Love ingrate further to solace thy soul; </l>

lines.text: For whatever of good can mortal declare of another
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="7">For whatever of good can mortal declare of another</l>

lines.text: Or can avail he do, such thou hast said and hast done;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="8">Or can avail he do, such thou hast said and hast done;</l>

lines.text: While to a thankless mind entrusted all of them perisht.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="9">While to a thankless mind entrusted all of them perisht.</l>

lines.text: Why, then, crucify self now with a furthering pain?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="10">Why, then, crucify self now with a furthering pain?</l>

lines.text: Why not steady thy thoughts and draw thee back from such purpose,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="11">Why not steady thy thoughts and draw thee back from such purpose,</l>

lines.text: Ceasing wretched to be maugrè the will of the Gods?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="12">Ceasing wretched to be maugrè the will of the Gods?</l>

lines.text: Difficult ’tis indeed long Love to depose of a sudden,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="13">Difficult ’tis indeed long Love to depose of a sudden,</l>

lines.text: Difficult ’tis, yet do e’en as thou deem to be best.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="14">Difficult ’tis, yet do e’en as thou deem to be best.</l>

lines.text: This be thy safe-guard sole; this conquest needs to be conquered;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="15">This be thy safe-guard sole; this conquest needs to be conquered;</l>

lines.text: This thou must do, thus act, whether thou cannot or can.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="16">This thou must do, thus act, whether thou cannot or can.</l>

lines.text: If an ye have (O Gods!) aught ruth, or if you for any
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="17">If an ye have (O Gods!) aught ruth, or if you for any </l>

lines.text: Bring at the moment of death latest assistance to man,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="18">Bring at the moment of death latest assistance to man,</l>

lines.text: Look upon me (poor me!) and, should I be cleanly of living,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="19">Look upon me (poor me!) and, should I be cleanly of living,</l>

lines.text: Out of my life deign pluck this my so pestilent plague,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="20">Out of my life deign pluck this my so pestilent plague,</l>

lines.text: Which as a lethargy o’er mine inmost vitals a-creeping,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="21">Which as a lethargy o’er mine inmost vitals a-creeping,</l>

lines.text: Hath from my bosom expelled all of what joyance it joyed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="22">Hath from my bosom expelled all of what joyance it joyed,</l>

lines.text: Now will I crave no more she love me e’en as I love her,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="23">Now will I crave no more she love me e’en as I love her,</l>

lines.text: Nor (impossible chance!) ever she prove herself chaste:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="24">Nor (impossible chance!) ever she prove herself chaste:</l>

lines.text: Would I were only healed and shed this fulsome disorder.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="25">Would I were only healed and shed this fulsome disorder.</l>

lines.text: Oh Gods, grant me this boon unto my piety due!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:76" n="26">Oh Gods, grant me this boon unto my piety due!</l>

head: TO RUFUS, THE TRAITOR FRIEND.

lines.text: Rufus, trusted as friend by me, so fruitlessly, vainly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:77" n="1">Rufus, trusted as friend by me, so fruitlessly, vainly, </l>

lines.text: (Vainly? nay to my bane and at a ruinous price!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:77" n="2">(Vainly? nay to my bane and at a ruinous price!)</l>

lines.text: Hast thou cajoled me thus, and enfiring innermost vitals,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:77" n="3">Hast thou cajoled me thus, and enfiring innermost vitals,</l>

lines.text: Ravished the whole of our good own’d by wretchedest me?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:77" n="4">Ravished the whole of our good own’d by wretchedest me?</l>

lines.text: Ravished; (alas and alas!) of our life thou cruellest cruel
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:77" n="5">Ravished; (alas and alas!) of our life thou cruellest cruel</l>

lines.text: Venom, (alas and alas!) plague of our friendship and pest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:77" n="6">Venom, (alas and alas!) plague of our friendship and pest.</l>

notes: Lines 7-10 of poem 77 in this edition are presented below as part of poem 78 in keeping with convention.

lines.text: Gallus hath brothers in pair, this owning most beautiful consort,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="1">Gallus hath brothers in pair, this owning most beautiful consort,</l>

lines.text: While unto that is given also a beautiful son.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="2">While unto that is given also a beautiful son.</l>

lines.text: Gallus is charming as man; for sweet loves ever conjoins he,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="3">Gallus is charming as man; for sweet loves ever conjoins he,</l>

lines.text: So that the charming lad sleep wi’ the charmer his lass.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="4">So that the charming lad sleep wi’ the charmer his lass.</l>

lines.text: Gallus is foolish wight, nor self regards he as husband,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="5">Gallus is foolish wight, nor self regards he as husband,</l>

lines.text: When being uncle how nuncle to cuckold he show.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="6">When being uncle how nuncle to cuckold he show.</l>

lines.text: Yet must I now lament that lips so pure of the purest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="7">Yet must I now lament that lips so pure of the purest </l>

lines.text: Damsel, thy slaver foul soiled with filthiest kiss.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="8">Damsel, thy slaver foul soiled with filthiest kiss.</l>

lines.text: But ne’er hope to escape scot free; for thee shall all ages
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="9">But ne’er hope to escape scot free; for thee shall all ages</l>

lines.text: Know, and what thing thou be, Fame, the old crone, shall declare.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:78" n="10">Know, and what thing thou be, Fame, the old crone, shall declare.</l>

lines.text: Lesbius is beauty-man: why not? when Lesbia wills him
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:79" n="1">Lesbius is beauty-man: why not? when Lesbia wills him</l>

lines.text: Better, Catullus, than thee backed by the whole of thy clan.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:79" n="2">Better, Catullus, than thee backed by the whole of thy clan.</l>

lines.text: Yet may that beauty-man sell all his clan with Catullus,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:79" n="3">Yet may that beauty-man sell all his clan with Catullus,</l>

lines.text: An of three noted names greeting salute he can gain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:79" n="4">An of three noted names greeting salute he can gain.</l>

lines.text: How shall I (Gellius!) tell what way lips rosy as thine are
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="1">How shall I (Gellius!) tell what way lips rosy as thine are</l>

lines.text: Come to be bleached and blanched whiter than wintry snow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="2">Come to be bleached and blanched whiter than wintry snow,</l>

lines.text: When as thou quittest the house a-morn, and at two after noon-tide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="3">When as thou quittest the house a-morn, and at two after noon-tide</l>

lines.text: Roused from quiet repose, wakest for length of the day?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="4">Roused from quiet repose, wakest for length of the day?</l>

lines.text: Certès sure am I not an Rumour rightfully whisper
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="5">Certès sure am I not an Rumour rightfully whisper</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="6"><gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . . . ."/></l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="7"><gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . . . ."/></l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:80" n="8"><gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . . . ."/></l>

lines.text: Could there never be found in folk so thronging (Juventius!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:81" n="1">Could there never be found in folk so thronging (Juventius!)</l>

lines.text: Any one charming thee whom thou couldst fancy to love,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:81" n="2">Any one charming thee whom thou couldst fancy to love,</l>

lines.text: Save and except that host from deadliest site of Pisaurum,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:81" n="3">Save and except that host from deadliest site of Pisaurum,</l>

lines.text: Wight than a statue gilt wanner and yellower-hued,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:81" n="4">Wight than a statue gilt wanner and yellower-hued,</l>

lines.text: Whom to thy heart thou takest and whom thou darest before us
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:81" n="5">Whom to thy heart thou takest and whom thou darest before us</l>

lines.text: Choose? But villain what deed doest thou little canst wot!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:81" n="6">Choose? But villain what deed doest thou little canst wot!</l>

lines.text: Quintius! an thou wish that Catullus should owe thee his eyes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:82" n="1">Quintius! an thou wish that Catullus should owe thee his eyes</l>

lines.text: Or aught further if aught dearer can be than his eyes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:82" n="2">Or aught further if aught dearer can be than his eyes,</l>

lines.text: Thou wilt not ravish from him what deems he dearer and nearer
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:82" n="3">Thou wilt not ravish from him what deems he dearer and nearer</l>

lines.text: E’en than his eyes if aught dearer there be than his eyes.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:82" n="4">E’en than his eyes if aught dearer there be than his eyes.</l>

lines.text: Lesbia heaps upon me foul words her mate being present;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:83" n="1">Lesbia heaps upon me foul words her mate being present;</l>

lines.text: Which to that simple soul causes the fullest delight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:83" n="2">Which to that simple soul causes the fullest delight. </l>

lines.text: Mule! naught sensest thou: did she forget us in silence,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:83" n="3">Mule! naught sensest thou: did she forget us in silence,</l>

lines.text: Whole she had been; but now what so she rails and she snarls,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:83" n="4">Whole she had been; but now what so she rails and she snarls,</l>

lines.text: Not only dwells in her thought, but worse and even more risky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:83" n="5">Not only dwells in her thought, but worse and even more risky,</l>

lines.text: Wrathful she bides. Which means, she is afire and she fumes.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:83" n="6">Wrathful she bides. Which means, she is afire and she fumes.</l>

lines.text: Wontis Arrius say Chommodious whenas commodious
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="1">Wontis Arrius say <q rend="double">Chommodious</q> whenas <q rend="double">commodious</q></l>

lines.text: Means he, and Insidious aspirate Hinsidious,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="2">Means he, and <q rend="double">Insidious</q> aspirate <q rend="double">Hinsidious,</q> </l>

lines.text: What time flattering self he speaks with marvellous purity,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="3">What time flattering self he speaks with marvellous purity,</l>

lines.text: Clamouring Hinsidious loudly as ever he can.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="4">Clamouring <q rend="double">Hinsidious</q> loudly as ever he can. </l>

lines.text: Deem I thus did his dame and thus-wise Liber his uncle
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="5">Deem I thus did his dame and thus-wise Liber his uncle</l>

lines.text: Speak, and on spindle-side grandsire and grandmother too.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="6">Speak, and on spindle-side grandsire and grandmother too.</l>

lines.text: Restful reposed all ears when he was sent into Syria,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="7">Restful reposed all ears when he was sent into Syria, </l>

lines.text: Hearing the self-same words softly and smoothly pronouncèd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="8">Hearing the self-same words softly and smoothly pronouncèd,</l>

lines.text: Nor any feared to hear such harshness uttered thereafter,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="9">Nor any feared to hear such harshness uttered thereafter,</l>

lines.text: Whenas a sudden came message of horrible news,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="10">Whenas a sudden came message of horrible news,</l>

lines.text: Namely th’ lonian waves when Arrius thither had wended,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="11">Namely th’ lonian waves when Arrius thither had wended,</l>

lines.text: Were lonian no more—they had Hionian become.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:84" n="12">Were <q rend="double">lonian</q> no more—they had <q rend="double">Hionian</q> become.</l>

lines.text: Hate I, and love I. Haps thou’lt ask me wherefore I do so.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:85" n="1">Hate I, and love I. Haps thou’lt ask me wherefore I do so.</l>

lines.text: Wot I not, yet so I do feeling a torture of pain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:85" n="2">Wot I not, yet so I do feeling a torture of pain.</l>

lines.text: Quintia beautiful seems to the crowd; to me, fair, and tall,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:86" n="1">Quintia beautiful seems to the crowd; to me, fair, and tall,</l>

lines.text: Straight; and merits as these readily thus I confess,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:86" n="2">Straight; and merits as these readily thus I confess,</l>

lines.text: But that she is beauteous all I deny, for nothing of lovesome,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:86" n="3">But that she is beauteous all I deny, for nothing of lovesome,</l>

lines.text: Never a grain of salt, shows in her person so large.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:86" n="4">Never a grain of salt, shows in her person so large. </l>

lines.text: Lesbia beautiful seems, and when all over she’s fairest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:86" n="5">Lesbia beautiful seems, and when all over she’s fairest,</l>

lines.text: Any Venus-gift stole she from every one.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:86" n="6">Any Venus-gift stole she from every one.</l>

head: TO LESBIA.

lines.text: Never a woman could call herself so fondly beloved
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:87" n="1">Never a woman could call herself so fondly beloved</l>

lines.text: Truly as Lesbia mine has been beloved of myself.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:87" n="2">Truly as Lesbia mine has been beloved of myself.</l>

lines.text: Never were Truth and Faith so firm in any one compact
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:87" n="3">Never were Truth and Faith so firm in any one compact</l>

lines.text: As on the part of me kept I my love to thyself.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:87" n="4">As on the part of me kept I my love to thyself.</l>

notes: See poem 75 for the remainder of the lines presented here in the print edition.

lines.text: What may he (Gellius!) do that ever for mother and sister
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="1">What may he (Gellius!) do that ever for mother and sister</l>

lines.text: Itches and wakes thro’ the nights, working wi’ tunic bedoffed?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="2">Itches and wakes thro’ the nights, working wi’ tunic bedoffed?</l>

lines.text: What may he do who nills his uncle ever be husband?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="3">What may he do who nills his uncle ever be husband?</l>

lines.text: Wottest thou how much he ventures of sacrilege-sin?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="4">Wottest thou how much he ventures of sacrilege-sin?</l>

lines.text: Ventures he (O Gellius!) what ne’er can ultimate Tethys
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="5">Ventures he (O Gellius!) what ne’er can ultimate Tethys</l>

lines.text: Wash from his soul, nor yet Ocean, watery sire.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="6">Wash from his soul, nor yet Ocean, watery sire.</l>

lines.text: For that of sin there’s naught wherewith this sin can exceed he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="7">For that of sin there’s naught wherewith this sin can exceed he</l>

lines.text: . . . . . . his head on himself.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:88" n="8"><gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . . ."/> his head on himself.</l>

lines.text: Gellius is lean: Why not?For him so easy a mother
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:89" n="1">Gellius is lean: Why not?For him so easy a mother</l>

lines.text: Lives, and a sister so boon, bonny and buxom to boot,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:89" n="2">Lives, and a sister so boon, bonny and buxom to boot,</l>

lines.text: Uncle so kindly good and all things full of his lady-
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:89" n="3">Uncle so kindly good and all things full of his lady-</l>

lines.text: Cousins, how can he cease leanest of lankies to be?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:89" n="4">Cousins, how can he cease leanest of lankies to be?</l>

lines.text: Albeit, touch he naught save that whose touch is a scandal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:89" n="5">Albeit, touch he naught save that whose touch is a scandal,</l>

lines.text: Soon shall thou find wherefor he be as lean as thou like.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:89" n="6">Soon shall thou find wherefor he be as lean as thou like.</l>

lines.text: Born be a Magus, got by Gellius out of his mother
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:90" n="1">Born be a Magus, got by Gellius out of his mother</l>

lines.text: (Marriagenefand!) who shall Persian augury learn.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:90" n="2">(Marriagenefand!) who shall Persian augury learn.</l>

lines.text: Needs it a Magus begot of son upon mother who bare him,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:90" n="3">Needs it a Magus begot of son upon mother who bare him,</l>

lines.text: If that impious faith, Persian religion be fact,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:90" n="4">If that impious faith, Persian religion be fact,</l>

lines.text: So may their issue adore busy gods with recognised verses
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:90" n="5">So may their issue adore busy gods with recognised verses</l>

lines.text: Melting in altar-flame fatness contained by the caul.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:90" n="6">Melting in altar-flame fatness contained by the caul.</l>

lines.text: Not for due cause I hoped to find thee (Gellius!) faithful
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="1">Not for due cause I hoped to find thee (Gellius!) faithful</l>

lines.text: In this saddest our love, love that is lost and forlore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="2">In this saddest our love, love that is lost and forlore,</l>

lines.text: Or fro’ my wotting thee well or ever believing thee constant,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="3">Or fro’ my wotting thee well or ever believing thee constant,</l>

lines.text: Or that thy mind could reject villany ever so vile,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="4">Or that thy mind could reject villany ever so vile,</l>

lines.text: But that because was she to thyself nor mother nor sister,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="5">But that because was she to thyself nor mother nor sister,</l>

lines.text: This same damsel whose Love me in its greatness devoured.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="6">This same damsel whose Love me in its greatness devoured.</l>

lines.text: Yet though I had been joined wi’ thee by amplest of usance,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="7">Yet though I had been joined wi’ thee by amplest of usance,</l>

lines.text: Still could I never believe this was sufficient of cause.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="8">Still could I never believe this was sufficient of cause.</l>

lines.text: Thou diddest deem it suffice: so great is thy pleasure in every
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="9">Thou diddest deem it suffice: so great is thy pleasure in every</l>

lines.text: Crime wherein may be found somewhat enormous of guilt.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:91" n="10">Crime wherein may be found somewhat enormous of guilt.</l>

lines.text: Lesbia naggeth at me evermore and ne’er is she silent
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:92" n="1">Lesbia naggeth at me evermore and ne’er is she silent</l>

lines.text: Touching myself: May I die but that by Lesbia I’m loved.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:92" n="2">Touching myself: May I die but that by Lesbia I’m loved.</l>

lines.text: What be the proof?I rail and retort like her and revile her
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:92" n="3">What be the proof?I rail and retort like her and revile her</l>

lines.text: Carefully, yet may I die but that I love her with love.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:92" n="4">Carefully, yet may I die but that I love her with love.</l>

lines.text: Study I not o’ermuch to please thee (Caesar!) and court thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:93" n="1">Study I not o’ermuch to please thee (Caesar!) and court thee,</l>

lines.text: Nor do I care e’en to know an thou be white or be black.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:93" n="2">Nor do I care e’en to know an thou be white or be black.</l>

lines.text: Mentula wooeth much: much wooeth he, be assurèd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:94" n="1">Mentula wooeth much: much wooeth he, be assurèd.</l>

lines.text: That is, e’en as they say, the Pot gathers leeks for the pot.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:94" n="2">That is, e’en as they say, the Pot gathers leeks for the pot.</l>

head: ON THE ZMYRNA OF THE POET CINNA.

lines.text: Zmyrna begun erstwhile nine harvests past by my Cinna
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="1"><q rend="double">Zmyrna</q> begun erstwhile nine harvests past by my Cinna</l>

lines.text: Publisht appears when now nine of his winters be gone;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="2">Publisht appears when now nine of his winters be gone;</l>

lines.text: Thousands fifty of lines meanwhile Hortensius in single
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="3">Thousands fifty of lines meanwhile Hortensius in single</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="4"><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * * * * * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Zmyrna shall travel afar as the hollow breakers of Satrax,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="5"><q rend="double">Zmyrna</q> shall travel afar as the hollow breakers of Satrax,</l>

lines.text: Zmyrna by ages grey lastingly shall be perused.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="6"><q rend="double">Zmyrna</q> by ages grey lastingly shall be perused.</l>

lines.text: But upon Padus’ brink shall die Volusius his annals
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="7">But upon Padus’ brink shall die Volusius his annals</l>

lines.text: And to the mackerel oft loose-fitting jacket afford.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="8">And to the mackerel oft loose-fitting jacket afford.</l>

lines.text: Dear to my heart are aye the lightest works of my comrade,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="9">Dear to my heart are aye the lightest works of my comrade,</l>

lines.text: Leave I the mob to enjoy tumidest Antimachus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:95" n="10">Leave I the mob to enjoy tumidest Antimachus.</l>

lines.text: If to the dumb deaf tomb can aught or grateful or pleasing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:96" n="1">If to the dumb deaf tomb can aught or grateful or pleasing</l>

lines.text: (Calvus!) ever accrue rising from out of our dule,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:96" n="2">(Calvus!) ever accrue rising from out of our dule,</l>

lines.text: Wherewith yearning desire renews our loves in the bygone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:96" n="3">Wherewith yearning desire renews our loves in the bygone,</l>

lines.text: And for long friendships lost many a tear must be shed;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:96" n="4">And for long friendships lost many a tear must be shed;</l>

lines.text: Certès, never so much for doom of premature death-day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:96" n="5">Certès, never so much for doom of premature death-day</l>

lines.text: Must thy Quintilia mourn as she is joyed by thy love.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:96" n="6">Must thy Quintilia mourn as she is joyed by thy love.</l>

lines.text: Never (so love me the Gods!) deemed I ’twas preference matter
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="1">Never (so love me the Gods!) deemed I ’twas preference matter</l>

lines.text: Or Aemilius’ mouth choose I to smell or his . . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="2">Or Aemilius’ mouth choose I to smell or his <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . "/></l>

lines.text: Nothing is this more clean, uncleaner nothing that other,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="3">Nothing is this more clean, uncleaner nothing that other,</l>

lines.text: Yet I ajudge . . . . . cleaner and nicer to be;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="4">Yet I ajudge <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . . "/> cleaner and nicer to be;</l>

lines.text: For while this one lacks teeth, that one has cubit-long tushes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="5">For while this one lacks teeth, that one has cubit-long tushes,</l>

lines.text: Set in their battered gums favouring a muddy old box,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="6">Set in their battered gums favouring a muddy old box,</l>

lines.text: Not to say aught of gape like wide-cleft gap of a she-mule
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="7">Not to say aught of gape like wide-cleft gap of a she-mule</l>

lines.text: Whenas in summer-heat wont peradventure to stale.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="8">Whenas in summer-heat wont peradventure to stale.</l>

lines.text: Yet has he many a motte and holds himself to be handsome—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="9">Yet has he many a motte and holds himself to be handsome—</l>

lines.text: Why wi’ the baker’s ass is he not bound to the mill?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="10">Why wi’ the baker’s ass is he not bound to the mill?</l>

lines.text: Him if a damsel kiss we fain must think she be ready
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="11">Him if a damsel kiss we fain must think she be ready</l>

lines.text: With her fair lips . . . . . . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:97" n="12">With her fair lips <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=". . . . . . . ."/></l>

lines.text: Rightly of thee may be said, an of any, (thou stinkingest Victius!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:98" n="1">Rightly of thee may be said, an of any, (thou stinkingest Victius!)</l>

lines.text: Whatso wont we to say touching the praters and prigs.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:98" n="2">Whatso wont we to say touching the praters and prigs.</l>

lines.text: Thou wi’ that tongue o’ thine own, if granted occasion availest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:98" n="3">Thou wi’ that tongue o’ thine own, if granted occasion availest</l>

lines.text: Brogues of the cowherds to kiss, also their . . . .
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:98" n="4">Brogues of the cowherds to kiss, also their <gap reason="ellipsis" rend=" . . . . "/></l>

lines.text: Wouldst thou undo us all with a thorough undoing (O Victius!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:98" n="5">Wouldst thou undo us all with a thorough undoing (O Victius!)</l>

lines.text: Open thy gape:—thereby all shall be wholly undone.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:98" n="6">Open thy gape:—thereby all shall be wholly undone.</l>

lines.text: E’en as thou played’st, from thee snatched I (O honied Juventius!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="1">E’en as thou played’st, from thee snatched I (O honied Juventius!)</l>

lines.text: Kissletof savour so sweet sweetest Ambrosia unknows.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="2">Kissletof savour so sweet sweetest Ambrosia unknows.</l>

lines.text: Yet was the theft nowise scot-free, for more than an hour I
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="3">Yet was the theft nowise scot-free, for more than an hour I</l>

lines.text: Clearly remember me fixt hanging from crest of the Cross,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="4">Clearly remember me fixt hanging from crest of the Cross,</l>

lines.text: Whatwhile I purged my sin unto thee nor with any weeping
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="5">Whatwhile I purged my sin unto thee nor with any weeping</l>

lines.text: Tittle of cruel despite such as be thine could I ’bate.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="6">Tittle of cruel despite such as be thine could I ’bate.</l>

lines.text: For that no sooner done thou washed thy liplets with many
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="7">For that no sooner done thou washed thy liplets with many</l>

lines.text: Drops which thy fingers did wipe, using their every joint,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="8">Drops which thy fingers did wipe, using their every joint,</l>

lines.text: Lest of our mouths conjoined remain there aught by the contact
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="9">Lest of our mouths conjoined remain there aught by the contact</l>

lines.text: Like unto slaver foul shed by the butterèd bun.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="10">Like unto slaver foul shed by the butterèd bun. </l>

lines.text: Further, wretchedmost me betrayed to unfriendliest Love-god
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="11">Further, wretchedmost me betrayed to unfriendliest Love-god</l>

lines.text: Never thou ceased’st to pain hurting with every harm,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="12">Never thou ceased’st to pain hurting with every harm,</l>

lines.text: So that my taste be turned and kisses ambrosial erstwhile
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="13">So that my taste be turned and kisses ambrosial erstwhile</l>

lines.text: Even than hellebore-juice bitterest bitterer grow.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="14">Even than hellebore-juice bitterest bitterer grow.</l>

lines.text: Seeing such pangs as these prepared for unfortunate lover,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="15">Seeing such pangs as these prepared for unfortunate lover,</l>

lines.text: After this never again kiss will I venture to snatch.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:99" n="16">After this never again kiss will I venture to snatch.</l>

lines.text: Caelius Aufilénus and Quintius Aufiléna,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="1">Caelius Aufilénus and Quintius Aufiléna,</l>

lines.text: Love to the death, both swains bloom of the youth Veronese,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="2">Love to the death, both swains bloom of the youth Veronese,</l>

lines.text: This woo’d brother and that sue’d sister: so might the matter
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="3">This woo’d brother and that sue’d sister: so might the matter</l>

lines.text: Claim to be titled wi’ sooth fairest fraternalest tie.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="4">Claim to be titled wi’ sooth fairest fraternalest tie.</l>

lines.text: Whom shall I favour the first?Thee (Caelius!) for thou hast provèd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="5">Whom shall I favour the first?Thee (Caelius!) for thou hast provèd</l>

lines.text: Singular friendship to us shown by the deeds it has done,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="6">Singular friendship to us shown by the deeds it has done,</l>

lines.text: Whenas the flames insane had madded me, firing my marrow:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="7">Whenas the flames insane had madded me, firing my marrow:</l>

lines.text: Caelius! happy be thou; ever be lusty in love.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:100" n="8">Caelius! happy be thou; ever be lusty in love.</l>

head: ON THE BURIAL OF HIS BROTHER.

lines.text: Faring thro’ many a folk and plowing many a sea-plain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="1">Faring thro’ many a folk and plowing many a sea-plain</l>

lines.text: These sad funeral-rites (Brother!) to deal thee I come,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="2">These sad funeral-rites (Brother!) to deal thee I come,</l>

lines.text: So wi’ the latest boons to the dead bestowed I may gift thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="3">So wi’ the latest boons to the dead bestowed I may gift thee,</l>

lines.text: And I may vainly address ashes that answer have none,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="4">And I may vainly address ashes that answer have none,</l>

lines.text: Sithence of thee, very thee, to deprive me Fortune behested,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="5">Sithence of thee, very thee, to deprive me Fortune behested,</l>

lines.text: Woe for thee, Brother forlore!Cruelly severed fro’ me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="6">Woe for thee, Brother forlore!Cruelly severed fro’ me.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="6a"><gap reason="lost" rend=" * * * "/></l>

lines.text: Yet in the meanwhile now what olden usage of forbears
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="7">Yet in the meanwhile now what olden usage of forbears</l>

lines.text: Brings as the boons that befit mournfullest funeral rites,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="8">Brings as the boons that befit mournfullest funeral rites,</l>

lines.text: Thinebe these gifts which flow with tear-flood shed by thy brother,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="9">Thinebe these gifts which flow with tear-flood shed by thy brother,</l>

lines.text: And,for ever and aye (Brother!) all hail and farewell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:101" n="10">And,for ever and aye (Brother!) all hail and farewell. </l>

lines.text: If by confiding friend aught e’er be trusted in silence,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:102" n="1">If by confiding friend aught e’er be trusted in silence,</l>

lines.text: Unto a man whose mind known is for worthiest trust,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:102" n="2">Unto a man whose mind known is for worthiest trust,</l>

lines.text: Me shalt thou find no less than such to secrecy oath-bound,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:102" n="3">Me shalt thou find no less than such to secrecy oath-bound,</l>

lines.text: (Cornelius!) and now hold me an Harpocrates.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:102" n="4">(Cornelius!) and now hold me an Harpocrates.</l>

lines.text: Or, d’ye hear, refund those ten sestertia (Silo!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:103" n="1">Or, d’ye hear, refund those ten sestertia (Silo!)</l>

lines.text: Then be thou e’en at thy will surly and savage o’ mood:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:103" n="2">Then be thou e’en at thy will surly and savage o’ mood:</l>

lines.text: Or, an thou love o’er-well those moneys, prithee no longer
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:103" n="3">Or, an thou love o’er-well those moneys, prithee no longer</l>

lines.text: Prove thee a pimp and withal surly and savage o’ mood.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:103" n="4">Prove thee a pimp and withal surly and savage o’ mood.</l>

lines.text: Canst thou credit that I could avail to revile my life-love,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:104" n="1">Canst thou credit that I could avail to revile my life-love,</l>

lines.text: She who be dearer to me even than either my eyes?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:104" n="2">She who be dearer to me even than either my eyes?</l>

lines.text: Ne’er could I, nor an I could, should I so losingly love her:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:104" n="3">Ne’er could I, nor an I could, should I so losingly love her:</l>

lines.text: But with Tappo thou dost design every monstrous deed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:104" n="4">But with Tappo thou dost design every monstrous deed.</l>

lines.text: Mentula fain would ascend Pipléan mountain up-mounting:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:105" n="1">Mentula fain would ascend Pipléan mountain up-mounting:</l>

lines.text: Pitch him the Muses down headlong wi’ forklets a-hurled.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:105" n="2">Pitch him the Muses down headlong wi’ forklets a-hurled.</l>

head: THE AUCTIONEER AND THE FAIR BOY.

lines.text: When with a pretty-faced boy we see one playing the Crier,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:106" n="1">When with a pretty-faced boy we see one playing the Crier,</l>

lines.text: What can we wot except longs he for selling the same?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:106" n="2">What can we wot except longs he for selling the same?</l>

lines.text: An to one ever accrue any boon he lusted and longed for
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="1">An to one ever accrue any boon he lusted and longed for</l>

lines.text: Any time after despair, grateful it comes to his soul.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="2">Any time after despair, grateful it comes to his soul.</l>

lines.text: Thus ’tis grateful to us nor gold was ever so goodly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="3">Thus ’tis grateful to us nor gold was ever so goodly,</l>

lines.text: When thou restorest thyself (Lesbia!) to loving-most me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="4">When thou restorest thyself (Lesbia!) to loving-most me,</l>

lines.text: Self thou restorest unhoped, and after despair thou returnest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="5">Self thou restorest unhoped, and after despair thou returnest.</l>

lines.text: Oh the fair light of a Day noted with notabler white!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="6">Oh the fair light of a Day noted with notabler white!</l>

lines.text: Where lives a happier man than myself or—this being won me—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="7">Where lives a happier man than myself or—this being won me—</l>

lines.text: Who shall e’er boast that his life brought him more coveted lot?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:107" n="8">Who shall e’er boast that his life brought him more coveted lot?</l>

lines.text: If by the verdict o’ folk thy hoary old age(O Cominius!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:108" n="1">If by the verdict o’ folk thy hoary old age(O Cominius!)</l>

lines.text: Filthy with fulsomest lust ever be doomed to the death,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:108" n="2">Filthy with fulsomest lust ever be doomed to the death,</l>

lines.text: Make I no manner of doubt but first thy tongue to the worthy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:108" n="3">Make I no manner of doubt but first thy tongue to the worthy</l>

lines.text: Ever a foe, cut out, ravening Vulture shall feed;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:108" n="4">Ever a foe, cut out, ravening Vulture shall feed;</l>

lines.text: Gulp shall the Crow’s black gorge those eye-balls dug from their sockets,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:108" n="5">Gulp shall the Crow’s black gorge those eye-balls dug from their sockets,</l>

lines.text: Guts of thee go to the dogs, all that remains to the wolves.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:108" n="6">Guts of thee go to the dogs, all that remains to the wolves.</l>

head: TO LESBIA ON HER VOW OF CONSTANCY.

lines.text: Gladsome to me, O my life, this love whose offer thou deignest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:109" n="1">Gladsome to me, O my life, this love whose offer thou deignest</l>

lines.text: Between us twain lively and lusty to last soothfast.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:109" n="2">Between us twain lively and lusty to last soothfast.</l>

lines.text: (Great Gods!) grant ye the boon that prove her promises loyal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:109" n="3">(Great Gods!) grant ye the boon that prove her promises loyal,</l>

lines.text: Saying her say in truth spoken with spirit sincere;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:109" n="4">Saying her say in truth spoken with spirit sincere;</l>

lines.text: So be it lawful for us to protract through length of our life-tide
