lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:109" n="5">So be it lawful for us to protract through length of our life-tide</l>

lines.text: Mutual pact of our love, pledges of holy good will!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:109" n="6">Mutual pact of our love, pledges of holy good will!</l>

lines.text: Aufiléna! for aye good lasses are lauded as loyal:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="1">Aufiléna! for aye good lasses are lauded as loyal:</l>

lines.text: Price of themselves they accept when they intend to perform.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="2">Price of themselves they accept when they intend to perform.</l>

lines.text: All thou promised’st me in belying proves thee unfriendly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="3">All thou promised’st me in belying proves thee unfriendly,</l>

lines.text: For never giving and oft taking is deed illy done.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="4">For never giving and oft taking is deed illy done.</l>

lines.text: Either as honest to grant, or modest as never to promise,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="5">Either as honest to grant, or modest as never to promise, </l>

lines.text: Aufiléna! were fair, but at the gifties to clutch
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="6">Aufiléna! were fair, but at the gifties to clutch</l>

lines.text: Fraudfully, viler seems than greed of greediest harlot
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="7">Fraudfully, viler seems than greed of greediest harlot</l>

lines.text: Who with her every limb maketh a whore of herself.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:110" n="8">Who with her every limb maketh a whore of herself.</l>

lines.text: Aufiléna! to live content with only one husband,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:111" n="1">Aufiléna! to live content with only one husband,</l>

lines.text: Praise is and truest of praise ever bestowed upon wife.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:111" n="2">Praise is and truest of praise ever bestowed upon wife.</l>

lines.text: Yet were it liefer to lie any wise with any for lover,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:111" n="3">Yet were it liefer to lie any wise with any for lover,</l>

lines.text: Than to be breeder of boys uncle as cousins begat.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:111" n="4">Than to be breeder of boys uncle as cousins begat.</l>

lines.text: Great th’art (Naso!) as man, nor like thee many in greatness
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:112" n="1">Great th’art (Naso!) as man, nor like thee many in greatness</l>

lines.text: Lower themselves (Naso!): great be thou, pathic to boot.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:112" n="2">Lower themselves (Naso!): great be thou, pathic to boot.</l>

lines.text: Pompey first being chosen Consul, twofold (O Cinna!)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:113" n="1">Pompey first being chosen Consul, twofold (O Cinna!)</l>

lines.text: Men for amours were famed:also when chosen again
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:113" n="2">Men for amours were famed:also when chosen again</l>

lines.text: Two they remained; but now is each one grown to a thousand
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:113" n="3">Two they remained; but now is each one grown to a thousand</l>

lines.text: Gallants:—fecundate aye springeth adultery’s seed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:113" n="4">Gallants:—fecundate aye springeth adultery’s seed.</l>

lines.text: For yon Firmian domain not falsely Mentula hight is
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:114" n="1">For yon Firmian domain not falsely Mentula hight is</l>

lines.text: Richard, owning for self so manyexcellent things—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:114" n="2">Richard, owning for self so manyexcellent things—</l>

lines.text: Fish, fur, feather, all kinds, with prairie, corn-land, and ferals.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:114" n="3">Fish, fur, feather, all kinds, with prairie, corn-land, and ferals.</l>

lines.text: All no good: for th’ outgoing, income immensely exceeds.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:114" n="4">All no good: for th’ outgoing, income immensely exceeds.</l>

lines.text: Therefore his grounds be rich own I, while he’s but a pauper.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:114" n="5">Therefore his grounds be rich own I, while he’s but a pauper.</l>

lines.text: Laud we thy land while thou lackest joyance thereof.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:114" n="6">Laud we thy land while thou lackest joyance thereof.</l>

lines.text: Mentula! masterest thou some thirty acres of grassland
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="1">Mentula! masterest thou some thirty acres of grassland</l>

lines.text: Full told, forty of field soil; others are sized as the sea.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="2">Full told, forty of field soil; others are sized as the sea.</l>

lines.text: Why may he not surpass in his riches any a Crœsus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="3">Why may he not surpass in his riches any a Crœsus</l>

lines.text: Who in his one domain owns such abundance of good,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="4">Who in his one domain owns such abundance of good,</l>

lines.text: Grasslands, arable fields, vast woods and forest and marish
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="5">Grasslands, arable fields, vast woods and forest and marish</l>

lines.text: Yonder to Boreal-bounds trenching on Ocean tide?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="6">Yonder to Boreal-bounds trenching on Ocean tide?</l>

lines.text: Great are indeed all these, but thou by far be the greatest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="7">Great are indeed all these, but thou by far be the greatest,</l>

lines.text: Never a man, but a great Mentula of menacing might.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:115" n="8">Never a man, but a great Mentula of menacing might.</l>

lines.text: Seeking often in mind with spirit eager of study
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="1">Seeking often in mind with spirit eager of study</l>

lines.text: How I could send thee songs chaunted of Battiadés,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="2">How I could send thee songs chaunted of Battiadés,</l>

lines.text: So thou be softened to us, nor any attempting thou venture
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="3">So thou be softened to us, nor any attempting thou venture</l>

lines.text: Shot of thy hostile shaft piercing me high as its head,—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="4">Shot of thy hostile shaft piercing me high as its head,—</l>

lines.text: Now do I ken this toil with vainest purpose was taken,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="5">Now do I ken this toil with vainest purpose was taken,</l>

lines.text: (Gellius!) nor herein aughthave our prayers availèd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="6">(Gellius!) nor herein aughthave our prayers availèd.</l>

lines.text: Therefore we’ll parry with cloak what shafts thou shootest against us;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="7">Therefore we’ll parry with cloak what shafts thou shootest against us;</l>

lines.text: And by our bolts transfixt, penalty due thou shalt pay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" xml:base="urn:cts:latinLit:phi0472.phi001.perseus-eng3:116" n="8">And by our bolts transfixt, penalty due thou shalt pay.</l>
